EDCS-60700083.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Caenii Iulianus and Caelianus, his sons, made this for their father Barbula, son of L. Caenius, a man of rare innocence, and for his well-deserving wife. [Agathemeris?], his wife.
EDCS-60700083.summary: A funerary dedication by sons for their father and mother, praising the father's character.

EDCS-60700084.translation: To the divine spirits. Marita placed [this monument] for Caius Paetronius Proclianus, with the happiest fate.
EDCS-60700084.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Paetronius Proclianus by his wife Marita, mentioning his fortunate death.

EDCS-60700137.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Nervae filius Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XII imperator VI consul V pater patriae viam novam Traianam a Volsiniis ad fines Clusinorum fecit XVII ddomini nnnostri Constantius et Maximianus Auggusti et Diocletianus et Maximianus nniores Auggusti et Severus et Maximinus nobbilissimi Caessares et milia XVII Bono generis humani creati Impperatores ddomini nnostri Constantini sic <et Licinius> perpetui semper Augusti XVII\n
EDCS-60700137.translation: The Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, son of the divine Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 12th time, imperator for the 6th time, consul for the 5th time, father of the country, made the new Trajanic road from Volsinii to the borders of Clusium. In the 17th year of our Lords Constantius and Maximianus Augusti and Diocletian and Maximianus the Younger Augusti and Severus and Maximinus, most noble Caesars, and in the 17th year of our Lords Constantinus and Licinius, perpetual always Augusti, for the benefit of mankind.
EDCS-60700137.summary: An inscription dedicating a new road constructed under various emperors, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, and commissioned by Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-60800046.translation: To Gaius Marcius, son of Lucius Marcius, Rusticus. [---] Marcia [---] [---]
EDCS-60800046.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication for Gaius Marcius Rusticus, with additional partially legible names.

EDCS-61300030.translation: For Tullia Marcilla, daughter of Publius, of the Quentinia gens, Rufina, for Rufia Procula, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-61300030.summary: An epitaph for Tullia Marcilla Rufina, identified by multiple names and familial/tribal affiliations, honored as a distinguished woman.

EDCS-61300046.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Aemilia Fortunata made this for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Antonius Ampiatus.
EDCS-61300046.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her husband, Lucius Antonius Ampiatus.

EDCS-61300047.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Nicephorus, slave of Lucius Aemilius Callimachus, his fellow colleague, who deserved well. They made this. He lived for about 35 years.
EDCS-61300047.summary: A funerary dedication for Nicephorus, a slave and colleague, by his associates, mentioning his age at death.

EDCS-61300051.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Marcus Efficius Fortunatus made this for himself and for his dearest wife Lucatia Tyche, who lived with me for 30 years, and also for my sons and their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants. In front 10 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-61300051.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Efficius Fortunatus, his wife, children, and freedmen, with land dimensions for a tomb complex.

EDCS-61300055.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Masculinius Titianus the younger made this for his most beloved parents.
EDCS-61300055.summary: A funerary dedication by a son, Masculinius Titianus the younger, for his parents.

EDCS-61300056.translation: To Masculinius Titianus. Aemilia Afrodite [made this] for her incomparable husband, who lived 44 years, 11 months, and 17 days.
EDCS-61300056.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, dedicated by a wife to her husband, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-61900004.translation: Gnaeus Laberius, son of Aulus, of the Pomptina tribe. To Aulus Haprnius, son of Aulus.
EDCS-61900004.summary: A funerary epitaph from Ostia, recording a dedication from Gnaeus Laberius to Aulus Haprnius, likely from the 1st century BCE to 1st century CE.

EDCS-63800143.summary: A fragmentary inscription from an unknown location, likely a funerary epitaph, identifying a servant of Clodius Lunensis, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-64000155.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Porcia Hyle made this for her dearest husband, Lucius Laberius Felix, freedman of Lucius, an oil merchant.
EDCS-64000155.summary: A funerary epitaph from Ostia, dedicated by a wife to her husband, an oil merchant, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400236.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Here lies Iulius Clemensianus, who lived 73 years. He made [this] with his wife, with whom he lived 43 years. He departed in peace on the 12th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-64400236.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, recording the lifespan and death date of Iulius Clemensianus and his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400251.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sextus Murrius Paezon [made this] for his most dutiful father, Sextus Murrius Pru[nic]us.
EDCS-64400251.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, recording a dedication from a son to his father, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400252.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Meclo Constitutus [made this] for his deserving son, Gaius Vessius Valens, the magistrate.
EDCS-64400252.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, recording a dedication from a father to his son, who held the office of magistrate, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400253.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, recording the lifespan of Lucius Hirrius Doryphorus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-64400254.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Larcia Verulla, who lived 13 years, 3 months, and 7 days. Her parents [made this] for their most dutiful daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-64400254.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, dedicated by parents to their young daughter, dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400255.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Pullius Servandus [made this] for his wife, Rutilia Felicula, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-64400255.summary: A funerary epitaph from an unknown location, dedicated by a husband to his wife, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-64400531.translation: To the departed spirits. Thrania Hermione made this for her well-deserving husband, Tiberius Claudius Amandus.
EDCS-64400531.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her husband, Tiberius Claudius Amandus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400532.translation: To the departed spirits. Thrania Hermione made this for her most dutiful, well-deserving son, Marcus Aponius Amandus.
EDCS-64400532.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother, Thrania Hermione, for her son, Marcus Aponius Amandus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400533.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Virasius Venusius made this for his most dutiful brother, Publius Virasius Hermogenes.
EDCS-64400533.summary: A funerary dedication by a brother, Publius Virasius Venusius, for his sibling, Publius Virasius Hermogenes, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400534.translation: To the departed spirits. Made for Primigenia, well-deserving.
EDCS-64400534.summary: A funerary dedication for Primigenia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500129.translation: Publius Eppius Eureticus made this, while alive, for himself.
EDCS-64500129.summary: A funerary or sepulchral dedication by Publius Eppius Eureticus for himself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500132.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianvs, the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, chief pontiff, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-64500132.summary: An honorific inscription for Emperor Maximian, recording his titles and honors, likely from the Tetrarchic period (late 3rd to early 4th century CE).

EDCS-64500134.translation: To the departed spirits. [---]misi, [---] Nonas, for himself and [---]ori his [---]
EDCS-64500134.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication, possibly for the deceased and a surviving individual, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500365.translation: Caelia Rufina made this for her foster-daughter, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-64500365.summary: A funerary dedication by Caelia Rufina for her foster-daughter, aged 16, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500379.translation: Lucius Tettius Fortunatus made this, while alive, for me(?) and for Tettia Felici, his contubernalis.
EDCS-64500379.summary: A funerary or sepulchral dedication by Lucius Tettius Fortunatus for himself and his female companion (contubernalis), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500384.translation: Sacred to Augustus's spring. Aulus Vibius Aper gave this offering.
EDCS-64500384.summary: A dedication to a sacred spring named 'Augustus's spring' by Aulus Vibius Aper, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64500501.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Caius Sulpicius Serenus, his well-deserving wife Sulpicia Hilaritas made this.
EDCS-64500501.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-64900862.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. His wife made this for Ulpius Candido. To Candidus the African.
EDCS-64900862.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-64901012.translation: freedman of Ianius... freedman of Marcus... Chrestus... freedman of Marcus... freedwoman... five years.
EDCS-64901012.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription possibly recording the names of freedmen and their ages, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-65400061.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or ownership mark, mentioning two individuals, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-65800122.translation: When Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus was consul with Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-65800122.summary: A dating formula mentioning the consuls Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, Paetinus, and Apronianus, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-66200012.translation: Lucius Aveius Attianus, son of Lucius, made this for his mother Sulpicia Polla, daughter of Sextus, and for his wife Valeria, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-66200012.summary: A funerary monument erected by a son for his mother and wife, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-67000014.translation: Marcus Antonius Neanthus, Augustalis, made this of his own accord and at his own expense, by decree of the decurions, free of charge.
EDCS-67000014.summary: An inscription recording an honor bestowed upon Marcus Antonius Neanthus, an Augustalis, who funded a public work himself, likely from an Italian town during the Imperial period.

EDCS-67000017.summary: A dedication or maker's inscription by Marcus Hortorius Thalamus, possibly related to a building or artwork, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-67200476.translation: adlected... and... Callistus... and... Crescens... and... Capito and... Diadumenus... and... Philippus... and...anthus... and...nius adlected... mens adlected... verus adlected...mus and... Treptus... and...nus and... Epaphroditus... Glaphyr adlected... ens and...hodus... genius adlected...ena and... Silvius... and...eus and... Euhemer... Marcellus adlected... Publius Aufidius... Lucius Pomentinus and Publius Rubrius... Publius Veturus rus and Publius Annius Fortunatus, Publius Annius Annianus adlected, Gaius Paetieus Hilarianus and Titus Flavius Primitivos, Lucius Numisius Delphicus adlected, Aulus Egrilius Sabinus and Gaius Julius Fortunatus, Gnaeus Apuleius Verus and Marcus Farranius Hermes, Gnaeus Turpilius Agathopus adlected, Gnaeus Turpilius Gnesius junior adlected, Marcus Aemilius... Publius Pompon... Quintus Patr... Titus Valerius Agathanus adlected, Quintus Cannus... and Sextus Sestius Pyramus, Lucius Sentius Hermes and Lucius Aristius Amemptus, Lucius Aristius Thallus adlected, Sextus Apuleius Veratius Decrius Auctus quinquennales, Quintus Valerius Zosimus and Gaius Popilius Phoebus, Titus Carvilius Olympicus adlected.
EDCS-67200476.summary: A very fragmentary inscription listing numerous names, many marked as 'adlected' (selected or appointed to a role), possibly related to a civic or administrative body, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-67200479.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Euphrates, Grania Asia.
EDCS-67200479.summary: A fragmented funerary dedication mentioning two individuals, possibly a couple or family members, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-68000013.translation: To the Divine Shades. Tyrannus, slave of Gaius Sulpicius Festus, to his beloved fellow slave, well-deserving.
EDCS-68000013.summary: This funerary epitaph, dating to the Roman Imperial period, records the devotion of a slave to his deceased partner.

EDCS-69500150.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Ulpius Decrianus the elder made this for Marcus Ulpius Decrianus.
EDCS-69500150.summary: This Roman funerary epitaph, likely from the Imperial period, records a father setting up a tomb for his son with the same name.

EDCS-70300306.translation: The entrance to the gymnasium of the young men of Lucoferia, along with all its roofing tiles and beams, was constructed from his own funds by the donor for his fellow young men. [---] He supervised the gymnasium for the young men under the curatorship of the esteemed Pompeianus and Geminius Felix, on the 21st day before the Kalends of May, in the consulship of Sabinus II and Anullinus.
EDCS-70300306.summary: This inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the construction of a gymnasium entrance by a benefactor for the local youth, including details of the officials and consuls.

EDCS-70700156.translation: Titus Flavius Euphrosynus, son of Titus, from the Arnensian tribe, a sevir Augustalis, aedile, quaestor of provisions, and duovir, during the consulship of Petronius Mamertinus and Tineius Rufus, with Quintus Vibius Paris and Publius Licinius Valentinus as curators.
EDCS-70700156.summary: This Roman inscription from the Imperial period lists the various magistracies held by Titus Flavius Euphrosynus, noting his service as duovir during a specific consulship.

EDCS-70700157.translation: Publius Aelius Aphrodisius, son of Publius, duovir with aedilician power, quaestor of provisions, and one of the Seviri Augustales, remitted the expenses after receiving the honour, for the women of Feron, the people, during the consulship of Lucius Bruttii Crispinus and Lucius Roscio Aelianus.
EDCS-70700157.summary: This inscription from the Roman Imperial period records Publius Aelius Aphrodisius, a local magistrate, remitting costs associated with an honour granted to him by the town of Feron.

EDCS-70800042.summary: This fragmentary Roman funerary epitaph records the name of a child, Cosconius, and their age at death.

EDCS-70800044.translation: Fisevia, daughter of Tiberius, lived 80 years.
EDCS-70800044.summary: This Roman funerary epitaph records the name and age at death of Fisevia, daughter of Tiberius.

EDCS-70800127.translation: To the Divine Shades. [---] Ulpius, of the Legion(?), who lived 45 years, 6 months, and 11 days. Ulpius Philomathes(?) and Ulpia Aprotes(?) made this monument for their dearest father. This monument shall not bind the heir.
EDCS-70800127.summary: This Roman funerary epitaph, likely from the Imperial period, records the death details of Ulpius and commemorates him with a monument that does not pass to his heir.

EDCS-70800225.translation: Publius Antistius Eros, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-70800225.summary: This Roman inscription from the Imperial period records the name and relationship (freedman) of Publius Antistius Eros.

EDCS-70800233.summary: This Roman funerary epitaph records the name of Lollia Procula and her age at death.

EDCS-70800234.translation: To Clodius Feliximus, who lived 65 years. Capr(i)ola made this for her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-70800234.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Capr(i)ola to her husband Clodius Feliximus.

EDCS-70800316.summary: This dedication is made to the goddess Ceres.

EDCS-70900765.summary: This funerary monument is for [3]inia Hillaria.

EDCS-70900834.summary: This funerary monument is for Vettia Pieris.

EDCS-70900844.summary: This funerary monument is for Albia Fortuna.

EDCS-70900845.translation: Of Lucius Tussanius Niger, son of Sextus, from Clustumina.
EDCS-70900845.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Tussanius Niger.

EDCS-70900997.translation: Sacred to Victoria. Lucius Perperna, son of Quintus; Gaius Terentius, son of Aulus; Gaius Gavius, son of Gaius Ru[...], the three men in charge. Sacred to the August Emperors' Concord.
EDCS-70900997.summary: This dedication likely records a group of officials dedicating something to Victoria and the Concord of the Emperors.

EDCS-70901075.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Gaius Fuficius Trophimus, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-70901075.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated to Gaius Fuficius Trophimus.

EDCS-71000443.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Severus, son of the deified Augustus Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the country. The public community of Hebanus, devoted to his divine majesty and power, placed this and saw to its erection by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-71000443.summary: This is a dedication by the community of Hebanus to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, recording his titles and dignities.

EDCS-71000459.translation: On the Nones of April(?), roses completed. Iulius Epagatus, C[3]nius Ful[vus](?), [3]ius [3], Cominius Faust[us] fulfilled their vow willingly(?). On the twelfth day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-71000459.summary: This inscription records individuals fulfilling a vow, possibly related to a floral offering, on specific dates.

EDCS-71000461.translation: Greetings? To Secundus, son of B...
EDCS-71000461.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or greeting, possibly to a person named Secundus.

EDCS-71000464.translation: Gaius Antistius Naso, son of Gaius, and Apate, freedwoman of a woman (named Fabia), wife of Dionysius, freedman of Faustus, a doctor, made this.
EDCS-71000464.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Apate for her husband Dionysius, who was a freedman and a doctor, commissioned by Gaius Antistius Naso.

EDCS-71000468.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription bearing the name and filiation of Lucius Larcius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-71000469.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the name and father of Quintus Purpuro.

EDCS-71000472.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription bearing the name and filiation of Publius Mituleius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-71000473.translation: Titus Hatilius Philod[---], freedman of Caius.
EDCS-71000473.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription for Titus Hatilius Philod[---], a freedman of Caius.

EDCS-71000474.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription bearing the name Lucius Manlius.

EDCS-71000476.translation: M. Hilarus, son of C. Caecilius...
EDCS-71000476.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a person named Hilarus, son of C. Caecilius.

EDCS-71000477.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription bearing the name Marcus Caecilius Marcasus(?).

EDCS-71000679.translation: Emperor Hadrianus Augustus to the Pyrgenses.
EDCS-71000679.summary: This inscription records a decree or dedication by Emperor Hadrian to the people of Pyrgi.

EDCS-71000740.translation: To [---], son of Marcus, of the Horatia tribe, [---] quaestor [---] by testament, by the arbitration of Philadespotus [---] from 50,000 sesterces.
EDCS-71000740.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a bequest from a man who died leaving a sum of money for a public official.

EDCS-71100136.translation: To the Great and Unconquered Emperor Caesar Gaius Valerius Diocletian, the Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, Tribune for the third time, Consul for the second time, Father of the Fatherland, Proconsul, the council and people of Luna, devoted to his divine majesty and authority.
EDCS-71100136.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Diocletian, likely set up by the local community of Luna, dating to his third tribunician power and second consulship.

EDCS-71100137.translation: To Marcus Turtellius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Galeria tribe.
EDCS-71100137.summary: This is a dedication to a man named Marcus Turtellius Rufus.

EDCS-71200439.translation: To Mars. Titus Julius Verecundus, a veteran of the First Minervia Legion, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-71200439.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mars by a veteran of the First Minervia Legion.

EDCS-71200440.summary: This is a very brief votive inscription to Hercules.

EDCS-71300029.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Marcus Ulpius Epaphroditus, freedman of Augustus, procurator of the private treasury, procurator of the Tiburtine estates, [---].
EDCS-71300029.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Ulpius Epaphroditus, a freedman of Augustus who held procuratorial posts.

EDCS-71300032.translation: To Gaius Rufius Marcellinus, most distinguished boy, grandson of [---] and of the Rufii, [---].
EDCS-71300032.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Gaius Rufius Marcellinus, whose maternal grandparents were from the Rufii family.

EDCS-71300035.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Publius Virasius Venusius made this for his most dutiful and deserving brother, Publius Virasius Hermogenes.
EDCS-71300035.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Publius Virasius Venusius for his brother Publius Virasius Hermogenes.

EDCS-71300036.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Made for Primigenia, who deserved it.
EDCS-71300036.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Primigenia.

EDCS-71400197.translation: Aulus [---] Optati [---] son of Lucius Rustius.
EDCS-71400197.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or a funerary marker, mentioning individuals named Aulus, Optatus, and Lucius Rustius.

EDCS-72600217.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the genitive of a Roman personal name, Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-72600224.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the Roman personal name, Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-72600303.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the genitive of a Roman personal name, Marcus Perennius.

EDCS-72600304.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the genitive of a Roman personal name, Marcus Perennius.

EDCS-72600308.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the genitive of a Roman personal name, Publius Cornelius.

EDCS-72600311.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning the genitive of a Roman personal name, Marcus Perennius.

EDCS-72900062.translation: Sextus Valerius Flaccus, son of Gaius; Gaius Herennius Ganymedes, freedman of Gaius; Sextus Sextius, freedman of Marcus; the three men, sacred to the Tutelary Hercules.
EDCS-72900062.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by three officials (IIIviri) to the god Hercules Tutanus, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-72900063.translation: [Unknown person], son of Gaius, Pontifex; Aulus Marcius Rentio, freedman of Aulus; Publius Vettius Antiocus, freedman of Publius; the three men, sacred to Mercury.
EDCS-72900063.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by three officials (IIIviri), including a Pontifex, to the god Mercury, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-72900064.translation: Lucius Firmius Pollio, son of Lucius, of the Clustumina tribe, quinquennalis, tribune of the soldiers of the 12th Gallic Legion and the Fourth Legion.
EDCS-72900064.summary: This inscription records the career of Lucius Firmius Pollio, who held civic office (quinquennalis) and military positions, likely from a colonia in the late 1st century BC or early 1st century AD.

EDCS-73800097.translation: To the spirits of the departed; to Faustinus, Fausticus, Festinus, and Festus, who deserved well.
EDCS-73800097.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring at least four individuals, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-74000094.translation: Lucius Aelius Crassus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-74000094.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-74000095.translation: Lucius Avillius Brocchus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-74000095.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-74700531.translation: To the divine spirits. To Aufidia Fortunata, for her well-deserving freedwoman and wife. Lucius Aufidius Iustus.
EDCS-74700531.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband to his deceased wife.

EDCS-74700533.translation: Aulus Cosconius Custurna, son of Aulus, of the tribe Tromentina.
EDCS-74700533.summary: This is a personal name with tribal affiliation, likely an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-74700559.translation: Flavia Epictesis dedicated this gift to Fortuna.
EDCS-74700559.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Flavia Epictesis.

EDCS-75200393.translation: To the divine spirits. To Publius Aquillius Restitutus, a well-deserving fellow student. Marcus Ulpius Maximianus. Aquilia Felicitas, sister, made this for her most devoted brother.
EDCS-75200393.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a colleague and a sister for Publius Aquillius Restitutus.

EDCS-75600261.translation: To Junia Calliena, a most distinguished woman.
EDCS-75600261.summary: This is an epitaph honoring Junia Calliena, likely a woman of high social standing.

EDCS-76000156.translation: Lucius Campatius Tobrio, son of Lucius.
EDCS-76000156.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-76000157.translation: Marcus Aburius Damio, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-76000157.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Aburius Damio, a freedman of a female owner.

EDCS-76000158.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-76400076.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Hostilius Maximus and Hostilia Flora set up this monument to Tiberius Claudius Hilarion, who lived 50 years, for his well-deserved merit.
EDCS-76400076.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Hilarion, set up by his heirs, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-76800109.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus Vismatius Corinthus set up this monument to Sextus Vismatius Romanianus, who lived 3 years, 8 months, and 3 days. [and] Primigenia [---].
EDCS-76800109.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Sextus Vismatius Romanianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-76900119.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Adinna Severus and Adinnia Maxima set up this monument to their most devoted father, Adinna Maximus, who lived 42 years, 7 months, and 5 days, for his well-deserved merit.
EDCS-76900119.summary: A funerary epitaph for Adinna Maximus, set up by his children, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-77700166.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Damio, freedman of Marcus Aburius [and of a woman, name illegible].
EDCS-77700166.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Damio, a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-77700185.translation: Aurelia Agapes, his wife, and their sons set up this monument to Aurelius He[r]eneus, who lived 71 years and 4 days, a deacon for 5 years, and a presbyter for 30 years and 8 months, for his well-deserved merit.
EDCS-77700185.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aurelius Hereneus, a Christian cleric, set up by his wife and sons, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-78200024.translation: In the consulship of Tiberius Claudius Caesar IV and Lucius Vitellius III.
EDCS-78200024.summary: A dating formula referencing the consuls Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and Lucius Vitellius, likely from the year 47 CE.

EDCS-78200041.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul. The council of the Rusellani, devoted to his divinity and majesty.
EDCS-78200041.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Constantius I, likely from the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, commissioned by the local council of the Rusellani.

EDCS-79300009.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Petronius Dignus, centurion of the XXII Primigenia legion, set up this monument to his excellent freedman, Publius Petronius Sosthenes.
EDCS-79300009.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Petronius Sosthenes, a freedman, set up by his patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80300117.summary: A fragmentary inscription with personal names, possibly an ownership mark or a dedication, of uncertain date.

EDCS-80300120.summary: A fragmentary inscription with personal names, possibly an ownership mark or a dedication, of uncertain date.

EDCS-80600047.summary: This is a gravestone or personal monument inscribed with the name Lucius Primus.

EDCS-80600057.summary: This is a gravestone or personal monument inscribed with the name Gaius Numerius Restitutus.

EDCS-81800031.translation: To Gaius Clodius, son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe.
EDCS-81800031.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Gaius Clodius, son of Lucius, mentioning his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-81800059.translation: Quintus Fabius Eutychianus, patron and perpetual quinquennial, dedicated at his own expense to the virtue of the body of the college of dendrophori of the Carians quarter.
EDCS-81800059.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Quintus Fabius Eutychianus, a patron and official, to the dendrophori college in the Carians quarter.

EDCS-82400015.summary: This is a gravestone or personal monument inscribed with the name Sextus Gavi Celer.

EDCS-82900057.translation: Gaius Autronius, Marcus Roscius, son of Marcus, Gaius Baebius, freedman of Gaius, Gaius Praeconius, masters, to Tiberinus Mercurius, to Jupiter.
EDCS-82900057.summary: This fragmented inscription records the names of officials (magistri) and dedications to the deities Mercurius and Jupiter, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-00380220.summary: This inscription is fragmentary, naming Aufustius, son of Quintus, with incomplete preceding and succeeding text.

EDCS-00380222.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a dedication of 30 feet made by Obsequentius.

EDCS-00380223.translation: Marinianus the deacon made 300 feet; Iovinianus made 200 feet; Marcellus made 200 feet; Gaudentius made 200 feet; Optatus made 100 feet; Septiminus made 100 feet; Euresius made 65 feet; Vericundus made 60 feet; Decentius made 50 feet; Delmatius made 50 feet; Laurentius made 50 feet; Iovianus made 50 feet; Fortunatus made 50 feet; Hilarius made 50 feet.
EDCS-00380223.summary: This inscription records a series of dedications of lengths of feet, likely for a building project or boundary, made by various individuals including Marinianus the deacon.

EDCS-00380225.translation: To the sweetest son Florentius, well-deserving, in peace, who lived 14 years, 2 months, 1 day.
EDCS-00380225.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Florentius, recording his age at death and commending him to peace.

EDCS-00380231.translation: Iucundus Lani Fo Iucundus Lani Fort
EDCS-00380231.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose, but contains the name Iucundus.

EDCS-00380236.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose, but records the name Quintus Fulvius.

EDCS-00600112.translation: Arbuscula, freedwoman of Egnatia Cai and wife.
EDCS-00600112.summary: This is an epitaph recording Arbuscula, a freedwoman of Egnatia Cai, who is also identified as his wife.

EDCS-02900217.translation: In honor of the most illustrious Saint Justus, the abbot ordered [it] to be made during the time of our lord Cunincpert, king, and bishop Gaudentianus, in the year...
EDCS-02900217.summary: This inscription records an order by the abbot to build something in honor of Saint Justus during the reign of King Cunincpert and Bishop Gaudentianus.

EDCS-02900218.translation: Abaeus X b, procurator of our lord Gallienus.
EDCS-02900218.summary: This inscription identifies Abaeus as a procurator of Gallienus.

EDCS-02900221.translation: in honor of the holy and illustrious Gastaldus, [he/she] ordered [it] to be made in the time of our lord Cunincpert, king, and bishop Gaudentianus, in the year
EDCS-02900221.summary: This inscription records an order by an unnamed individual to build something in honor of Gastaldus during the reign of King Cunincpert and Bishop Gaudentianus.

EDCS-02900225.translation: Lucius P D Lucius P D
EDCS-02900225.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose, but repeats the name Lucius.

EDCS-02900226.translation: Cassius, the slave of Cai, made [this].
EDCS-02900226.summary: This is a private dedication by a slave named Cassius, likely for his owner Cai.

EDCS-02900230.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Claudia Longina perished without blame; a bitter fate snatched her away.
EDCS-02900230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Claudia Longina, lamenting her untimely death.

EDCS-02900232.translation: The workshop of Iulia Saturnina, during the consulship of Gallicanus and Vetus; pottery work.
EDCS-02900232.summary: This inscription records pottery production from the workshop of Iulia Saturnina, dated by consuls to the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-03000321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Domatia Cyrene at death.

EDCS-03300197.summary: This is a numerical inscription, possibly related to a measurement or count, with an unknown context.

EDCS-03300198.summary: This inscription identifies an individual as the 'procurator of the city' and provides a number, possibly a reference to a building or property.

EDCS-03300204.summary: This is a short inscription identifying 'Euticius' as a martyr, likely from a tomb or commemorative marker.

EDCS-03300205.translation: Volcia, freedwoman of a woman, made [this] for herself and her family, and for Lucius Sestius Primigenius.
EDCS-03300205.summary: This is a private dedication made by Volcia, a freedwoman, for herself, her family, and Lucius Sestius Primigenius.

EDCS-03300207.translation: Gaius Furius Proculus, son of Gaius, lived [here].
EDCS-03300207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and filiation of Gaius Furius Proculus.

EDCS-03700205.translation: Manius Acilius Proculus, son of Gaius, consul, captured Heraclea.
EDCS-03700205.summary: This inscription commemorates the military achievement of Manius Acilius Proculus, who captured Heraclea during his consulship.

EDCS-03700208.summary: This is an epitaph for Caius Vittidius Niger, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700247.translation: To the Divine Manes. Julius Valens erected this for his father-in-law, the well-deserving.
EDCS-03700247.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Julius Valens for his father-in-law, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900259.translation: Theotimus, slave of Bara Appius Marci, made this. Diodorus, slave of Bara Appius Marci, made this. Sosia.
EDCS-04900259.summary: This inscription records the construction or dedication of a monument by slaves of Bara Appius Marci, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900266.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, for Sextus Avilledius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900267.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Gaius Baius, son of Gaius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900268.translation: Gaius Clodius Successus, Gaius Clodius Syrianus.
EDCS-04900268.summary: This inscription lists two names, Gaius Clodius Successus and Gaius Clodius Syrianus, possibly related individuals, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-04900270.translation: Lucius Tuccius, son of Tiberius, of the Arnensian tribe, Rufus; Caius Tuccius, son of Tiberius, of the Arnensian tribe, Scaeva; Lucius Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the Maxumus branch; Caius Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the Rufi branch; Lucius Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the Galli branch. In front 20 feet, in the field 12 feet.
EDCS-04900270.summary: This inscription records the names of several members of the Tuccius family, likely marking land ownership or a property boundary, with dimensions given in feet, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000217.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Larthia Methonia, noting her mother Tosnonia, likely from the Roman Imperial period, possibly of Etruscan origin.

EDCS-05000218.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Quintus Narius, son of Oumbrius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000227.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Publius Anilius, son of Publius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05000228.translation: To our lord Flavius Iovianus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious and Triumphant, Ever Augustus, born for the good of the republic, 86,000 [units of tribute?].
EDCS-05000228.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Jovian, likely from a provincial administrative context, dating to his reign (363-364 AD).

EDCS-05000231.translation: Lucius Aburius Pelops, son of Lucius. Cinthia Flora, freedwoman of Caius. Aburia Glycera, freedwoman of [?]. Lucius Veturius Antigonus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-05000231.summary: This inscription lists the names of several freedmen and freedwomen, likely belonging to different households or patrons, possibly from a funerary context.

EDCS-05000236.translation: Quintus Salvidenus Zosimus, attendant of Lucius Cornificius. Saturnia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius, by the arbitration of Caius Cuspius Capito and Saturia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-05000236.summary: This inscription records a legal arbitration overseen by individuals, indicating a property or inheritance dispute settlement.

EDCS-05000238.translation: Minio Ciminus Silva, sacred [place?]; Subseciva; Ultra.
EDCS-05000238.summary: This inscription seems to be a territorial or boundary marker, possibly indicating sacred land or land beyond a certain point.

EDCS-05000239.translation: Caius Valerius Zetus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-05000239.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication or ownership marker by a freedman, likely on a tomb or property.

EDCS-05200198.translation: Marcus Quinctius Chilo, son of Marcus Quinctius, of the Horatia tribe, military tribune, first-rank centurion.
EDCS-05200198.summary: This inscription records the career of Marcus Quinctius Chilo, detailing his military service and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05200202.translation: Marcus Lucilius, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe, made this for his mother while alive.
EDCS-05200202.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Lucilius for his mother, specifying his tribe and that it was erected during his lifetime.

EDCS-05200203.translation: Marcus Larcius, son of Marcus, of the Stellatina tribe, and Posilla Hermidia, daughter of Caius, of the Stellatina tribe, made this for themselves and their families.
EDCS-05200203.summary: This inscription is a joint funerary dedication made by Marcus Larcius and Posilla Hermidia for themselves and their families, indicating their tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05200204.translation: Caius Anicius, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe, aedile, and Alpionia, freedwoman of the woman Statonia, and Lucius Caius Anicius, a freedman, [?].
EDCS-05200204.summary: This inscription records the names and offices of several individuals, including an aedile and freedpersons, possibly related to a public building or benefaction.

EDCS-05200212.summary: This inscription is a simple ownership or dedication statement, possibly for a tomb or property, belonging to Sextus Titus Stellinus.

EDCS-05401309.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus.
EDCS-05401309.summary: This inscription is a dedication or acclamation to the emperor Maxentius, likely dating to his reign (306-312 CE).

EDCS-06100234.translation: To good memory, in peace. Petronia lived for 20 years and 50 days, laid to rest the day before the Ides of November.
EDCS-06100234.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia, recording her lifespan and date of burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06200004.translation: Quintus Fundanius, son of Gaius, of the Galerian tribe, lies here. Quintus Fundanius, son of Quintus, a Roman, made (this tomb) in his lifetime for himself and his descendants, with 12 feet in front and 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-06200004.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and tomb construction record by Quintus Fundanius for himself and his descendants, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot, likely from the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-06200007.translation: Achilles for his own wife Geminia Myrtale, for the sake of final remembrance, this tomb, on condition that no one has the authority to sell or place (anyone else) in it, except if Achilles himself suffers a human fate. But if anyone ejects Myrtale, he will pay 2500 (denarii) to the treasury.
EDCS-06200007.summary: This is a funerary dedication with specific conditions for burial and penalties for violation, commissioned by Achilles for his wife Myrtale, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06200008.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Barachai, son of Gaius, of Sidon. Hilara, his wife.
EDCS-06200008.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Barachai, son of Gaius, of Sidonian origin, by his wife Hilara, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06200011.translation: To good memory. Lucius Venuleius and Lucius Venuleius Apronianus (dedicated this) to Laetilia Celerina, his wife.
EDCS-06200011.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Lucius Venuleius and Lucius Venuleius Apronianus to Laetilia Celerina, his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06200012.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Aurellius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06200013.translation: To Dexippus, slave of Tiberius Caesar.
EDCS-06200013.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Dexippus, a slave of Tiberius Caesar, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400156.translation: To the departed spirits. For Hordionius Genialis, to his son Marcus Hordionius Romanus, well-deserving, who lived for 3 years, 2 months, 28 days, 10 hours.
EDCS-07400156.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Hordionius Romanus, recording his age at death with exceptional detail, dedicated by his father Hordionius Genialis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400276.translation: Sacred to Good Health. Gnaeus Pacilius Marna, sevir and Augustalis from Sutrium, from Faleri, in fulfillment of a vow. Pacilia Primitiva (dedicated this) to the good Bonadia Castrensis, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-07400276.summary: This inscription records two votive dedications to the goddess of Good Health (Salus), one by Gnaeus Pacilius Marna and another by Pacilia Primitiva, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400284.summary: This inscription is a name, likely of the deceased, on a tombstone.

EDCS-07400285.translation: Of Marcus Lollius Felix, son of Decimus.
EDCS-07400285.summary: This inscription is a name and patronymic, likely of the deceased, on a tombstone.

EDCS-07400286.translation: Lucius Nivellius, son of Lucius Nivellius.
EDCS-07400286.summary: This inscription appears to be a name and patronymic, possibly recording ownership or a familial relationship on a monument.

EDCS-07400287.translation: Of Publius Aninius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-07400287.summary: This inscription is a name and patronymic, likely of the deceased, on a tombstone.

EDCS-07400288.translation: Albanus, freedman of Caius Minicius, made [this].
EDCS-07400288.summary: This inscription records that Albanus, a freedman of Caius Minicius, dedicated a monument.

EDCS-08300275.translation: Cn. [son] of Caius, of the Feronia tribe, gives this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08300275.summary: This inscription records a willing dedication by Cn. [son] of Caius, of the Feronia tribe.

EDCS-08300276.translation: [---]ius, son of Marcius, of the Feronia tribe, gives willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08300276.summary: This inscription records a willing dedication by [---]ius, son of Marcius, of the Feronia tribe.

EDCS-08300292.translation: Vettia Pasiphila willingly and deservedly [gives] to Isis a stole and a cloak, golden eyes.
EDCS-08300292.summary: This inscription records a dedication of religious items, including golden eyes, to the goddess Isis by Vettia Pasiphila.

EDCS-08500285.translation: This is the palace of Minerva, [built in the year] 507 of the city.
EDCS-08500285.summary: This inscription marks a building as belonging to Minerva and dates it to 507 AUC (255 CE).

EDCS-08500287.summary: This inscription records the manumission status of an individual, linking them to both a previous owner and potentially a freedman of Feronia.

EDCS-08500288.translation: Lucius Calpurnius, a worthy gift to Feronia.
EDCS-08500288.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Feronia by Lucius Calpurnius.

EDCS-08500291.translation: To Sorilius Bassus, son of Caius, of the Pupinia tribe, chief scribe, Pacia, daughter of Caius, his wife, [dedicates this to] Caius Sorilius, son of Quintus, of the Romilia tribe.
EDCS-08500291.summary: This funerary inscription names several family members and includes their tribal affiliations and a profession.

EDCS-08900323.translation: Sacred to Fortunae Visentis. Marcus Minatius, son of Marcus, Sabatina, wife of Gallus, IIvir iure dicundo, in his quinquennial term, as a mark of honor, also on account of an honorary dedication, gave a feast for the villagers and pastry and honeyed wine for the people.
EDCS-08900323.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Fortuna by Marcus Minatius, a magistrate, who also provided a public feast and refreshments.

EDCS-08900324.translation: Augustalis lived for years in Rome, contubernalis.
EDCS-08900324.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription recording the life span and status of an Augustalis, possibly a soldier or member of a collegium.

EDCS-08900325.translation: To the Divine Shades and memory of Aurelia Felicitas, a wife well-deserving, mother of sons.
EDCS-08900325.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aurelia Felicitas, a devoted wife and mother.

EDCS-08900362.translation: To good memory. Paulus, who lived more or less 90 years, to whom three sons erected this monument, was buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of December, in peace.
EDCS-08900362.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial of Paulus, who lived to be about 90 years old, and was honored by his three sons.

EDCS-08900902.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sons made [this] for Caetenia Acta, a mother well-deserving.
EDCS-08900902.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by sons to their deserving mother, Caetenia Acta.

EDCS-08900904.translation: To Tigris, the best mother, Sextus Nonius Absens [dedicated this].
EDCS-08900904.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Tigris, referred to as 'best mother', by Sextus Nonius Absens.

EDCS-08900908.translation: Valeria, freedwoman of Quintus, made this monument for Psicharius, her freedman, and for herself, Lucio Quintio, freedman of Lucius, while alive.
EDCS-08900908.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription set up by Valeria, a freedwoman, for herself, her freedman, and another freedman, Lucio Quintio.

EDCS-08900914.summary: This is a simple funerary monument inscription stating that Lucius Ataeus Caunus made it.

EDCS-08900922.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deity Auxano, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08900923.translation: Here rests the well-deserving girl Valeria, from the third school of the shield-bearers, during the consulship of Honorius Augustus for the 7th time and Theodosius Augustus for the 2nd time, on the 8th day before the Ides of February. She breathed her last when she was 16 years, 5 months old. She was with her husband Virginus for 3 years, 6 months, and 7 days. She rested in peace and for herself and her heirs.
EDCS-08900923.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young girl named Valeria, detailing her age, marital status, and the date of her death during the consulships of Honorius and Theodosius, indicating a date in the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-08900930.translation: Here lies Candidilla the infant, who died before completing her second year and thus rested in peace. Her parents, always reluctant, made her an eternal home. Interred on the 17th day before the Kalends of August, during the consulship of Anicius Bassus and Flavius Philippus, most excellent men.
EDCS-08900930.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an infant named Candidilla, who died before the age of two, and records her burial date and the consuls of the year, placing it in the late Roman period.

EDCS-09001307.translation: To the Divine Shades, Quintus Curtius Apolonius is placed here.
EDCS-09001307.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the underworld deities (Dis Manibus) for Quintus Curtius Apolonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09001318.translation: Here rests in peace Moderatus of remarkable memory, who lived approximately 50 years. Interred on the 14th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-09001318.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Moderatus, noting his approximate age at death and the date of his burial, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09001322.translation: Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, made this in Calenos.
EDCS-09001322.summary: This inscription records the action of Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, and specifies the location as Calenos, likely a dedication or construction record from the Roman period.

EDCS-09001325.translation: Here will rest the spotless lamb, Carterius, who lived 3 years, 6 months, and 15 days. Interred in peace during the consulship of Calepius and Artaburus for the third time, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-09001325.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Carterius, specifying his age and burial date, including the consuls, placing it in the late Roman period.

EDCS-09200253.summary: This is a simple funerary or dedication mentioning Aurelius Cresimus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200264.translation: Caius Numitorius Ion made this for himself, his wife Egnatia Nysa, and his children Egnatia Elpis and Calpurnia Spatale, and his descendants.
EDCS-09200264.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Caius Numitorius Ion for himself, his family, and his descendants, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09300896.translation: A good man who advised on this road.
EDCS-09300896.summary: This is an epitaph or dedication praising a 'good man' who was involved with the construction or maintenance of a road, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-09400322.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Gavius Capito Maximianus, scribe of a tribune, quaestor's scribe, scribe of the curule aediles, tribune of the tenth legion Gemina.
EDCS-09400322.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gavius Capito Maximianus, who held several administrative and military positions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400323.translation: Valeria Polla made this for herself and for Gaius Caecilius Proculus, scribe of the curule aediles, her most excellent and indulgent patron.
EDCS-09400323.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Valeria Polla for herself and her patron, Gaius Caecilius Proculus, a scribe of the curule aediles, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400324.translation: Varro, freedman of Publius Cartilius Menippus, made this; also for Publius Cartilius Varro, son of Publius, and for Polla, daughter of Roia; and Hilara, freedwoman of Publius Cartilius.
EDCS-09400324.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by several freedmen and family members for deceased individuals, including Varro and Hilara, freedmen of Publius Cartilius, and Publius Cartilius Varro, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09400327.translation: Gaius Petronius Hilarus, freedman of Reicius, willingly fulfilled a vow he had undertaken, as he deserved.
EDCS-09400327.summary: This is a dedication recording the fulfillment of a vow by Gaius Petronius Hilarus, a freedman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400328.translation: Salvilla Voluminia made this for Sextus Aponius Theophilus, freedman of Sextus.
EDCS-09400328.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Salvilla Voluminia for her freedman, Sextus Aponius Theophilus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400329.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulia Athenais, a freedwoman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400330.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Clecius Mactorius, a triclinium worker, placed this for one who deserved well.
EDCS-09400330.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Clecius Mactorius, identified as a 'triclinium worker', likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400331.translation: Maecia Saluta, freedwoman of Gaius, for herself, and for her patron, and for Titus Reienus Celer, son of Titus.
EDCS-09400331.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Maecia Saluta, a freedwoman, for herself, her patron, and Titus Reienus Celer, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400332.translation: Menander Faustus, freedman, from his own resources.
EDCS-09400332.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription set up by Menander Faustus, a freedman, using his own funds, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09400333.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Lucius Obilius, son of Lucius, likely from the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09400334.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Populonius, an actor, made this for his dearest grandson Pompeius Gordianus, who lived for 3 years, 11 days, and 3 hours, his deserving dearest.
EDCS-09400334.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young boy, set up by his grandfather, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09400335.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Justinus, Laegitima Leo and Rufina Laegitimus, children and grandchildren, erected this for their deserving mother Rufia Rufina, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-09400335.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman, set up by her children and grandchildren, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09400336.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Eucharistus, the father, and Chia, the mother, made this for their prematurely taken infant Valerianus.
EDCS-09400336.summary: A funerary epitaph for an infant, set up by his parents, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09400337.translation: Valeria, daughter of Caius, [daughter] of the Julian line of Caius, [for] Gaius Julius Avitus, son of Caius, who lived for [years]...
EDCS-09400337.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely for a son named Gaius Julius Avitus, set up by his mother Valeria, with some genealogical information.

EDCS-09400338.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly the name of a person, the context or purpose is unknown.

EDCS-09400339.translation: Caesia Isstabilis set this up for her most unusual husband, who lived 26 years.
EDCS-09400339.summary: A funerary epitaph for a husband, set up by his wife, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09400340.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Gaius Cutius Taurus made this for his deserving wife Vibia Legitima, who lived 30 years, 3 months, 20 days. Legitima, farewell.
EDCS-09400340.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her husband, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09401057.translation: Remember death. Agapomenus, my freedman, made this for Felicitas, his deserving wife, a most sweet mother of children, who lived 50 years, 3 months, 10 days, and who lived with me for 35 years, 11 months, 10 days, with fidelity and chastity.
EDCS-09401057.summary: A funerary epitaph for a wife, set up by her freedman husband, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09401413.translation: Lucius Torius Pilarus [set this up for] Hilarus, son of Ruber.
EDCS-09401413.summary: A dedication or funerary epitaph, possibly for Hilarus, son of Ruber, by Lucius Torius Pilarus.

EDCS-09700136.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary epitaph for Terentius Calocas.

EDCS-09700948.translation: To our Lords, Constantius and Maximianus Augusti, and Diocletian and Maximianus, elder Augusti, and Severus and Maximinus, most noble Caesars, 13 miles. For the good of the Republic, to our master Flavius Claudius Julianus, pious, fortunate, victorious, and triumphant, ever Augustus, 85 miles.
EDCS-09700948.summary: This inscription, likely a milestone, records distances under the Augusti Diocletian and Maximian and the Caesars Severus and Maximinus, and also honors Julian the Apostate.

EDCS-09701466.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Gaius Grebo, son of Caius.

EDCS-09701467.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Murria Secunda, daughter of Quintus.

EDCS-09701468.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Marcus Pontius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-09701470.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Marcus Rusius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-09701471.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Saturia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-09701474.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Marcus Tarna, son of Lucius.

EDCS-09701475.translation: Felix, freedman of the woman Marcus Rufius.
EDCS-09701475.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felix, a freedman, mentioning his former mistress Marcus Rufius.

EDCS-09701477.translation: Of Lucius Aelius Crassus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-09701477.summary: This is a funerary epitaph referring to Lucius Aelius Crassus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-10700705.translation: Dedicated on the 15th day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of the divine Iovianus and Varronianus, to Iunius Bassus, a most distinguished man, count of the first order, vicar of the city of Rome, prefect of the city, judge of sacred cognitions, son of Iunius Bassus, a most distinguished man, prefect of the Praetorium for 14 years, and ordinary consul.
EDCS-10700705.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument or honors Iunius Bassus, a high-ranking official, in the consulship of Iovianus and Varronianus, likely in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-10700707.summary: An inscription identifying Quintus Arius as a prefect.

EDCS-10700714.summary: A dedication or maker's mark by Lucius Ataeus Caunus.

EDCS-10700729.translation: Publius Fulvius Suto, son of Caius, grandson of Caius, died on the 20th day before the Kalends of December, during the consulship of Caius Atilius and Quintus Servilius.
EDCS-10700729.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death date of Publius Fulvius Suto and the consuls of that year.

EDCS-10700748.summary: A fragmented inscription likely dedicating something to a beloved person, possibly a family member.

EDCS-10900476.translation: The burial of Justus on the 13th day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-10900476.summary: A record of the burial date of Justus.

EDCS-11600076.translation: Sextus Murrius Festus, Lucius Rasinius Pisanus, Sextus Murrius Pisanus, Lucius Rasinius Pisanus, SMP.
EDCS-11600076.summary: An inscription listing several names, possibly related to a group or public office, with an abbreviation SMP of unknown meaning.

EDCS-11800773.translation: Aulus Semonius Apolloni, son of Tiberius, a gift.
EDCS-11800773.summary: A dedication of a gift by Aulus Semonius, son of Tiberius, to someone named Apolloni.

EDCS-13302344.translation: Let the ancient builder be silent, let the past be mute. The diligent and skillful persistence of the supervisor built this work you see rising with rough roofs; Arzygius, supervisor, dedicates these baths.
EDCS-13302344.summary: An epigram on a bathhouse, attributing its construction to the supervisor Arzygius and praising his efforts.

EDCS-13400069.translation: Sacred to Nortina Minerva. Lucius Aebutius Saturnanus, son of Lucius, of the Sabatina tribe.
EDCS-13400069.summary: A dedication to the goddess Nortina Minerva by Lucius Aebutius Saturnanus.

EDCS-13400070.translation: To Caius Ligurios, son of Caius, and Aulus Gavius Fortunatus, curators of the republic, from an edict of the Saturnian decurions, with private funds, because he fostered the state's condition and cared for all with moderation. While Gnaeus Afranius Acceptus was acting as curator.
EDCS-13400070.summary: A dedication honoring Caius Ligurios and Aulus Gavius Fortunatus for their public service and moderation, funded privately by decurions under the supervision of Gnaeus Afranius Acceptus.

EDCS-13400072.translation: Aulus Herennius, son of Lucius, born of Vibia.
EDCS-13400072.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Herennius, identifying his father and mother.

EDCS-13400160.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pestinia Pollius, identifying her origin.

EDCS-13800190.translation: Eco, a tombstone for Titus. Vendias, son of Mamar, [died].
EDCS-13800190.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Eco, Titus, and Vendias.

EDCS-13900108.translation: Manius Acilius, son of Caius, consul, captured Scarphea.
EDCS-13900108.summary: This inscription records a military achievement by Manius Acilius, a consul, in capturing Scarphea.

EDCS-13900114.translation: Pesco Salvia Plaria, freedwoman of Titus, dedicated this to Feronia willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13900114.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Feronia by Pesco Salvia Plaria, a freedwoman.

EDCS-14000174.translation: To the Liberators of the world, our lords, Flavius Valentinianus, Valens and Gratianus, always Augusti, for the tenth anniversary vows and the happy twentieth anniversary vows.
EDCS-14000174.summary: This is a dedication related to anniversary vows for the emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian.

EDCS-14000175.translation: Publius Menates, son of Publius, plebeian aedile, Rome, 21.
EDCS-14000175.summary: This inscription records Publius Menates, a plebeian aedile, possibly indicating a location or year.

EDCS-14000183.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Veturius Cerdon.

EDCS-14000186.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aulus Tuccius Cyrus.

EDCS-14000189.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius, son of Lartius.

EDCS-14000190.translation: Iucundus, the farm manager, gave this as a gift to the Lares and Fortune.
EDCS-14000190.summary: This is a dedication by a farm manager to household deities and Fortune.

EDCS-14000191.translation: Concius Lora, from the theatre, scurrilous Oppia L Irena, M.
EDCS-14000191.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary list of names, possibly related to a theatrical performance or association.

EDCS-14000193.translation: To all the gods of the underworld. Lucius Anpius Polycarpus to his most sweet daughter Vetulena Gallitana, who lived 8 years, 5 months, 5 days.
EDCS-14000193.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young girl, dedicated by her father.

EDCS-14000196.summary: This is a simple owner's inscription, likely identifying property belonging to Marcus Valerius Africanus.

EDCS-14000197.summary: This is a personal name, possibly an owner's inscription or a very brief funerary marker.

EDCS-14000199.translation: Quintus Aelius Quintus. Quintus Aelius Quintus. Quintus Aelius Quintus.
EDCS-14000199.summary: This inscription is a repetitive naming, potentially an ownership mark or a practice of inscription.

EDCS-14000200.translation: Hilarus, the farm manager, for Lucius Lucretius Rufus and Septicia.
EDCS-14000200.summary: This inscription records a farm manager dedicating something for Lucretius Rufus and Septicia.

EDCS-14300118.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Minerva by Lucius Tolonios.

EDCS-15000076.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Ceres by Lucius Tolonios.

EDCS-15000120.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Casnius Secundus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-15000120.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Casnius Secundus.

EDCS-15700111.translation: Publius Seve constructed the aqueduct and fishpond.
EDCS-15700111.summary: This is a private dedication of an aqueduct and fishpond, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15800314.translation: Hermia, slave of Paquius, made this.
EDCS-15800314.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman or slave for their patron, dating probably to the early Empire.

EDCS-16100364.translation: To Luna, having undertaken a vow, Tiberius Claudius Paris offered half a pound of gold.
EDCS-16100364.summary: This is a votive offering to the goddess Luna by Tiberius Claudius Paris, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16100365.translation: Sabatinus Fabianus, son of Marcus, soldier of Legions VI and XXIX, VVVVVG, made this and took care of his own.
EDCS-16100365.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a soldier and his wife, mentioning his military service and honors, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16200755.translation: Lucius Avaenius Paser, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, soldier of the first praetorian cohort, in the centuria of Quintus Mago Clodius, served for 14 years, lived for 38 years.
EDCS-16200755.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a praetorian guardsman, detailing his service and age, likely from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16300049.translation: The Emperor Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, son of the deified Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 12th time, imperator for the 6th time, consul V, father of the country, constructed the road from Volsinii to the borders of the Clusines, the 13th.
EDCS-16300049.summary: This is a milestone or formal dedication by Emperor Trajan for the construction of a road, dated to his 12th tribunician power, likely around 108 AD.

EDCS-16400490.summary: This is a brief dedication to a deity or local spirit named Mursina, probably from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16700072.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or ownership marker, mentioning Lucius Calpetanius Rufus, probably from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16700073.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or ownership marker, mentioning Caius Cetennius Euanteus, probably from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16700074.summary: This is a dedication or funerary monument made by Caius Caetennius Saturninus, probably from the Roman Empire.

EDCS-16700150.translation: Germanus, freedman of the Emperor, made and adorned with every refinement the imperial buildings.
EDCS-16700150.summary: This inscription records the construction and decoration of imperial buildings by Germanus, an imperial freedman and procurator, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16700189.translation: To the Divine Manes. Mother Delia made this tomb for her daughter Aproniana, aged 4 years, 9 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-16700189.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a tomb by Delia for her young daughter Aproniana, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-19700173.translation: Lars Cotena, son of Lartis, dedicated this sacred offering to Minerva, having vowed it by decree of the senate when it was conceived.
EDCS-19700173.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Minerva made by Lars Cotena, son of Lartis, following a senatorial decree, likely dating to the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-19700329.summary: This inscription is a very brief dedication or marker, possibly naming an individual or individuals, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700330.summary: This inscription names an individual, Aulus Cav Panurgus, likely serving as a personal marker or dedication, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700366.translation: Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, made this.
EDCS-19700366.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700367.translation: Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, made this in Calenos.
EDCS-19700367.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, in the location of Calenos, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700373.translation: Retus Gabinius, slave of Cai, made this.
EDCS-19700373.summary: This inscription records a dedication or construction made by Retus Gabinius, a slave of Cai, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700374.translation: Retus Gabinius, slave of Cai, made this.
EDCS-19700374.summary: This inscription records a dedication or construction made by Retus Gabinius, a slave of Cai, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700375.translation: Retus Gabinios, slave of Cai, made this testament.
EDCS-19700375.summary: This inscription records a testament made by Retus Gabinius, a slave of Cai, dating to the Roman Republican or Imperial period.

EDCS-19700376.translation: Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, made this in Calenos.
EDCS-19700376.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Canoleios, son of Lucius, from Calenos.

EDCS-19700386.translation: Lucius, son of Gabinius, made this.
EDCS-19700386.summary: This inscription records that Lucius, son of Gabinius, made something.

EDCS-19700387.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Lucius Canoleios.

EDCS-19700406.summary: This inscription identifies Caius Popilius from Mevania.

EDCS-19700412.summary: This inscription identifies Cilo, son of Caius Popilius.

EDCS-19700626.translation: Titus Fourios, son of Titus, made this.
EDCS-19700626.summary: This inscription records that Titus Fourios, son of Titus, made something.

EDCS-20401517.translation: In the name of God, Gerontius, servant of Christ, wanting to fulfill his vows, placed this so that this church might be more beautiful and strengthened in Christ's name, having been worn out by age.
EDCS-20401517.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Gerontius, a servant of Christ, for the beautification and strengthening of a church, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-20402770.translation: Our workshop had it made. Sacred to Emperor Trajan Augustus and Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Aithales, the steward of Florus, a slave, set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-20402770.summary: This is a dedication from a workshop, likely in the Roman imperial period, honoring Trajan and Jupiter, and set up by Aithales, a steward and slave.

EDCS-20402789.translation: Marcus Claudius Marcellus, son of Marcus, consul for the second time.
EDCS-20402789.summary: This inscription records the name and consular iteration of Marcus Claudius Marcellus.

EDCS-20402819.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or ownership marker for Lucius Aufidius.

EDCS-20402827.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Caius Furficius.

EDCS-20402833.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Nunnius Festus, son of Marcus, and Ianuarius, to their most excellent wife and associate, Nunnia Brysa.
EDCS-20402833.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Nunnia Brysa by her husband Caius Nunnius Festus and Ianuarius.

EDCS-20402834.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or ownership marker for Caius Poppaeus Ligur.

EDCS-20402836.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication to a woman named Septuma, identified as an aunt.

EDCS-20402840.translation: To Quintus Valerius Iucundus, freedman. Agilis, Pietas, and Nor[---]r[---]vo[---] and Laev[---]vi [---].
EDCS-20402840.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to the freedman Quintus Valerius Iucundus by his freedmen Agilis, Pietas, and others.

EDCS-20402845.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Volumnius Avonius, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-20402849.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or funerary text mentioning possibly Achilius, Turtellius, and Hermonia.

EDCS-20402855.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Tertia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-20402879.translation: In this holy place rests in peace Stefaniate, who lived for more or less 22 years. She was laid to rest on the third day before the Ides of June, which renewed the sorrows of her parents. Her husband Secundus could not live longer with her, except for 7 months and 24 days, under Emperor Lord Justinian Caesar, in his 8th year.
EDCS-20402879.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Stefaniate, dating to the reign of Emperor Justinian VIII.

EDCS-20402882.translation: To good memory, in this holy place rests in peace Vigilius, a most distinguished man, who lived for more or less forty years and was laid to rest on the... day.
EDCS-20402882.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vigilius, a distinguished man, whose exact date of death is incomplete.

EDCS-20402885.translation: Marcus Cossutius, freedman of Marci, and Lucius Valerius Antiochus, freedman of Dom Lucius, willingly give this marble as a deserved offering to Fortuna Primigenia.
EDCS-20402885.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Primigenia by two freedmen, Marcus Cossutius and Lucius Valerius Antiochus, who were marble workers.

EDCS-20402887.translation: The magistri Mercuriales, Minucius Alexander and Papirius Phileros, consecrated [this].
EDCS-20402887.summary: This is a dedication by two magistri, Minucius Alexander and Papirius Phileros, to the Mercuriales, likely a collegium.

EDCS-20402890.translation: On the 13th day before the Kalends of October in Pisa, in the forum, in the Augustean [area], the following were present for the public records: Quintus Petillius, son of Quintus; Publius Rasinius Bassus, son of Lucius; Marcus Pupius, son of Marcus; Quintus Sertorius, son of Quintus; Pica; Cnaeus Octavius Rufus, son of Cnaeus; Aulus Albius Gutta, son of Aulus. Caius Canius Saturninus, as duovir, made a speech concerning the augmentation of honors for Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus Caesar, father of the fatherland, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 25th time, son of an augur, consul-designate, prince of youth, patron of our colony; what it seemed best to do regarding this matter. They resolved as follows: since the senate and people of Rome, among many other immense honors for Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus Caesar, father of the fatherland, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 25th time, son of an augur, consul-designate, by the consensus of all orders and with eager zeal, it is determined that a commission be given to Caius Canius Saturninus, as duovir, and the first ten [magistrates], to choose and inspect which of them seems to be the more suitable location for purchase with public money from private individuals, and to use the place they approve most, and at that altar, that on the 13th day before the Kalends of September, sacrifices be publicly sent to his Manes by these magistrates or those who will preside over legal proceedings there, dressed in purple mourning togas, and that at the same time black bulls and ewes, adorned with blue fillets, be sacrificed to his Manes and that those victims be burned in that place, and over them, individual urns of milk, honey, and oil be poured. And then, finally, a concession having been made to the others, if any privately wish to send offerings to his Manes, no one shall send more than one candle or one lamp or a garland, provided that those who made the sacrifices, girded in the Gabine rite, light a pyre of wood, and that they arrange it in such a way that the area before that altar, where the pyre is to be gathered and arranged, is open in all directions for 40 feet and enclosed by sturdy posts, and heaps of wood for this purpose are to be established there annually, and a large cippus is to be fixed next to the altar. This decree, along with the preceding decrees pertaining to his honors, is to be cut and inscribed. For what concerns other solemnities which it was decided and seemed proper to avoid or take care of on that same day, that what the senate and people of Rome have decreed concerning them is to be followed. And as soon as possible, legates from our order are to approach Emperor Caesar Augustus, father of the fatherland, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 25th time, and ask him to permit the colonists of Iulia, of the colony Opsequentis Iulia Pisana, to carry out and execute all these things according to this decree.
EDCS-20402890.summary: This is a lengthy public decree from Pisa, passed during the duovirate of Caius Canius Saturninus, concerning honors and sacrifices for Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, in his 25th year of tribunician power, and requesting imperial permission to enact these measures.

EDCS-20402894.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Hadrian, grandson of the divine Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the divine Nerva, Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, most indulgent prince.
EDCS-20402894.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, listing his titles and consular and tribunician powers.

EDCS-20402897.translation: To Iulia Augusta, mother of Augustus, and of the camps, and of the senate, and of the fatherland.
EDCS-20402897.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Iulia Augusta, likely Livia, mother of the emperor.

EDCS-20402900.translation: Gaius Bellicus Natalis Tebanianus, XV vir of the Flaviales.
EDCS-20402900.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Gaius Bellicus Natalis Tebanianus as a member of the XV viri of the college of the Flaviales.

EDCS-20402901.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Lucius Iulius Larcius Sabinus, tribune of the plebs, who lived 28 years and 5 days, and died while in office as tribune. His son survives him. Grandson of Prifernus Paetus, of consular rank. Son of Iulius Lucanus, of praetorian rank. His body was cared for by Cornelia Privigna, his wife, daughter of Lucius, his mother Co[...].
EDCS-20402901.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Larcius Sabinus, a tribune of the plebs who died in office at the age of 28, and details his family lineage.
