EDCS-20402905.translation: To the spirits of the dead. For Marcus Ulpius Verna, freedman of Augustus, in charge of Latin correspondence. His most unhappy wife, Vibia Thisbe.
EDCS-20402905.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Ulpius Verna, an imperial freedman in charge of Latin correspondence, dedicated by his wife.

EDCS-20402906.translation: To his devoted wife, Marcus Aurelius Iustianus, soldier of the IIII Praetorian cohort, of the century of Florus Prior, who lived 33 years and served 13 years, erected this monument. Saturnina Iovina made this for her deserving husband.
EDCS-20402906.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Saturnina Iovina for her husband, Marcus Aurelius Iustianus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402909.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Saturius Secundus, son of Lucius Saturius Picens, from the first-rank centurionate, of the Fabia tribe, a Roman knight from one of the five decuries, prefect of the II Cohort of Asturians, augur, patron of the colony of Asculum, lived 19 years and 27 days. His father erected this for his most devoted son.
EDCS-20402909.summary: This funerary monument honors Caius Saturius Secundus, a young man from a prominent family who held military and civic positions, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402910.translation: Caius Virrius Iucundus, standard-bearer of the II Cohort of Vigiles, of the century of Visertus Latinus, served for 6 years, 7 months, and 19 days, during which time he served as tesserarius, optio, and standard-bearer. He lived 27 years. He ordered this altar with its base to be set up by his will, under the supervision of Lucilia Lacaena and his son Caius Virrius Iucundus.
EDCS-20402910.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and service of Caius Virrius Iucundus, a member of the Vigiles fire brigade, who died at age 27 and directed the erection of his monument in his will, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402913.translation: To the divine shades. Quintus Largennius Chresimus, father, who for the honor of the seat (for magistrates) gave 50,000 sesterces to the public treasury of the Pisans, (erected this) for his son Quintus Largennius Severus, of the Galeria tribe, formerly aedile of Pisa.
EDCS-20402913.summary: This funerary monument honors Quintus Largennius Severus, a former aedile of Pisa, and records a significant donation of 50,000 sesterces made by his father to the city, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402917.translation: To the divine shades. Quintus Minucius Hermes, father, erected this for his most devoted son, Quintus Minucius Restitutus, a sevirus Augustalis, who lived 45 years.
EDCS-20402917.summary: This funerary monument honors Quintus Minucius Restitutus, a sevirus Augustalis (a priest of the imperial cult), and was erected by his father, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402922.translation: The living erected this to the divine shades for themselves and their descendants, those listed below: Quintus Caecilius Amandus, Augustalis, son of Quintus Caecilius, of the Galeria tribe, from Lucius; Quintus Caecilius Lucceianus; Titus Fabius Seppianus; Lucius Atilius Modestus; Sextus Scutarius Successus; Marcus Lucceius Bachylus; Lucius Lappius Receptus; Lucius Atilius Sotericus; Aulus Caecilius Eutycus; Lucius Olcius Venustus; Titus Fabius Galaesus; Lucius Castricius Carus; Marcus Modius Masculus; Fuscus Alypus; Paris; Decimius Cosmus; Cicero; Albius Ianuarius; Petronius Eucaerus; Terentius Abascantus.
EDCS-20402922.summary: This is a collective funerary inscription for a group of men, identified as 'cultores Herculis somnialis decuria I' (members of the first dream decuria of Hercules), who established this monument for themselves and their descendants, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-20402925.translation: To the divine shades. Titus Aelius Lucifer, freedman of Augustus, placed this for himself while alive.
EDCS-20402925.summary: This is a self-dedicated funerary monument for Titus Aelius Lucifer, a freedman of Emperor Augustus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402926.translation: To the divine shades. Publius Albius Athictus erected this for his well-deserving wife, Albia Ionice, and for himself.
EDCS-20402926.summary: This funerary monument was jointly dedicated by Publius Albius Athictus for his wife, Albia Ionice, and himself, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402927.translation: To the divine shades. Aulus Faesonius Theuda erected this for his most pious and deserving wife, Anneia Restituta, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-20402927.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Aulus Faesonius Theuda for his wife, Anneia Restituta, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402928.translation: To the divine shades. Antonia Restituta, who lived 26 years.
EDCS-20402928.summary: This is a simple funerary monument for Antonia Restituta, who died at the age of 26, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-20402929.translation: To Lucius Aquilius Epaphroditus, heir and husband to Flavia Magna.
EDCS-20402929.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Flavia Magna by her heir and husband, Lucius Aquilius Epaphroditus.

EDCS-20402930.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Atilia Fortunata, freedwoman of Marcus, from Ulpia Hy[---] Atilia Marcellina, dearest mother.
EDCS-20402930.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Atilia Fortunata, freedwoman of Marcus, from her mother Ulpia Hy[---] Atilia Marcellina.

EDCS-20402931.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Aufidia Victoria, a deserving wife, Publius Veturius Martialis made this, with whom he lived for 25 years, 10 months, 15 days, and 7 hours, without any complaint.
EDCS-20402931.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the details of the life shared by Publius Veturius Martialis and his wife Aufidia Victoria.

EDCS-20402932.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Marcus Aurelius Otius.
EDCS-20402932.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Marcus Aurelius Otius.

EDCS-20402933.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Quintus Caedilius Celer and Naevia Iadis.
EDCS-20402933.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Caedilius Celer and Naevia Iadis.

EDCS-20402934.translation: To Caecinia, an excellent woman, from her patron Caius Caecinius Theodorus.
EDCS-20402934.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caecinia by her patron, Caius Caecinius Theodorus.

EDCS-20402935.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Lucius Calpurnius Ibycus, freedman of Lucius, who died in his third year.
EDCS-20402935.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Calpurnius Ibycus, a child who died in his third year.

EDCS-20402936.translation: Tiberius Camidenus Nodulus, son of Tiberius, of the Galeria tribe, made this for Vibia Lychnis, freedwoman of Lucius, for Gaius Herennius, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, and for Prima, daughter of Herennia, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-20402936.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Tiberius Camidenus Nodulus for himself and other family members, including his wife Vibia Lychnis.

EDCS-20402937.translation: Of Titus Camurenius, son of Myron.
EDCS-20402937.summary: This is a dedication, possibly funerary, to Titus Camurenius, son of Myron.

EDCS-20402938.translation: Titus Cestius Philippus, freedman of Titus, and Cestia Nica, freedwoman of Titus, and Lucius Cestius Agathocles, freedman of Titus, bought a plot of immortal ground, 14 feet in front and 16 feet in the field, and built [a tomb] for themselves and their heirs and successors.
EDCS-20402938.summary: This inscription records the purchase of a burial plot and the construction of a tomb by Titus Cestius Philippus, Cestia Nica, and Lucius Cestius Agathocles, all freedmen of Titus.

EDCS-20402939.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Cipia Successa.
EDCS-20402939.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cipia Successa.

EDCS-20402940.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Caius Cominius Posidonius made this for his brother, Cominius Hermes.
EDCS-20402940.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Cominius Posidonius for his brother, Cominius Hermes.

EDCS-20402941.translation: Publius Cornelius Torquatus, son of Lucius, made this for the spirits of the departed, for Publius Cornelius Maro.
EDCS-20402941.summary: This funerary inscription records that Publius Cornelius Torquatus made a monument for Publius Cornelius Maro.

EDCS-20402942.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Fabia Melianthis, his dearest wife with whom he lived 25 years, Lucius Fabius Pergamus made this for himself also.
EDCS-20402942.summary: This funerary inscription records that Lucius Fabius Pergamus set up a monument for his wife Fabia Melianthis and himself, noting they lived together for 25 years.

EDCS-20402943.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Fania, daughter of Caius, who lived 30 years, 3 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-20402943.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Fania, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-20402944.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Felix, slave of our Caesar, from Alexandria, Marcus Ulpius Marcellus made this for his excellent and deserving master.
EDCS-20402944.summary: This funerary inscription records that Marcus Ulpius Marcellus dedicated a monument to his slave Felix.

EDCS-20402946.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Galeria Felicissima, who made this for herself and for Decia Restituta and Lucius Calpurnius Abascantus, her parents, likewise for her children, and for Volusius Saecularis, her husband, and for Calpurnius, her most excellent son, and for Nicia and Marcus, her brothers, likewise for their freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants; this monument shall not pass to an outside heir.
EDCS-20402946.summary: This funerary inscription by Galeria Felicissima records the dedication of a monument for herself, her parents, children, husband, brothers, and their descendants, stipulating it cannot pass to an outside heir.

EDCS-20402947.translation: Titia, freedwoman of Titus, [set this up for] Aulus Granius Grania, freedwoman of Titus, [and] Lucius Aebutius Restitutus.
EDCS-20402947.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Titia, a freedwoman of Titus, likely for her freedman husband Lucius Aebutius Restitutus and another freedwoman.

EDCS-20402948.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Hostilia Omphale, here rests a deserving mother.
EDCS-20402948.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and rest of Hostilia Omphale, described as a deserving mother.

EDCS-20402949.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Hostilia Zoe, here rests a deserving wife.
EDCS-20402949.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and rest of Hostilia Zoe, described as a deserving wife.

EDCS-20402950.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Sextilius Vitalis, with his own money, arranged for this monument to be erected for his well-deserving wife, Iulia Isiadis. It measures 160 feet in front and 50 feet in the ground.
EDCS-20402950.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Publius Sextilius Vitalis for his wife Iulia Isiadis.

EDCS-20402951.translation: Marcus Manlius Blastus for himself and for his well-deserving wife, Cisidia Fortunata, and for Felicitas, his beloved, who lived 17 years, 5 months, 17 days, and 4 hours. It measures 15 feet in front and 15 feet in the ground.
EDCS-20402951.summary: This tombstone was set up by Marcus Manlius Blastus for himself, his wife, and a beloved individual named Felicitas.

EDCS-20402952.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Miliasia Prima rests here, who lived 50 years, a most devoted mother.
EDCS-20402952.summary: This epitaph records the death of Miliasia Prima, described as a devoted mother.

EDCS-20402954.summary: This very brief inscription simply marks the burial place of Aulus Nonius Victorinus.

EDCS-20402957.translation: Greetings, Parthenius. May you fare well, you who greet me along with my daughter Sossia.
EDCS-20402957.summary: This is a friendly greeting addressed to someone named Parthenius, including the speaker's daughter Sossia.

EDCS-20402958.translation: For Marcus Perelius Motalis, well-deserving, erected by his brother Publius Publilius Bio, his freedman Marcus Perelius Euphemus, and his wife Flavia Arescusa.
EDCS-20402958.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the brother, freedman, and wife of the deceased Marcus Perelius Motalis.

EDCS-20402959.summary: This is an incomplete inscription that seems to identify Petronia as the wife of Pinarius Tiberi.

EDCS-20402964.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilius Dius erected this for his well-deserving wife, Sallustia Homilia, who was also called Caecilia, and who lived 35 years.
EDCS-20402964.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Caecilius Dius for his wife, Sallustia Homilia (also known as Caecilia).

EDCS-20402965.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Tampius Hermeros erected this for his dearest wife, Scribonia Hedone, with whom he lived 18 years without complaint, and vowing that after her he would have no other wife.
EDCS-20402965.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quintus Tampius Hermeros for his wife Scribonia Hedone, expressing his devotion and vow of lifelong fidelity.

EDCS-20402966.translation: Sextus Suetonius Philodamus, freedman of Sextus, erected this while alive for his freedwoman Suetonia Zophrona, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-20402966.summary: This is a funerary dedication made during his lifetime by Sextus Suetonius Philodamus for his freedwoman Suetonia Zophrona and their descendants.

EDCS-20402967.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of Publius Suillius.

EDCS-20402968.translation: His father for his most dutiful sons, Marcus Valerius Domitius and Domitia.
EDCS-20402968.summary: This dedication by a father is for his sons, Marcus Valerius Domitius and Domitia.

EDCS-20402969.translation: To the Divine Shades. Callippus made this for his sweetest son, Marcus Valerius Glyco, who lived for 6 years, 11 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-20402969.summary: This epitaph records the death of Marcus Valerius Glyco at the age of 6 years, 11 months, and 10 days, set up by his father Callippus.

EDCS-20402970.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Flavius Zosimus made this for his well-deserving wife, Valeria Hedone, consecrated.
EDCS-20402970.summary: This epitaph records Titus Flavius Zosimus' dedication to his wife, Valeria Hedone.

EDCS-20402972.translation: Venuleia Pyralla made this while alive for her daughter Restituta, and for herself and her family.
EDCS-20402972.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Venuleia Pyralla for her daughter Restituta and herself.

EDCS-20402973.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Vettius Zosimus made this for his well-deserving companion, Chrestinus.
EDCS-20402973.summary: This epitaph records Lucius Vettius Zosimus' dedication to his companion, Chrestinus.

EDCS-20402976.translation: To the Divine Shades. Visidia Festa, daughter of Lucius, of incomparable life, farewell, and you too.
EDCS-20402976.summary: This epitaph honors Visidia Festa, daughter of Lucius, with a farewell message.

EDCS-20402977.translation: To the Divine Shades. Vitellia Diodota.
EDCS-20402977.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Vitellia Diodota.

EDCS-20402978.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cale and Mater Myrtilus, father Tata, and Cale, mother, lived for 16 years, 9 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-20402978.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of a person whose parents were Cale and Mater Myrtilus, with father Tata and mother Cale, who lived for 16 years, 9 months, and 8 days.

EDCS-20402981.translation: To the Divine Shades. Elata, daughter of [---].
EDCS-20402981.summary: This epitaph, though heavily damaged, is dedicated to Elata, daughter of [---].

EDCS-20402985.translation: Here rests in peace Palladius, a most distinguished man, who lived 50 years and was buried on the fifth day before the Ides of January, in the ninth indiction, after the consulship of Lampadius and Horestes, most distinguished men consuls.
EDCS-20402985.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Palladius, a distinguished man, dating to a period after the consulship of Lampadius and Horestes.

EDCS-20402986.translation: Cirra, who lived 46 years, 5 months, and 13 days, was buried on the day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-20402986.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cirra, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-20402988.translation: His son Caecina Placidus set this up for Aulus Caecina Quadratus.
EDCS-20402988.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Caecina Placidus to Aulus Caecina Quadratus.

EDCS-20402991.translation: Primisinia Severina, of good reputation and faithful, who lived 67 years, 3 months, and 5 days. Her most dutiful son, Fulvius Macer Primus, set this up for his mother, who deserved well.
EDCS-20402991.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primisinia Severina, set up by her son, recording her age and praising her character.

EDCS-20402995.translation: Benedictus, who lived 80 years, 6 months, and 5 days. His sweet wife and sons made this for his good memory.
EDCS-20402995.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benedictus, set up by his wife and sons, recording his age.

EDCS-20402997.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Domitius Caricus made this for his brother and patron, Quintus Domitius Cascellius Crescenti, who deserved well.
EDCS-20402997.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Domitius Caricus to his brother and patron, Quintus Domitius Cascellius Crescenti.

EDCS-20402998.translation: Quintus Titus Anquirinni set this up in accordance with the will for Sextus Anquirinnus, son of Lucius, of the Galeria tribe, of the 19th Legion.
EDCS-20402998.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Anquirinnus, son of Lucius, of the 19th Legion, set up by Quintus Titus Anquirinni as per his will.

EDCS-20403000.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caesilius Mercurialis, for his most holy and chaste wife Procula, daughter of Lucius, with whom he lived 26 years and 30 days, on behalf of himself and his son Caesilius Proculianus.
EDCS-20403000.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gabinia Procula, dedicated by her husband Caesilius Mercurialis and son, recording their marital duration.

EDCS-20403002.translation: For Thalia Coclia. For Lucius Peregrinus, decurion of the 13th Legion, decurion of Pisis, quaestor to the treasury. By her heirs.
EDCS-20403002.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Thalia Coclia and Lucius Peregrinus, who held military and administrative positions, likely set up by heirs.

EDCS-20403004.translation: For Lucius Papirius Mandatus, freedman of Lucius Papirius, a *clupeolarius*? an Augustalis of Pisis and Luca. For Lucius Papirius Apellus, his patron.
EDCS-20403004.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Papirius Mandatus, a freedman and *clupeolarius* (or similar), and possibly for his patron Lucius Papirius Apellus, related to Pisis and Luca.

EDCS-20403006.translation: Of the worshippers of Mars: 50 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-20403006.summary: This is a boundary inscription, likely marking land dedicated to the god Mars.

EDCS-20403007.translation: To Sextus Afranius Burranus, who lived 35 years and 49 days. Afrania Musa, his mother, made this for her son.
EDCS-20403007.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403010.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lucius Dentrius Lygdamus, who lived 7 years.
EDCS-20403010.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Lucius Dentrius Lygdamus.

EDCS-20403013.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For my most sweet and most holy wife, Pamphila.
EDCS-20403013.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to a wife named Pamphila by her husband.

EDCS-20403014.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Vibius Felix, Gaius Vibius Bota, Gaius Vibius Iustus, Vibia Daphne, and Vibia Pia made this for their well-deserving brother, Gaius Vibius Vitalis. R.
EDCS-20403014.summary: A funerary monument erected by siblings for their brother, Gaius Vibius Vitalis.

EDCS-20403015.translation: Gaius Villius Maternus, son of Gaius, and Gaius Villius Aper, freedman of Gaius, and Villia Phasis, who was Rubellia Procula, [made this] to Gaius Villius Inventus, their father and patron, most excellent, to the Spirits of the Underworld, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-20403015.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a family and freedmen to their father and patron, Gaius Villius Inventus, with a dedication authorized by local magistrates.

EDCS-20403016.translation: In this holy place, here rests in peace Antoninus, who lived 65 years. He was buried on the day before the Kalends of May, again, after the consulship of the most illustrious man Paulinus the Younger, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-20403016.summary: A funerary epitaph providing details of the burial date and the deceased's age, referencing specific consuls and an indiction cycle for dating, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-20403017.translation: For Lucius Baebius, son of Publius, of the Velina tribe, a baker, four-man official in charge of justice.
EDCS-20403017.summary: An inscription honoring Lucius Baebius, a baker and local magistrate.

EDCS-20403018.translation: Lucius Venonnius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, made this while alive for himself and for Vennonia Phil-, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-20403018.summary: A tombstone erected by Lucius Venonnius for himself and his freedwoman Vennonia Phil-.

EDCS-20403020.translation: To Lady Isis Taposiris. Gaius Gargennius Maximus, veteran, son of Spurius, on behalf of his brother Marcus Gargennius Macrinus, veteran, son of Spurius, of the Scaptia tribe.
EDCS-20403020.summary: A dedication to the goddess Isis Taposiris, made by a veteran on behalf of his brother, also a veteran.

EDCS-20403024.translation: Aulus Faltennius, son of Caius, of the Scaptia tribe, sexvir, and Ladinnia Tertia, daughter of Aulus, his wife.
EDCS-20403024.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Faltennius and his wife Ladinnia Tertia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403025.translation: To Severinus, colleague of the guild of builders of Faesulae.
EDCS-20403025.summary: This is a dedication to Severinus, a member of the guild of builders in Faesulae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403026.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Lucius Terentius Fidus and his comrade Novicia, by the guild of the crossroads shrine.
EDCS-20403026.summary: This is a funerary dedication by the crossroads shrine guild for Lucius Terentius Fidus and his comrade Novicia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403027.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caius Titallius Ursus, a living sexvir and dendrophorus, erected this for himself and for his deserving wife Marcia Etrusca.
EDCS-20403027.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Titallius Ursus for himself and his wife Marcia Etrusca, who held religious offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403030.translation: For Remnia Primigenia, the garland-maker, 6 feet in front and 6 feet in the rear.
EDCS-20403030.summary: This is a boundary marker or land grant inscription for Remnia Primigenia, specifying land dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403031.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Lucius Tettius Crescentis, devotees of Saturn.
EDCS-20403031.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Tettius Crescentis by his fellow devotees of Saturn, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403032.translation: To the Divine Manes. Eutychus erected this for his most beloved wife Fortunata, who deserved well.
EDCS-20403032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Eutychus for his deserving wife Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403033.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Marcus Murrius Ianuaris.
EDCS-20403033.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication for Marcus Murrius Ianuaris, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403034.translation: Utilis, freedman of Petronia, gives this cippus from his own property to Flaminia, freedwoman of Asia.
EDCS-20403034.summary: This is a property transfer inscription recording the gift of a cippus by the freedman Utilis to the freedwoman Flaminia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403035.translation: To the Divine Manes. Publius erected this for his most sweet son Publius Faustininus.
EDCS-20403035.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Publius for his son Publius Faustininus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20403036.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Lucius Terentius Hilarus, Lucius Terentius Corinthus for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-20403036.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Terentius Corinthus to his brother Lucius Terentius Hilarus.

EDCS-20403037.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Lucius Tettius Primitivus, Lucius Tettius Onesimus for his foster son.
EDCS-20403037.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Tettius Onesimus to his foster son Lucius Tettius Primitivus.

EDCS-20403039.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Tettia, freedwoman of Lucius, Tigris, a pious and simple soul. Quintus Publicius Fuscus for his well-deserving wife. The last duties of fate I set up for you, my wife; I attest this duty ought to have been yours. I beg you, whoever you are, do not be offended to say 'May the earth be light upon her.'
EDCS-20403039.summary: This funerary inscription is a heartfelt epitaph by Quintus Publicius Fuscus for his wife Tettia Tigridis, expressing grief and a plea for passersby to wish her peace.

EDCS-20403040.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Tigris, daughter of Crescentis, for her most beloved husband and daughter Salutaria. She lived 5 years, 2 months, 19 days. For her who deserved well.
EDCS-20403040.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tigris, recording her lifespan and mentioning her husband and daughter.

EDCS-20403041.summary: This is a simple funerary record for Thannia, daughter of Ali, stating her age at death.

EDCS-20403042.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Gaius Tullius Justus, Gaius Vettius Crysogonus for his most excellent brother, who deserved well.
EDCS-20403042.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Vettius Crysogonus to his brother Gaius Tullius Justus.

EDCS-20403043.translation: To the Divine Spirits: To Marcus Valerius Fortunatus, Marcus Valerius Sabinus for his pious son, who deserved well. He lived 26 years, 3 months, 8 days.
EDCS-20403043.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Valerius Sabinus for his son Marcus Valerius Fortunatus, recording his age at death.

EDCS-20403052.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication to a deity named Felicitas (Happiness) by a parent, or possibly a dedication for a parent to Felicitas.

EDCS-20403059.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Lucius Paccius Leo, possibly a funerary dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-20403069.translation: Tunni Iovis: Gaius Ceuna Iustus willingly paid a vow of 10 pounds of silver.
EDCS-20403069.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Gaius Ceuna Iustus fulfilling a vow to Jupiter (Iovis) by donating 10 pounds of silver.

EDCS-20403072.translation: Quintus Aurelius Scaptia Rufus, son of Quintus, a speculator, lived for 42 years and served for 19 years; he is buried here; his heirs [left this].
EDCS-20403072.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Aurelius Scaptia Rufus, a speculator, stating his age and years of service.

EDCS-20403074.translation: Lucius Pedanius Macer, son of Caius, a veteran of the 11th legion, erected this by his will.
EDCS-20403074.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by will for Lucius Pedanius Macer, a veteran of the 11th legion.

EDCS-20403076.translation: To Quintus Septimius Primus, son of Quintus, of the Scaptia tribe, who was prefect of craftsmen, aedile, duovir, and pontifex; this funerary plot and place of burial was publicly granted to him as a gift.
EDCS-20403076.summary: This is a public dedication of a burial plot and place of sepulture to Quintus Septimius Primus, an official who held several civic and religious offices.

EDCS-20403080.translation: Atilia Severa for herself and for her husband Lucius Sattius Creticus, a sexvir and master of the Augustales.
EDCS-20403080.summary: This is an epitaph set up by Atilia Severa for herself and her husband, Lucius Sattius Creticus, who held positions related to the imperial cult.

EDCS-20403081.translation: To Caspia Tertulla, flaminica of Augusta, aged [3]..., and [---]VA[---] who placed [this] for Arminia Brocca, grandmother, and Marcia Caspia Rogatina. Probus willingly dedicated this altar.
EDCS-20403081.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to several women, including Caspia Tertulla and Marcia Caspia Rogatina, possibly by Probus.

EDCS-20403082.translation: To Festus, master of the Augustales, and Etruscus. O Eupholis...
EDCS-20403082.summary: This inscription fragment appears to be a dedication to Festus, a master of the Augustales, and possibly to someone named Etruscus and Eupholis.

EDCS-20403083.translation: To Flavius Probus, son, aged 24, and Lucius Flavius Fuscus, son, aged 23. According to a decree of the decurions, with their wealth, in front 70 feet, in the field 90 feet.
EDCS-20403083.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a plot of land granted by decree of the decurions to the sons of someone, Flavius Probus and Lucius Flavius Fuscus.

EDCS-20403084.translation: Publius Fontinius Priamus, freedman of Publius, a sexvir [---]; Fontinia Heraclea, freedwoman of Publius [---]
EDCS-20403084.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Publius Fontinius Priamus, a sexvir, and Fontinia Heraclea, possibly his relative or wife.

EDCS-20403085.translation: Made during his lifetime for Gaius Gellius Etruscus, son of Gaius, of the Scaptia tribe, decurion, Florentinus.
EDCS-20403085.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a living person for Gaius Gellius Etruscus, a decurion.

EDCS-20403086.translation: Caius Murrius Eucharistus made this, during his lifetime, for his patron, Caius Murrius, aedile, duovir, and pontifex, keeper of sacred rites, well-deserving.
EDCS-20403086.summary: This is a dedication made by a freedman, Caius Murrius Eucharistus, for his patron, Caius Murrius, who held several important civic and religious offices.

EDCS-20403087.translation: To Gaius Poblicius Mahetus, freedman of Gaius, a municipal councilor and magistrate of the Augustales. Decimia Pneuma, freedwoman of Marcus, his wife, [erected this].
EDCS-20403087.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Poblicius Mahetus, erected by his wife, which mentions his public roles as a member of the Augustales and a magistrate.

EDCS-20403088.translation: To Aulus Raventius Severus, a decurion. Aulus Raventius Ursio, a decurion.
EDCS-20403088.summary: This is an epitaph recording two individuals, Aulus Raventius Severus and Aulus Raventius Ursio, both holding the position of decurion, likely from the same family.

EDCS-20403089.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gaius Saenius Diadumenus, a fellow freedman, and Sergia Hypora erected this at their own expense to Gaius Saenius Euhemerus, freedman of Gaius, a decurion, who deserved well.
EDCS-20403089.summary: This funerary monument was erected by freedmen for Gaius Saenius Euhemerus, a decurion, commemorating their relationship and his good character.

EDCS-20403090.translation: To Nerutus, freedman. Marcus Titius Martialis and Marcus Titius Pyramus, brothers and decurions, for themselves and their wives Calpurnia Myrtale and Titia Saturnina and their mother's sister? Apustia Romana, this monument will not follow the heir, and for Percennia Iunice, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-20403090.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription detailing the dedicants (brothers and decurions), the beneficiaries (wives and a relative), and a legal clause regarding inheritance, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403091.translation: For themselves and for Valeria IIImia, daughter of Irmius, and for Valerius Felix, their comrade, a decurion.
EDCS-20403091.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument for a group of individuals, including a couple and a decurion, likely for funerary purposes.

EDCS-20403093.translation: To Gaius Umbricius Canso, son of Gaius, from the Scaptia tribe, enrolled as a colonist by decree of the Florentine decurions, for himself and his wife Volturnia Tertulla, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-20403093.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Umbricius Canso, a colonist admitted by the decurions of Florence, and his wife, establishing their burial plot.

EDCS-20403094.translation: [...]TA[---] / [---]misi L[---] Pupilla [---] / [---] for the Augustales a feast and for the urban plebs for each person.
EDCS-20403094.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record a donation or bequest for a public feast for the Augustales and the urban plebs, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-20403095.translation: To Gnaeus Tullius Aeso, freedman of Gnaeus, a physician, 14 feet in front, 14 feet in width.
EDCS-20403095.summary: This is a boundary stone inscription for a property owned by Gnaeus Tullius Aeso, a freedman and physician, indicating the dimensions of his land.

EDCS-20403097.translation: To the slave Eutyches, manager of the common business, an agent of Sextus Avidius Eutyches, a retailer. [...]ami, to his deserving wife.
EDCS-20403097.summary: This funerary inscription is for a slave named Eutyches who managed business affairs for a retailer, Sextus Avidius Eutyches, and also commemorates his wife.

EDCS-20403099.translation: To the Divine Shades. Eutyches made this for Ampliata, his deserving wife, with whom he lived for one year and three months.
EDCS-20403099.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ampliata, erected by her husband Eutyches, recording their marital relationship and its duration.

EDCS-20403100.translation: To the divine shades. Caius Aninius Eutyches for his deserving brother Quintus Aninius Martialis, for his bones and ashes.
EDCS-20403100.summary: A funerary dedication for a deserving brother, Quintus Aninius Martialis, by his sibling Caius Aninius Eutyches.

EDCS-20403118.translation: Antestia M<x=S>milla, daughter of Caius, for herself and for her husband Quintus Varronius Pamphilus, and for Quintus Varronius Serranus, son of Quintus, and Gemellus, and for Varronia, daughter of Quintus, and her husband Lucius Popilius, son of Quintus, and for their grandsons Lucius Popilius Celer, son of Lucius, and Caius Popilius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-20403118.summary: A funerary dedication for multiple family members including Antestia Ma<x=S>milla, her husband, children, and grandchildren.

EDCS-20403119.translation: Anthidus, slave of Lucius Annaeus Blastus, lived 10 years, 9 months, 12 days.
EDCS-20403119.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Anthidus, a slave of Lucius Annaeus Blastus.

EDCS-20403120.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly recording names of individuals, likely of the Attius family.

EDCS-20403122.translation: To the divine shades. Aelius Secundinus for his deserving mother Baebia Trepta.
EDCS-20403122.summary: A funerary dedication for a deserving mother, Baebia Trepta, by her son Aelius Secundinus.

EDCS-20403123.translation: Cafatia Faustilla, freedwoman of Caius, lived 25 years. 10 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-20403123.summary: A funerary epitaph for the freedwoman Cafatia Faustilla, also specifying the dimensions of her burial plot.

EDCS-20403124.translation: To the divine shades. Apusulena Romana made this for her excellent and deserving husband Quintus Cascellius Mercurialis.
EDCS-20403124.summary: A funerary dedication for an excellent and deserving husband, Quintus Cascellius Mercurialis, by his wife Apusulena Romana.

EDCS-20403125.translation: 14 feet in front, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-20403125.summary: An inscription specifying the dimensions of a plot, likely for a tomb or boundary marker.

EDCS-20500022.translation: Titus Aemilius Trophimus, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-20500022.summary: An epitaph identifying Titus Aemilius Trophimus as the freedman of Titus.

EDCS-20700405.translation: In the consulship of Emperor Caesar Augustus for the 13th time and Marcus Plautius Silvanus. Lucius Scribonius Diogenes, freedman of Libo. To Silvanus.
EDCS-20700405.summary: A dedication dated by consuls, possibly an official inscription or a private dedication by Lucius Scribonius Diogenes to Silvanus.

EDCS-20700415.translation: By decree, the council and citizens of Lunensium, having been relieved by immortal benefits, have erected a statue for posterity to Lucilius Constantus, praeses of Mauretania and Tingitania, clarissimus vir, consular of Tuscia and Umbria, and Lidius Favonius Aemilius Papus Minor Celsus.
EDCS-20700415.summary: This is a public monument erected by the citizens of Lunensium to honor Lucilius Constantus for his benefits.

EDCS-20700430.translation: The decurions and coloni of Lunensium gave the honor of Augustalis gratis for the first time to [L(ucius?)] Tettius Demosthenes.
EDCS-20700430.summary: This inscription records the gratuitous bestowal of the Augustalis honor by the local authorities and citizens of Lunensium upon Tettius Demosthenes.

EDCS-20700467.translation: To the divine shades: Lucius Cassidarius Ingenuus made this for his most dutiful mother, Lucilia Ianuaria.
EDCS-20700467.summary: A private funerary monument dedicated by Lucius Cassidarius Ingenuus to his mother, Lucilia Ianuaria.

EDCS-20700470.summary: A very brief epitaph or identification marker for Titus Petronius, son of Titus.

EDCS-20700473.translation: Spendusa set this up for Saturninus, who deserved well.
EDCS-20700473.summary: A dedication by Spendusa to Saturninus, honoring him for his merits.

EDCS-20700485.summary: A fragmentary inscription with illegible names and numbers, likely part of a list or dedication.

EDCS-20700487.translation: To the good memory, in this holy place rests in peace Amandiana, an honorable woman, who lived more or less [number] years, buried on the day before the Kalends of October, after the consulship of Mavortius.
EDCS-20700487.summary: A Christian funerary inscription for Amandiana, specifying her honorable status, approximate age, and burial date relative to a consulship.

EDCS-20700488.translation: The deposition of holy Eutherius, powerful and life-giving, whose holy bones lie here, the people also in peace before C---
EDCS-20700488.summary: A Christian inscription relating to the burial of holy Eutherius, mentioning his venerable remains and the peace of the people.

EDCS-20700490.translation: --- was the father of the apostle
EDCS-20700490.summary: A very fragmented inscription, possibly related to Christian genealogy or hagiography.

EDCS-20700491.translation: --- and of the decurions. Constans, Augustalis, by decree of the decurions, thanks from his own money.
EDCS-20700491.summary: An inscription indicating that Constans, an Augustalis, funded something by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-20700492.translation: To the departed spirits. Hail, Nympha, Achelous, and Heorte, my dearest daughters! You who stand here and look upon my monument, see how unfairly my life was taken! I died in my sixth year, while my parents still lived. Do not grieve for us, parents; it was necessary to die; fate willed it. Just as unripe fruit hangs on a tree, so our bodies fall, either ripe or soon to be snatched away unripe. I implore you, stone, rest lightly upon the bones, lest you be heavy for this tender age. Farewell.
EDCS-20700492.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman period, laments the premature death of two young daughters, Nympha and Heorte, and offers philosophical reflections on mortality.

EDCS-20700493.translation: To the departed spirits. Ascle, the heir, made this for Gaius Mussius Quietus, his deserving kinsman.
EDCS-20700493.summary: This tombstone records a dedication by an heir to a deserving kinsman, Gaius Mussius Quietus.

EDCS-20700494.translation: Valeria Camilla made this for herself while alive, to the departed spirits. To the deserving Valeria Camilla, to the departed spirits. To the deserving Valeria Camilla, to the departed spirits.
EDCS-20700494.summary: This inscription records that Valeria Camilla commissioned her own tombstone during her lifetime.

EDCS-20800230.translation: To Publius Statius Caltichus, the doctor. Statius Alexander [made this] for his student and parent.
EDCS-20800230.summary: This dedication was made by Statius Alexander for his student and surrogate parent, the doctor Publius Statius Caltichus.

EDCS-20800233.translation: To Marcus, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, from Mutina, father. Marcia, freedwoman of Caius, mother. Caius Marcius Pamphilus, freedman of Caius, [made this]. Matteia, wife.
EDCS-20800233.summary: This epitaph lists family members including a father, mother, and son, indicating a familial burial plot.

EDCS-20800235.translation: Sextus Gabinius and Vestricia made this while alive.
EDCS-20800235.summary: This inscription records that Sextus Gabinius and Vestricia commissioned their tombstone during their lifetime.

EDCS-20800237.translation: Priccius, son of Publius, Pilargurus, made this while alive for his wife. Aufidia, freedwoman of Caius, [is] the wife.

EDCS-21000272.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a freedwoman named Calidon by her owner Fortunata, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-21000275.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Verus, a slave of Pacinus Aper, placed this for his friend Hilarius, a well-deserving freedman, on his own behalf and that of his wife Crementalis, out of memory and loyalty.
EDCS-21000275.summary: This funerary dedication was set up by Verus, a slave, for his friend Hilarius, a freedman, commemorating their loyalty and friendship.

EDCS-21000277.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Parents for their daughter Iulia Iusta, who lived 14 years and [some number of] months, a well-deserving [daughter].
EDCS-21000277.summary: This is a funerary inscription by parents for their daughter Iulia Iusta, who died at the age of 14, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-21000278.translation: [This is for] Iusta, daughter of [---]tenius, [---] of the Senate.
EDCS-21000278.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely for a woman named Iusta, possibly connected to senatorial rank, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000280.translation: To [---] and Lollia Maximilla, his wife, for [her] well-deserving [husband/relative].
EDCS-21000280.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to a man by his wife Lollia Maximilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000281.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Munatius the father made this for his most dutiful daughter Munatia Festa.
EDCS-21000281.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a father for his daughter Munatia Festa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000282.translation: Of Aulus Muttius Calvo, 8 feet in front.
EDCS-21000282.summary: This inscription likely refers to the dimensions of a tomb or plot belonging to Aulus Muttius Calvo, possibly dating to the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-21000283.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying ownership or a tomb belonging to Aulus Muttius Calvo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000285.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Caius Norbanus Novus, his freedman, made this for Norbana Rufilla.
EDCS-21000285.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Caius Norbanus Novus, a freedman, for Norbana Rufilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000291.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Titus Statilius Magnus made this, and had it made, for his dearest brother Titus Statilius Maximus.
EDCS-21000291.summary: This funerary inscription was erected by Titus Statilius Magnus for his brother Titus Statilius Maximus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000292.translation: The daughters made this for their well-deserving mother, Niae Successae.
EDCS-21000292.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by daughters for their mother.

EDCS-21000293.summary: This inscription identifies Titia, daughter of Aulus, likely on a tombstone or other marker.

EDCS-21000294.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Trophimus made this for his most beloved and well-deserving sister, Caecilia.
EDCS-21000294.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Trophimus to his sister Caecilia.

EDCS-21000295.translation: To Titus Tullius Ianuarius, son of Tullius, of the tribe Voltinia.
EDCS-21000295.summary: This inscription likely records the name and tribal affiliation of Titus Tullius Ianuarius, possibly on a tomb or public record.

EDCS-21000296.translation: Of Aulus Veianius, son of Aulus, of the tribe Saturninus.
EDCS-21000296.summary: This inscription provides the full name and tribal affiliation of Aulus Veianius Saturninus.

EDCS-21000298.translation: For Vibiae Tertia, daughter of Lucius, from the tribe Pomptina; for Aulus Caesius, son of Caius.
EDCS-21000298.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Vibiae Tertia and Aulus Caesius.

EDCS-21000299.translation: To the spirits. Caius Voconius Urbanus for his most dutiful mother, Voconia Primitiva.
EDCS-21000299.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Caius Voconius Urbanus for his mother, Voconia Primitiva.

EDCS-21000300.translation: Volunseia, freedwoman of Maria, Tyche, lived 32 years.
EDCS-21000300.summary: This inscription records the name, status, and age at death of a freedwoman named Tyche.

EDCS-21000306.summary: This inscription indicates that Felicitas dedicated or placed a monument.

EDCS-21000313.translation: A traveler who marveled at the laws was here; if you wish to know what happened, read my inscription; a girl fell from on high and returned life to fate; here I rest without pain, delivered to eternal reading. Felicissimae, her daughter. Lucius Caesennius Magnus, father.
EDCS-21000313.summary: This epitaph, set up by Lucius Caesennius Magnus for his daughter Felicissima, describes her death from a fall and her peaceful rest.

EDCS-21000322.translation: To the good memory of Vincentius, an innocent neophyte, who lived 12 years, 4 months, and 7 days, buried the day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-21000322.summary: This inscription is a tombstone commemorating a young boy named Vincentius who died in the early Christian period.

EDCS-21000323.translation: Urse, may you live in God.
EDCS-21000323.summary: This is a short epitaph, likely Christian, wishing a person named Urse eternal life.

EDCS-21000327.translation: Liberalis, freedman of Quadratus and Larcia, fulfilled the vow of his patrons.
EDCS-21000327.summary: This inscription records a freedman fulfilling a vow on behalf of his patrons, Larcia and Quadratus.

EDCS-21000328.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Achilleus, the actor, who deserved well.
EDCS-21000328.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Achilleus, identified as an actor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000329.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Appius Restitutus, from the college.
EDCS-21000329.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a college (guild or association) to Appius Restitutus.

EDCS-21000330.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Valeria Philoteti, Marcus Valerius [set this up].
EDCS-21000330.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Valerius for Valeria Philoteti.

EDCS-21000334.translation: For Lucius Cocceius Primus, freedman of Lucius, and Accepta, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-21000334.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Cocceius Primus and Accepta, both freedpersons of a Lucius, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-21000335.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Gabinia Vitellia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-21000335.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gabinia Vitellia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-21000336.translation: Lucius Anicius Saturinus, son of Lucius, lived 30 years.
EDCS-21000336.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Lucius Anicius Saturinus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-21000337.translation: Sextus Sextilius Corno, son of Cnaeus, lived 11 years.
EDCS-21000337.summary: This inscription records the lifespan of Sextus Sextilius Corno, son of Cnaeus.

EDCS-21000338.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph naming Posilla Herennia.

EDCS-21000339.translation: Gaius Petilius Gallo lived for 53 years.
EDCS-21000339.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gaius Petilius Gallo.

EDCS-21000340.translation: Gaius Pituanius, son of Sabinianus, lived for 7 years.
EDCS-21000340.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Gaius Pituanius, son of Sabinianus.

EDCS-21000341.translation: Lucius Titius Sulo, son of Lucius, lived for 72 years.
EDCS-21000341.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Titius Sulo, son of Lucius.

EDCS-21000342.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Scribo.

EDCS-21000343.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-21000344.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Marcus Valerius, with the exact age missing.

EDCS-21000345.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Marcus Valerius.

EDCS-21000350.translation: Sextus Venuleius, son of Sextus, aged 56 years.
EDCS-21000350.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Sextus Venuleius, son of Sextus.

EDCS-21000375.translation: Sextus Culcius Matho, freedman of Sextus. Alpionia Felicula, freedwoman of a woman. Herennia Faventina, freedwoman of Gaius. Gaius Varius Primus, freedman of Vena.
EDCS-21000375.summary: This inscription lists the names and freedman/freedwoman status of several individuals, likely from a tomb or public dedication.

EDCS-21000380.summary: This is a dedication to an unnamed, exceptionally esteemed individual from Ferentino, likely honoring their civic virtues or achievements.

EDCS-21000387.translation: perished Gaius Pomponius; perished Herma the left-handed; released Gaius Sallustius; released Bucolus; Apelles; won Pierus; released Gaius Iu[lianus?].
EDCS-21000387.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of participants in a competition or contest, noting those who perished, were released, or won, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-21000388.translation: [---] XX; [---] in number VII; [---] in number II; [---]utus in number I; [---]archia in number [---]; Gaius Junius in number [---]; Vitali[s?]; Lyc[---].
EDCS-21000388.summary: This inscription seems to list individuals or items with associated numerical counts, possibly a record of inventory, census, or participants in an event, with dating uncertain due to fragmentation.

EDCS-21000389.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a victory or achievement, possibly related to a competition or a personal accomplishment, with names and context largely lost.

EDCS-21000391.summary: This very fragmented inscription mentions the name Verus, possibly alongside a word related to virtue, hinting at a personal epitaph or dedication, but lacking sufficient context for dating.

EDCS-21000415.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcus Annius Magnus.
EDCS-21000415.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Annius Magnus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000416.translation: Diodorus made [this] for his dearest son, who lived 1 year and 15 days.
EDCS-21000416.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Diodorus for his young son, who died at the age of one year and fifteen days, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000417.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or name inscription for Arronia Fortunata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000418.translation: Lucius Cincius Diomedes, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-21000418.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Cincius Diomedes as the freedman of a certain Lucius, likely a funerary or ownership marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000425.translation: To the departed spirits, Etusius Justus [dedicated this] to his most sweet daughter Etusia Iustina, who lived 4 years, 10 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-21000425.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Etusius Justus for his young daughter Etusia Iustina, who died at the age of four years, ten months, and nine days, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000426.translation: Publius Fabricius, son of Publius, lived 79 years.
EDCS-21000426.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Fabricius.

EDCS-21000436.translation: To Sabinia Lucilla Rufina, dearest daughter, who lived 14 years and 4 months. Her parents, grieving, made this for her and her husband, with 2 months remaining in the year.
EDCS-21000436.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by grieving parents for their daughter Sabinia Lucilla Rufina and her husband, likely from the early Imperial period given the style.

EDCS-21000445.translation: Quintus Atilius Postumus, son of Quintus, of the Stellatina tribe, who lived 48 years, concerning the administration of justice.
EDCS-21000445.summary: This epitaph commemorates Quintus Atilius Postumus, who lived 48 years and was involved in judicial administration, possibly as a magistrate.

EDCS-21000446.translation: To Glitilleia Primigenia, freedwoman of Quintus, a deserving wife, he made this for her and himself while alive.
EDCS-21000446.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a husband for his deceased wife, Glitilleia Primigenia, and for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-21000448.translation: Quintus Plotidius Acer, freedman of Quintus; Attia Tertia, freedwoman of Caius; Quintus Plotidius, freedman of Quintus; Quintus Plotidius, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-21000448.summary: This inscription lists the names of several freedmen and potentially their patrons, likely part of a funerary monument or a record of property ownership.

EDCS-21000451.translation: Gaius Varius Hermes dedicated this to Sanctus Soranus Apollo for his own health, and that of his son, and his patron, and his wife, and her children.
EDCS-21000451.summary: This is a religious dedication made by Gaius Varius Hermes to Apollo for the health of himself, his family, his patron, and his children.

EDCS-21000464.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Aulus Popillius Placidus, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, from Signia, who lived 41 years, 4 months, and 6 days. Calpurnia Ianuaria to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-21000464.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Calpurnia Ianuaria to her husband Aulus Popillius Placidus, providing his lifespan and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-21000469.translation: Marcus Spurilius, son of Caius, twice quaestor, duovir.
EDCS-21000469.summary: This is a titulus honorarius listing the career of Marcus Spurilius, a Roman magistrate who held the offices of quaestor and duovir.

EDCS-21000470.translation: Gaius Spurilius, son of Marcus, member of the board of four, quaestor.
EDCS-21000470.summary: This inscription records the cursus honorum of Gaius Spurilius, a Roman official who served as a quaestor and a member of the board of four.

EDCS-21000473.translation: Gaius Egnatius, son of Sextus, oversaw the construction of meadows.
EDCS-21000473.summary: This inscription records the civic responsibility of Gaius Egnatius, who oversaw the construction or maintenance of meadows.

EDCS-21000483.translation: Opia Calitenes, daughter of Arontis, wife of Cesies Lartio.
EDCS-21000483.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Opia Calitenes and her familial connections.

EDCS-21000485.translation: Cavio Nomesina, of Maxomo, and Zervatronia.
EDCS-21000485.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple identification of individuals, likely funerary, given the context of other inscriptions.

EDCS-21000486.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Caia Vipi and her father.

EDCS-21000488.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Statio Aco and his mother.

EDCS-21000489.translation: Marcus Meronius, son of Aulus, and Flavolea, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-21000489.summary: This inscription identifies two individuals, Marcus Meronius and Flavolea, by their patronymics, possibly for funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-21000493.translation: Marcus Aconius Tautil, son of Ceilia.
EDCS-21000493.summary: This inscription is a funerary epitaph identifying Marcus Aconius Tautil and his mother.

EDCS-21000500.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed: Aurelia Chreste, Claudia Eutychis, and their own freedmen and their descendants.
EDCS-21000500.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial space to the deceased spirits and specifying the beneficiaries, likely set up by Aurelia Chreste and Claudia Eutychis.

EDCS-21000501.translation: Lucius Fulcinius, son of Publius, of the Sergia tribe; Quintus Fulcinius, son of Publius, of the Sergia tribe; Fulcinia M. For Publius Fulcinius, Roman knight, alive.
EDCS-21000501.summary: This inscription lists multiple members of the Fulcinius family, including a Roman knight, and likely pertains to a funerary monument or property ownership.

EDCS-21000503.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aulus Maianius Ianuarius made [this] while alive for himself and for his dearest wife Acilia Tyche and for their descendants.
EDCS-21000503.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Aulus Maianius Ianuarius, while alive, dedicated a burial to himself, his wife Acilia Tyche, and their descendants.

EDCS-21000510.summary: This inscription is a dedication or commemoration honoring two individuals named Agatho and Agati, identified as presbyters.

EDCS-21000511.translation: Virginia, his wife, made this for her most beloved Felisius, who lived more or less 45 years, 6 months, and 32 days, and was buried on the day of Jupiter after the fifth day before the Kalends of June, in the second hour of the evening.
EDCS-21000511.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felisius, set up by his wife Virginia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000512.translation: His most devoted sons made this for Marcus Aurelius Propinquus, a most distinguished man, their father, who by the hard work of military service and by his industry deservedly achieved eminent glory and increased family wealth.
EDCS-21000512.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Propinquus, erected by his sons, commending his distinguished career and family success, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000513.translation: For Publius Tettius Certus, scribe and bookkeeper of the plebeian aediles, who lived 97 years. Publius Tettius Conveniens made this for himself and his family. In front, 12 feet.
EDCS-21000513.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Tettius Certus, a scribe and bookkeeper for the plebeian aediles, erected by Publius Tettius Conveniens, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000514.translation: For Iulia Calicles, and for her freedmen, and for the freedmen of Alypius, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-21000514.summary: This inscription records ownership or dedication of property or a tomb for Iulia Calicles and her freedmen, as well as those of Alypius, a freedman of Augustus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000515.translation: Antigonus, freedman of Lucius Iulius Mercator, son of Lucius.
EDCS-21000515.summary: This is a simple identification of an individual, Antigonus, a freedman of Lucius Iulius Mercator, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000516.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Minia Betuellia Procula, who lived 10 years, 5 months, and 6 days. Her most devoted parents, Betucllius Proculus and Ellhia Prima, made this for their sweetest daughter.
EDCS-21000516.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Minia Betuellia Procula, erected by her parents, Betucllius Proculus and Ellhia Prima, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000517.translation: Gaius Minucius Urbicus, son of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe; Marcus Valerius Trypho, son of Aristonichus, of Athens; Minucia ChrHeste, mother.
EDCS-21000517.summary: This inscription lists three individuals: Gaius Minucius Urbicus, Marcus Valerius Trypho, and Minucia ChrHeste, possibly family members or associated with a tomb, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000521.translation: For Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix, son of Lucius, the dictator.
EDCS-21000521.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial for Lucius Cornelius Sulla Felix, son of the famous dictator Sulla, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-21000523.translation: From the will of Licinius, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-21000523.summary: This inscription indicates something was established or given according to the will of Licinius, son of Tiberius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21000536.translation: To the holy guardian Silvanus, Lucius Pomponius Romanus.
EDCS-21000536.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Silvanus by Lucius Pomponius Romanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21100433.translation: Licinia Venusta, daughter of Faustus, made this.
EDCS-21100433.summary: This is a dedication by Licinia Venusta, likely for herself or another.

EDCS-21100439.translation: Rutilia, daughter of Aruntis, from Olenum, lived 50 years.
EDCS-21100439.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Rutilia.

EDCS-21100442.translation: Publius Kamerius, son of Caius, lived 42 years.
EDCS-21100442.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Publius Kamerius.

EDCS-21100443.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Publius Ceneius, with the age missing.

EDCS-21100444.translation: Secunda, daughter of Gavia, lived 7 years.
EDCS-21100444.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Secunda.

EDCS-21100445.translation: Numerius Herennius, son of Lucius, lived 15 years.
EDCS-21100445.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Numerius Herennius.

EDCS-21100446.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Nice, mother, for her dearest son Publius Lucilius Auctus, son of Publius, who lived 10 years, 10 months, and 28 days.
EDCS-21100446.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her young son, providing detailed age at death.

EDCS-21100447.translation: Navitta, son of Marcius, lived 4 years.

EDCS-21100449.translation: Caius Quintius Iucundus, freedman of Caius, lived 27 years.
EDCS-21100449.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age at death of Caius Quintius Iucundus.

EDCS-21100450.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Salvia Hortensi.

EDCS-21100451.translation: Lucius State, son of Lucius, lived 60 years.
EDCS-21100451.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and lifespan of Lucius State.

EDCS-21100452.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and lifespan of Tidioclia.

EDCS-21100453.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Caius Balerius.

EDCS-21100459.translation: Here rests Restutus, in peace, a praiseworthy boy who lived about ten years, was buried on the third day before the Nones of October, four years after the consulship of the most distinguished man Basilius, in the ninth indiction. Here rests Iusta, in peace, who lived about 75 years, was buried on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of August, after the consulship of the most distinguished man Basilius, in the sixteenth year, in the fifth indiction.
EDCS-21100459.summary: A complex funerary inscription recording the burials and lifespans of two individuals, Restutus and Iusta, with detailed chronological information based on consulships and indictions.

EDCS-21100461.translation: Here rests Vincomalus, buried on the sixth day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-21100461.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial date of Vincomalus.

EDCS-21100462.summary: A dedication inscription, possibly from a tomb, indicating that Nelianus and Nelius Cornelianus were the makers or dedicators.

EDCS-21100464.translation: Lucius Sempronius and Memmia, to their children Sempronia and Lucius Sempronius.
EDCS-21100464.summary: A dedication inscription, likely from a family tomb, by Lucius Sempronius and Memmia to their children.

EDCS-21100470.summary: This is a personal name inscription identifying Marcus Faltinius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-21100618.translation: To the divine Manes. His freedman, Aprilis, made this for Gaius Velcaeus Actius, his patron, who deserved well.

EDCS-21100656.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Junius Callistus for his daughter, Junia Balbilla.

EDCS-21100657.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Priscus's Primigenia, a deservedly beloved wife, who lived 20 years, 3 months, and 5 days.

EDCS-22000001.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tiberius Claudius Attalus, the brother of Epinicus, intended for the underworld spirits.

EDCS-22000002.translation: Made by the living Lucius Cornificius Magnus, son of Lucius, for himself, and for Praesidia Vitalis, daughter of Caius, his wife, and for Saenia Sextia, daughter of Caius; 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the field.

EDCS-22000004.summary: This inscription is a fragment of a dedication, possibly funerary, mentioning Epaphroditus and his daughter Aeta.

EDCS-22000005.translation: Made by the living, to the spirits of the underworld: for Euphrosynus, companion of Zosimenus, well-deserving.
EDCS-22000005.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Euphrosynus for his well-deserving companion, Zosimenus, addressed to the underworld spirits.

EDCS-22000006.translation: ...son of Lucius; Folnia Secunda, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-22000006.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording family relationships, possibly a funerary monument, mentioning a son of Lucius and Folnia Secunda.

EDCS-22000008.translation: CV E Iucunda, 4th daughter, 10 feet in front, in the field...
EDCS-22000008.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary marker or property record, identifying Iucunda and specifying plot dimensions.
