EDCS-22000010.translation: Upon the death of Lucius Lusianus Bassus, by Lucius Lusianus Hymetus while alive, and by Lusiana Cailis, freedwoman of Lucius, while alive.
EDCS-22000010.summary: This funerary inscription records the establishment of a burial plot by Lucius Lusianus Hymetus and Lusiana Cailis for Lucius Lusianus Bassus, likely a family member.

EDCS-22000011.translation: The boundary of Maius, 10 feet in length and 10 feet in width.
EDCS-22000011.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Maius.

EDCS-22000012.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Mamilia Adiecta made this for her deserving husband, Titus Mamilio Castus.
EDCS-22000012.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deserving husband, dating likely to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22000014.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aulus Naevius Marcellinus made this for his most excellent father, Aulus Naevius Saturninus, who was buried before this monument.
EDCS-22000014.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a son for his father, indicating the deceased was buried prior to the monument's erection.

EDCS-22000017.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Petronius Trophimus for his most devoted wife, Tettia Tyche.
EDCS-22000017.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband for his devoted wife.

EDCS-22000018.translation: Gaius Pontius Naso, son of Gaius, of the Scaptia tribe, Iunianus Paulinus, lived 41 years.
EDCS-22000018.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, tribal affiliation, and lifespan of Gaius Pontius Naso Iunianus Paulinus.

EDCS-22000019.translation: Valerius lived 25 years. Proculus made this for his brother Antaeus, son of Marcus Proculus, who lived 27 years.
EDCS-22000019.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Proculus for his brother Antaeus, including their ages at death.

EDCS-22000020.translation: Of Proculus and Priscus, 50 feet in the front and 30 feet in the land.
EDCS-22000020.summary: This inscription likely records the dimensions of a property or tomb belonging to Proculus and Priscus.

EDCS-22000021.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Dionysius made this for his deserving wife, Rusticania Felicula, who lived 17 years, 7 months, and 14 days.
EDCS-22000021.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, detailing her age at death with remarkable precision.

EDCS-22000022.translation: Lucius Saena Saturninus, son, made this for his father Quintus Saena Celer, son of Lucius, and for his brother Quintus Saena Clemens, son of Lucius, and for his aunt Cramponia Maxima, daughter of Aulus, wife of Nan, of the Scaptia tribe. In the front 12 feet, in the land 12 feet.
EDCS-22000022.summary: A funerary monument set up by Lucius Saena Saturninus for his father, brother, and aunt, also recording the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-22000023.translation: To Lucius Scribonius, son of Lucius, called Scirna, aged 28, 10 feet in front and 10 feet on the frontage in the field.
EDCS-22000023.summary: This is a boundary marker or a funerary inscription for Lucius Scribonius, noting his age and dimensions of his plot, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000025.translation: To Sentilius Modestus, from Sentilia Asterope, for her most devoted brother.
EDCS-22000025.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Sentilia Asterope to her brother Sentilius Modestus, indicating a strong familial bond, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000026.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Taminia Sabina, from Amantinius Maximus, for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-22000026.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Amantinius Maximus for his wife Taminia Sabina, expressing his devotion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000027.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, for Tertulla Albricia, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000029.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Trebonia, Pious daughter of Quintus, a well-deserving wife, Quintus Fabius Paternus made this.
EDCS-22000029.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by Quintus Fabius Paternus for his wife Trebonia, praising her virtues, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000030.translation: Valeria made [this] for [her mother? A relation?] well-deserving.
EDCS-22000030.summary: This inscription, though partially illegible, appears to be a funerary dedication by Valeria for a respected female relative, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000031.translation: Varena Arescusa, freedwoman of Publius, for herself and for Philadis, freedwoman of Lucius, 10 feet in front and 12 feet in the field.
EDCS-22000031.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot belonging to two freedwomen, Varena Arescusa and Philadis, specifying dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000039.translation: Here lies Makaria, daughter of Ioannes, from the village of Nikeratai. She lived three years, three months, and ten days. She died faithful on the 22nd of Xandikos, under the consulship of Honorius Augustus for the 1st time and Constantius for the 2nd time.
EDCS-22000039.summary: This is a Greek funerary inscription for Makaria, recording her parentage, village, lifespan, death date, and consular dating to the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-22000041.translation: To a good memory. Here rests in peace Aquilia Paulina, a praiseworthy woman, who lived more or less 60 years, buried on the 7th day before the Kalends of October, under the consulship of the most illustrious men Isodorus and Senator.
EDCS-22000041.summary: This is a Latin funerary inscription for Aquilia Paulina, providing her age, burial date, and consular dating to the 5th century CE.

EDCS-22000042.translation: To a good memory. Here rests in peace Anastasius Galata, who lived 58 years, 6 months, and 20 days, he was buried in peace on the 16th day before the Kalends of May, again after the consulship of Paulinus Iunior, the most illustrious man, a consul.
EDCS-22000042.summary: This Latin funerary inscription for Anastasius Galata records his lifespan, burial date, and a specific dating reference to the post-consulship of Paulinus Iunior, likely in the 5th century CE.

EDCS-22000043.translation: Macrobis, primicerius of the first cohort of Theodosian troops, who lived about fifty years, is laid to rest here in peace, on the sixth day after the Ides of May, in the tenth indiction, following the consulship of the most distinguished Basilius the Younger.
EDCS-22000043.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Macrobis, a primicerius, dated by consul and indiction.

EDCS-22000044.translation: Aquilia Valentina, who lived about 53 years and 58 days, is laid to rest here in peace, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-22000044.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aquilia Valentina, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000045.translation: Here lies Cartaco, of good memory, who lived 22 years; her husband Erpa placed this monument for his sweetest wife; she is laid to rest.
EDCS-22000045.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cartaco, set up by her husband, recording her age.

EDCS-22000046.translation: Aquilius Constantius, of good memory, who lived 37 years, is laid to rest here in peace on the fifth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-22000046.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aquilius Constantius, recording his age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000047.translation: Constia, of good memory, who lived 12 years, is laid to rest here in peace on the day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-22000047.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Constia, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000048.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Crispi Consta, recording his age.

EDCS-22000049.translation: Decianus, servant of God, of good memory, who lived 55 years, is laid to rest here in peace, and was laid to rest on the sixth day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-22000049.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Decianus, a servant of God, recording his age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000050.translation: Flavius Romulianus, an infant, of good memory, who lived 6 years and 7 months, and his siblings, Verus, who lived 10 years, and Romanus, who lived 5 years, and Augustula, 3 and a half years, who were placed in various cemeteries, in peace.
EDCS-22000050.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Romulianus and his siblings, recording their ages.

EDCS-22000051.translation: Flavia Martina, a girl, of good memory, who lived 6 years and 9 months, is laid to rest here in peace, on the ninth day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-22000051.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Martina, recording her age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000053.translation: Florentius, a boy, of good memory, who lived about 10 years, is laid to rest here in peace, on the eighth day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-22000053.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Florentius, recording his approximate age and date of burial.

EDCS-22000054.translation: In good memory, Fundanius Iovianus, a lector, lies here, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 20 days, laid to rest in peace on the day before the Nones of January.
EDCS-22000054.summary: This epitaph records the death of Fundanius Iovianus, a lector, who died at the age of 17 years, 9 months, and 20 days, and was buried on January 4th.

EDCS-22000055.translation: In good memory, Florentius Numisius, a deacon, who lived about 55 years, laid to rest in peace on the 5th day before the Ides of October.
EDCS-22000055.summary: This epitaph records the death of Florentius Numisius, a deacon, who lived approximately 55 years, and was buried on October 11th.

EDCS-22000056.translation: In good memory, Maria rests here, who lived one year, [blank] months, laid to rest two [illegible characters].
EDCS-22000056.summary: This epitaph records the death of Maria, who lived for one year and an unspecified number of months, with the rest of the text illegible.

EDCS-22000057.translation: Here Maximinus, a most distinguished man, a tribune, rests in peace, laid to rest on the 15th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-22000057.summary: This epitaph records the death of Maximinus, a distinguished man and tribune, who was buried on May 18th.

EDCS-22000058.translation: Here lies Mundilo the elder, of the schola gentilium, who lived about 40 years.
EDCS-22000058.summary: This epitaph records the death of Mundilo the elder, a member of the schola gentilium, who lived approximately 40 years.

EDCS-22000059.translation: In good memory, Pompeius Lupicinus, a lector, lies here, who lived 5 years and 5 days.
EDCS-22000059.summary: This epitaph records the death of Pompeius Lupicinus, a lector, who died at the age of 5 years and 5 days.

EDCS-22000060.translation: In good memory, Potisius Ianuarius, who lived [blank] years.
EDCS-22000060.summary: This epitaph records the death of Potisius Ianuarius, with the duration of his life unspecified.

EDCS-22000061.translation: In good memory, Segetius of the schola gentilium lies here, who lived thirty-eight years, laid to rest on the sixth day before the Ides of February in the [blank] indiction.
EDCS-22000061.summary: This epitaph records the death of Segetius, a member of the schola gentilium, who lived 38 years and was buried on February 8th, during an unspecified indiction.

EDCS-22000074.translation: Here rests in peace Curredia Iunia, an honorable girl, who lived 9 years and 5 days, laid to rest on [blank] day.
EDCS-22000074.summary: This epitaph records the death of Curredia Iunia, an honorable girl, who lived 9 years and 5 days, with the date of her burial unspecified.

EDCS-22000076.translation: Here rests Felicitas, who lived [blank] months.
EDCS-22000076.summary: This epitaph records the death of Felicitas, with the duration of her life unspecified.

EDCS-22000079.translation: To the good memory of Fadia Verianena, dearest daughter, who lived for [years]
EDCS-22000079.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a daughter named Fadia Verianena, who died at an unspecified age.

EDCS-22000080.translation: To the good memory of Prastinia Maximina, an actress of consular rank, who was joined to her husband for sixteen years, and who also possessed a husband for 16 years, she left behind three sons, through
EDCS-22000080.summary: This funerary inscription honors Prastinia Maximina, an actress of consular rank, noting her marriage duration and number of children, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-22000081.translation: Flavius Faustinianus, her most devoted husband and domestic official, had this monument made for his most loving wife, Usi imui, a citizen of Alamanna, who lived 34 years, departed in peace on the 4th day before the Nones of December, during the consulship of Marinianus and Asclipiodotus.
EDCS-22000081.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Usi imui, a 34-year-old Alamannian citizen, in December during the consulship of Marinianus and Asclipiodotus, and was erected by her devoted husband.

EDCS-22000082.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Nonia Phenusa made this for her well-deserving father, Publius Nonius Eupales of the Tromentina tribe.
EDCS-22000082.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Nonia Phenusa for her father, Publius Nonius Eupales, a member of the Tromentina tribe.

EDCS-22000083.translation: Tiberius Iulius Rho, procurator, lived for 10 years.
EDCS-22000083.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Iulius Rho, a procurator, who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-22000087.translation: Sacred to Bellona. Donax, freedman of Augustus, a surveyor, gave this gift.
EDCS-22000087.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Bellona by Donax, a freedman of the emperor and a surveyor.

EDCS-22000090.translation: For Pupienia Cethegilla, most illustrious girl. Pupienus Eutychianus and Pupienus Philumenus, her foster parents.
EDCS-22000090.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the foster parents, Pupienus Eutychianus and Pupienus Philumenus, for the young girl Pupienia Cethegilla.

EDCS-22000093.translation: From Lucius Cacina [---] from the V [---] battle lines. Lucius Volasen[na ---]
EDCS-22000093.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records military service or honors for Lucius Cacina, with a partial mention of Lucius Volasenna.

EDCS-22000094.translation: To Gaius Caesilius, son of Sextus, a four-man official for dispensing justice, for the second time, who lived 60 years.
EDCS-22000094.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Gaius Caesilius, son of Sextus, who served twice as a four-man official responsible for justice and lived to be 60.

EDCS-22000096.translation: Gaius Cilnius, son of Caius Varus, four-man official.
EDCS-22000096.summary: This inscription records the name and official position (IIII vir) of Gaius Cilnius Varus.

EDCS-22000097.translation: To Aulus Novius Plicontus, freedman of Aulus, a sevirus Augustalis, by his associates.
EDCS-22000097.summary: This inscription honors Aulus Novius Plicontus, a sevirus Augustalis, as indicated by his associates.

EDCS-22000098.summary: This inscription records the name of Perperna, who served as an aedile.

EDCS-22000099.translation: Quintus Poena Aper, a member of the IV viri aedilis, had this constructed at his own expense.
EDCS-22000099.summary: This inscription states that Quintus Poena Aper, holding the office of IV vir aedilis, funded the construction of the monument.

EDCS-22000100.translation: Caius Traulus Phoebus, freedman of Caius, a seviral Augustalis, lived 37 years; Pergonia Prima.
EDCS-22000100.summary: This inscription is a funerary notice for Caius Traulus Phoebus, a seviral Augustalis, who lived 37 years, with Pergonia Prima also mentioned.

EDCS-22000101.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Urbicus, public steward, by decree of the council, having had many benefits from him, he managed the quaestorship for 44 years without a single stain.
EDCS-22000101.summary: This funerary inscription honors Urbicus, a public steward, who served the quaestorship for 44 years with distinction, as decreed by the council.

EDCS-22000102.translation: Aedile, IV vir iure dicundo, pontifex, quinquennalis, first by decree of the decurions in honor of Perpernia n.
EDCS-22000102.summary: This inscription records a monument dedicated by decree of the decurions in honor of Perpernia, mentioning various offices held by the dedicator, including aedile and pontifex.

EDCS-22000103.translation: Of Domitia Phillis, wife of Caius Domitius Lemnus, procurator of Germanicus Caesar.
EDCS-22000103.summary: This inscription commemorates Domitia Phillis, wife of Caius Domitius Lemnus, who was the procurator of Germanicus Caesar.

EDCS-22000104.summary: This inscription identifies Caius Manneius Coranus as an archimimus, or chief mime.

EDCS-22000105.translation: Agatinia, daughter of Lucius, aged 4 years.
EDCS-22000105.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Agatinia, daughter of Lucius, likely a funerary epitaph.

EDCS-22000107.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Lucius Antonius Lupus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-22000107.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Lucius Antonius Lupus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22000108.translation: Quintus Aulinna, son of Sextus, of the Sabatina tribe.
EDCS-22000108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Quintus Aulinna, son of Sextus, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22000109.translation: To the Divine Manes. Baebi Novianus and Secundinus (dedicate this) to Lucius Baebius Aurelianus, their father; and Aurelius Maximus to his brother; and Vibia Profutura to her most dear and deserving husband.
EDCS-22000109.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by family members to the deceased Lucius Baebius Aurelianus, his brother, and his wife.

EDCS-22000110.translation: To Sextus Caecina, from the will.
EDCS-22000110.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Sextus Caecina, made according to his will.

EDCS-22000111.translation: Caius Caecina Baro, freedman of Caius, lived 38 years.
EDCS-22000111.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Caecina Baro, a freedman.

EDCS-22000112.translation: Caius Caecina Caspo, son of Quintus, lived 20 years.
EDCS-22000112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Caecina Caspo, son of Quintus.

EDCS-22000113.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Aulus Caecina Cesaula.

EDCS-22000114.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Aulus Caecina Selcia.

EDCS-22000116.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Lucius Caecina Nicephor is buried here.

EDCS-22000117.translation: His father made this monument for Aulus Caecina Superstes, son of Aulus, orphaned after his birth, to whom he might entrust his father's bones after death, having lived twenty-one years...
EDCS-22000117.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a father for his son, Aulus Caecina Superstes, who died young and to whom the father intended to entrust his own remains.

EDCS-22000118.translation: Caecinia Prima, daughter of Lucius, lived 13 years. Pomponia, mother (dedicates this) to her daughter.
EDCS-22000118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Pomponia to her daughter, Caecinia Prima, recording her age at death.

EDCS-22000119.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Heroidis, freedwoman of Calpurnia Lucia.
EDCS-22000119.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Heroidis, a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000120.translation: Gaius Caspo, son of Mani, aged 22.
EDCS-22000120.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Gaius Caspo, likely a tombstone from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000121.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Castica Victorina, his dearest and most longed-for wife, Casticus Cocceianus, his deserving wife.
EDCS-22000121.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a husband to his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000122.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cerficius Severius, Cerficia Severina, Cerficius Severinus, to their deserving father, and Velinia Artemidora, his deserving wife.
EDCS-22000122.summary: This is a funerary dedication from children and a wife to their deceased family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000123.translation: Cimarulina made this for Onesimus, who deserved well.
EDCS-22000123.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Cimarulina for Onesimus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000125.translation: Troilus for his dearest freedman. Fecunda for her dearest freedman. Volus Severinus for his brother. Caecinia Capria for her brother. Volus Zoilus for his brother, lived 33 years.
EDCS-22000125.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of several individuals, possibly family members and freedmen, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000126.translation: Lived 7 years, 2 months, 23 days. Quietus and Quieta, parents.
EDCS-22000126.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Festa, recording her age and identifying her parents, Quietus and Quieta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000127.translation: Flavia, daughter of Caius, aged 3 years.
EDCS-22000127.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Flavia, the daughter of Caius, likely a tombstone from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000128.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Iaronia Verecunda, most dutiful mother, from her sons Ursus, Aper, and Lupus, her deserving mother. Lived 41 years.
EDCS-22000128.summary: This is a funerary dedication from sons to their mother, Iaronia Verecunda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000129.translation: Marcianus made this for his well-deserving sister Iuventa and his wife Festiva.
EDCS-22000129.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Marcianus for his sister Iuventa and his wife Festiva, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22000130.summary: This is an epitaph for two individuals named Sextus Laberius, likely father and son.

EDCS-22000131.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Murtius Verinus, a cruel father, inscribed this monument for his daughters Murtia Verina and Murtia Floriana, who deserved well of him. Verina received 10,000 sesterces, lived 12 years, 5 months. Floriana received 12,000 sesterces, lived 8 years, 3 months. The innocent ones received from their father what they owed him.
EDCS-22000131.summary: This funerary inscription records the posthumous endowment and epitaph set up by Murtius Verinus for his two young daughters, Murtia Verina and Murtia Floriana, detailing their ages and sums of money left to them.

EDCS-22000132.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Novius Pantherus, and for Novia Veneris, his deserving wife, and for Novius Honoratus, his deserving father.
EDCS-22000132.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Lucius Novius Pantherus, his wife Novia Veneris, and his father Novius Honoratus.

EDCS-22000133.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the name and age of Papiria, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-22000134.translation: Pedanius, son of Publius, [and his] daughter Tertia Scaeva.
EDCS-22000134.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of Pedanius, son of Publius, and his daughter Tertia Scaeva, likely on a shared monument.

EDCS-22000135.translation: Aulus Persius Severus, son of Aulus, lived 8 years, 3 months, 19 days.
EDCS-22000135.summary: This epitaph records the name and very young age of Aulus Persius Severus.

EDCS-22000136.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Vergilia Saturnina. Aulus Persius Severus [erected this] to his excellent wife.
EDCS-22000136.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Aulus Persius Severus to his 'excellent wife', Vergilia Saturnina.

EDCS-22000138.translation: To Petronia Hetaera. Traulus Quadratus [erected this] to his excellent wife.
EDCS-22000138.summary: This funerary inscription records Traulus Quadratus dedicating a monument to his 'excellent wife', Petronia Hetaera.

EDCS-22000139.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Plagallus Maximius. Laucumnia Felicitas [erected this] to her deserving husband.
EDCS-22000139.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Laucumnia Felicitas to her 'deserving husband', Plagallus Maximius.

EDCS-22000140.translation: To Ixtia Procula. Volasenus Iustus [erected this] to his wife. She lived 25 years.
EDCS-22000140.summary: This funerary inscription records Volasenus Iustus dedicating a monument to his wife, Ixtia Procula, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-22000141.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vettius Iulianus to his well-deserving wife Publicia Marcella, and Vettius Marcellus to his most dutiful mother. She lived 23 years, 3 months, 15 days.
EDCS-22000141.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publicia Marcella, set up by her husband and son, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000142.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vettius Iustus, his son, and Volca Ianuarius and Volcia Maritima set up this monument to the well-deserving Vettius Iulius.
EDCS-22000142.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vettius Iulius, set up by his son and two others, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000143.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Here lies Quintus Spurius Firminus, once a youth blessed with outstanding virtue, distinguished in age, birth, and honors, whom his mother's devotion preserves and the goddess herself protects; the love of his brother made him a sharer [in this monument?] and took away his mother's grief, so that his family and equal glory may always remain. To the Spirits of the Underworld. Grapthus, freedman, [dedicated this] from a vow for the preservation of his daughter, the well-deserving Squaetinia Maxima.
EDCS-22000143.summary: A complex funerary epitaph for Quintus Spurius Firminus and Squaetinia Maxima, set up by the freedman Grapthus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000144.translation: Lucius Vettius Philonicus, freedman of Lucius, aged 45 years.
EDCS-22000144.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Vettius Philonicus, a freedman, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000145.translation: To the well-deserving Lupus [and] Lupa Ianuaria, Cornelianus Verus [dedicated this] to Volasenna [their patron?].
EDCS-22000145.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Volasenna by Lupus and Lupa Ianuaria, possibly her freedmen or clients, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000146.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Volasenna Novianus to his most dutiful mother, Volasennia Pyramidia.
EDCS-22000146.summary: A funerary epitaph for Volasennia Pyramidia, set up by her son, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000152.translation: To Macrothymia, my incomparable, inestimable, most beloved, most chaste, most holy, only wife, impeccable and irreproachable, who lived with me without deceit, without fraud for 20 years, 6 months, 15 days, whom an accursed day and dark fate snatched away, submerging her unmerited [death] before her time. To my well-deserving wife, Aquilinus bearing witness, I have erected this monument for her and for our parents, with whom it is my vow to dwell in eternal peace.
EDCS-22000152.summary: A deeply personal funerary epitaph for Macrothymia, set up by her grieving husband Aquilinus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000153.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Caius Victricius Memor, one of the six priests of Augustus, erected this.
EDCS-22000153.summary: A dedication to the god Silvanus by Caius Victricius Memor, a member of the Augustales college, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000156.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Laelius Epagathus and Crescens, freedmen, to their well-deserving patron Lucius Laelius Valens, son of Lucius, veteran. He lived 39 years, 6 months.
EDCS-22000156.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Laelius Valens, a veteran, set up by his freedmen, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000159.translation: Lucius Arrius Restitutus, son of Lucius, lived eight years.
EDCS-22000159.summary: A tombstone for a young boy named Lucius Arrius Restitutus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22000160.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Vicceius Crescens, son of Lucius Vicceius Quirina, lived 18 years. Lucius Vicceius Crescens, his father, set this up.
EDCS-22000160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his deceased son, Lucius Vicceius Crescens, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-22000161.translation: His sons set this up for Marcus Fonteius Balbus, son of Caius, of the Sabatina tribe, and for Tertia, wife of Titus Quintus, by their father's will.
EDCS-22000161.summary: This epitaph records the dedication of a monument by sons for their father, Marcus Fonteius Balbus, and his wife Tertia, as stipulated in their father's will.

EDCS-22000162.translation: Gaius Gavius Tuscus, son of Aulus, of the Fabia tribe.
EDCS-22000162.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Gaius Gavius Tuscus, son of Aulus, and mentioning his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22000163.translation: Manlius Primio, freedman of a woman, 7 years old. Manlia Prisca, 6 years old.
EDCS-22000163.summary: This inscription records the names and ages of two young children, Manlius Primio and Manlia Prisca, likely a funerary monument for them.

EDCS-22000165.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Publilia Marcella, who lived 37 years. Marcell [erected this].
EDCS-22000165.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Publilia Marcella, who died at the age of 37, likely erected by a relative named Marcell.

EDCS-22000172.translation: Sacred to the divine genius. Julius Silvanus, a veteran.
EDCS-22000172.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the divine genius by Julius Silvanus, identified as a veteran.

EDCS-22000173.translation: To the unconquered, holy, healthy god Prunicianus, from Myron, his slave.
EDCS-22000173.summary: This is a dedication to a god, identified as Prunicianus, made by his slave Myron.

EDCS-22000174.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Liber by Lucius Cas Carpi.

EDCS-22000176.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicating something to Lucius Caesar, who held the office of pontifex maximus.

EDCS-22000179.translation: Manius Valerius Maximus, son of Volusius, was appointed dictator before holding any magistracy; he was dictator, triumphed over the Sabines and Medullines, led the plebeians down from the Sacred Mount, reconciled the people with the fathers through a grave favor, and the Senate freed the people from this affair through his advocacy; the place of the curule seat was granted to him and his descendants for the purpose of watching from the Murcia. He was elected princeps in senatum once.
EDCS-22000179.summary: This is a lengthy political and military biography of Manius Valerius Maximus, detailing his early appointment as dictator, military victories, and role in reconciling the plebeians and patricians, along with honors granted to him and his descendants.

EDCS-22000182.translation: Lucius Aemilius Paullus, son of Lucius, twice consul, censor, interrex, praetor, curule aedile, quaestor, military tribune for the third time, augur. After conquering the Ligurians in his first consulship, he triumphed. As consul for the second time, in order to wage war against the king in person, he was made commander of the forces and destroyed the king's army in ten days after reaching Macedonia. He captured the king with his children.
EDCS-22000182.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary or commemorative inscription for Lucius Aemilius Paullus, detailing his distinguished military and political career.

EDCS-22000183.translation: Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, son of Publius.
EDCS-22000183.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely for Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, listing his name and filiation.

EDCS-22000184.translation: Lucius Licinius Lucullus, son of Lucius, consul, praetor, curule aedile, quaestor, military tribune, augur. He triumphed over King Mithridates of Pontus and King Tigranes of Armenia, after defeating the armies of both kings in several battles on land and sea. He rescued his colleague, who had been defeated by King Mithridates, after he had withdrawn to Calchedon, from siege.
EDCS-22000184.summary: This inscription commemorates the military achievements of Lucius Licinius Lucullus, detailing his triumphs over Mithridates VI of Pontus and Tigranes the Great of Armenia.

EDCS-22000188.translation: To Lucius Petronius Taurus Volusianus, son of Lucius, of the Sabatine tribe, a man of consular rank, ordinary consul, prefect of the praetorium, an most eminent man, prefect of the vigiles, a most perfect man, tribune of the first Praetorian cohort, protector of our Emperors, also tribune of the fourth Praetorian cohort, tribune of the eleventh urban cohort, tribune of the third cohort of vigiles, legionary of the 14th Gemina legion and the 10th legion in the province of Upper Pannonia, also prefect of the Dacia legions, commander of the singular cavalry of our Emperors, primus pilus of the 30th Ulpian legion, centurion appointed with public horse from the five decuries of the Laurēntēs Lavīnātēs. The town council of Arretium, to their excellent patron.
EDCS-22000188.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Petronius Taurus Volusianus, listing his extensive military and administrative career, and his honorary title as patron by the people of Arretium.

EDCS-22000196.translation: To Publius Helvius, of Arretium, Apollinaris, sexvir.
EDCS-22000196.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Helvius Apollinaris, identifying his tribal affiliation and his position as a sexvir.

EDCS-22000197.translation: Aulus Paccius, son of Aulus, and Quintus Gavius, son of Lucius, duoviri, by decree of the decurions, saw to the building of the bridge.

EDCS-22000198.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicated to Gaius Rufus, who held the office of aedile.

EDCS-22000199.translation: To Quintus Spurinna Quintianus, son of Quintus, of the Pomptine tribe, belonging to the equestrian order of the Laurēntēs Lavīnātēs, aedilicius duovir, curator of the calendar of the plebs of Arretium, curator of the public affairs of the Vetulonians. The urban plebs, by decree of the decurions, granted this place.
EDCS-22000199.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quintus Spurinna Quintianus, detailing his various public offices and honors granted by the plebs of Arretium and Vetulonia.

EDCS-22000205.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication to Lucius Avillius Proculus.

EDCS-22000211.translation: Marcus Cincius Clemens, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, lives for himself.

EDCS-22000213.translation: To Cluvia Quartina, daughter of Marcus, wife of Asellionis. The women of the village, with money collected.

EDCS-22000719.translation: Aulus Halinus, son of Aulus, veteran, served in the 5th Praetorian cohort for 21 years, deceased. Quintus Pomponius Severus [erected this].

EDCS-22000730.translation: To Publius Volumnius, son of Publius, called Violentus, four times magistrate, twice magistrate, by the fellow citizens and residents, from their own funds.

EDCS-22100739.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Sabinius, identified by his father Lucius.

EDCS-22100740.translation: To the Divine Shades. Saboni Saenianus and Iustus, sons of Aulus Sabonius Caerellianus, and Iusta.
EDCS-22100740.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Aulus Sabonius Caerellianus by his sons and possibly wife.

EDCS-22100741.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Quintus Saenius Servilianus.
EDCS-22100741.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Saenius Servilianus.

EDCS-22100743.translation: Lucius Scaevius Laevinus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensian tribe.
EDCS-22100743.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Scaevius Laevinus, identified by his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22100744.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Hastia Scandilia.

EDCS-22100746.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph listing multiple names, possibly of a family or individuals.

EDCS-22100747.translation: Q. Scr[...], A. Scr[...], C. Vet[...], vacatio[...], and vend[...
EDCS-22100747.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record names and possibly terms related to land or property.

EDCS-22100749.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Senia, identified by her father Lucius.

EDCS-22100750.translation: Quintus Sentius, son of Lucius, born of Arria.
EDCS-22100750.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Sentius, identified by his father Lucius and mother Arria.

EDCS-22100751.summary: This inscription records the name of a person, Gaius Sentius Alchus Clepatras, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-22100752.summary: This inscription records the name of a person, Clepatra Teoas, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-22100754.translation: Lucius Sentius Iustus, son of Lucius, born in the Modiensis tribe
EDCS-22100754.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Sentius Iustus, likely for a census or legal record.

EDCS-22100756.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Sentius Phoebus, possibly on a monument or gift.

EDCS-22100757.translation: Lucius Sentius Sabinius Blaesus, son of Lucius, of the Aemilian tribe
EDCS-22100757.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Lucius Sentius Sabinius Blaesus, likely for a census or legal record.

EDCS-22100759.summary: This inscription records the name of Telesphorus, a freedman of Lucius Sentius, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-22100761.translation: Senti Vilinal and Sentia, daughter of Sextus
EDCS-22100761.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, Senti Vilinal and Sentia, daughter of Sextus, possibly on a shared monument.

EDCS-22100764.summary: This inscription records the name of Persis, a freedwoman of Lucius, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-22100765.summary: This inscription records the name of Sentia Thannia, daughter of Aulus, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-22100766.translation: Lucius Sertorius Longus, son of Lucius
EDCS-22100766.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Sertorius Longus, son of Lucius, likely for a census or legal record.

EDCS-22100768.translation: Gaius Sertorius (owns land) 11 feet in front and 9 feet in the field, for himself and his family.
EDCS-22100768.summary: This is a boundary inscription specifying land dimensions owned by Gaius Sertorius.

EDCS-22100770.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Hastia Sethrnei and her father.

EDCS-22100772.translation: To the departed spirits of Silia Felicissima, Silius Romanus (erected this) for his deserving wife.
EDCS-22100772.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Silius Romanus for his wife, Silia Felicissima.

EDCS-22100774.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Tavia Sudernia and her father.

EDCS-22100775.translation: Thania Sudernia, daughter of Aruns, daughter of Tania Sadnal.
EDCS-22100775.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Thania Sudernia and her parentage.

EDCS-22100778.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Aruns as a freedman of Publius Tifile.

EDCS-22100779.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Dana and her father.

EDCS-22100780.translation: il Tite, born to Larisus II and Cainus.
EDCS-22100780.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying il Tite and his parentage, possibly with a name corruption.

EDCS-22100781.translation: Gaius Titius, son of Lucius, of the Mamilia tribe.
EDCS-22100781.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Gaius Titius with his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22100782.translation: Lucius Titius, son of Gaius Aberra.
EDCS-22100782.summary: This is a personal inscription identifying Lucius Titius with his father.

EDCS-22100783.translation: Lucius Titius Etruscus, son of Titus.
EDCS-22100783.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker.

EDCS-22100784.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker.

EDCS-22100785.translation: Aulus Titius Scaeva, son of Aulus, son of Titus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-22100785.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker, indicating familial and freedman relationships.

EDCS-22100787.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker, indicating familial relationships.

EDCS-22100790.summary: This inscription appears to record non-Roman names, possibly from a person of foreign origin or a unique local naming convention.

EDCS-22100791.translation: AO TREPI OAMASA Arunsis Trebi Histro.
EDCS-22100791.summary: This inscription records personal names, possibly with Etruscan or Italic linguistic elements, likely from a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22100796.translation: Lucius Trebonius Laelaps, freedman of Lucius [son of Publius].
EDCS-22100796.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker, indicating a freedman and his patron.

EDCS-22100797.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker.

EDCS-22100798.translation: To the departed spirits, Ceridonius Tertius for Atia Ianuaria and Trebonius Adiectus, who deserved well.
EDCS-22100798.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Ceridonius Tertius to Atia Ianuaria and Trebonius Adiectus, honoring their merits.

EDCS-22100801.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tomb or boundary marker, indicating familial relationships.

EDCS-22100804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextia, freedwoman of Varia Quintus.

EDCS-22100807.translation: Lucius Venetus, son of Velius, of the Arria tribe.
EDCS-22100807.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Venetus, son of Velius, identifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22100808.translation: Of Aulus Vensius, son of Callus.
EDCS-22100808.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aulus Vensius, son of Callus.

EDCS-22100810.translation: Of Sextus Vettius, son of Caius.
EDCS-22100810.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Vettius, son of Caius.

EDCS-22100811.translation: Gaius Veitius Varius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-22100811.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Veitius Varius Rufus, son of Lucius, identifying his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22100812.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Vettius Proculus (dedicates this) to Vettia Procula, and to Primitivus Taediar, and to himself. Plot of the monument: 108 Roman feet in every direction.
EDCS-22100812.summary: This is a funerary epitaph and tomb plot description set up by Gaius Vettius Proculus for Vettia Procula and Primitivus Taediar, and himself.

EDCS-22100817.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ramta Lautni, freedwoman of Vibies.

EDCS-22100818.translation: Gaius Vibius Rufus, son of Gaius, grandson of Lucius.
EDCS-22100818.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vibius Rufus, son of Gaius and grandson of Lucius.

EDCS-22100821.translation: Of Lares Vibineus Crasnus, son of La La Vipinus, son of Carus.
EDCS-22100821.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lares Vibineus Crasnus, son of La La Vipinus, son of Carus.

EDCS-22100826.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Velus, son of Vissius Velos.

EDCS-22100827.summary: This inscription names Umbricia Philaenis, likely a personal inscription on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22100828.translation: Aulus Voesius, son of Aulus, born
EDCS-22100828.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that names Aulus Voesius and his filiation, possibly the beginning of a funerary or commemorative text.

EDCS-22100833.translation: Velus Annius, son of Velius and Ramta Laurstia
EDCS-22100833.summary: This inscription provides the name and parentage of Velus Annius, likely part of a larger funerary inscription.

EDCS-22100834.translation: Tania Uni, daughter of Veties Arnensis
EDCS-22100834.summary: This inscription identifies Tania Uni and her father Veties Arnensis, probably a fragment from a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-22100866.translation: Set aside a place for his wife Fonteia Victoria, in the service of the departed spirits.
EDCS-22100866.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Fonteia Victoria, made by an unnamed husband, to be placed in a burial site.

EDCS-22100913.translation: Stefanus rests here, who lived 9 years and rested in peace on the Kalends of December, in the 8th consulship of the divine Valentinian Augustus.
EDCS-22100913.summary: This inscription records the death of Stefanus, detailing his age and the date of his passing, including the consulship of Valentinian Augustus VIII, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-22100915.translation: Laurentia, a praiseworthy woman, rests here in peace, who believed in the resurrection and lived more or less 25 years, and was buried on the day before the Nones of June, in the consulship of the most illustrious Albinius.
EDCS-22100915.summary: This inscription details the life and death of Laurentia, a Christian woman, noting her age and burial date, which is dated to the consulship of Albinius, indicating a post-Constantinian date.

EDCS-22100917.summary: This is a simple dedication made by Saint Florentinus, a bishop, likely for a religious building or object.

EDCS-22100918.translation: Flavius Partenius of most illustrious memory rests here in peace with his wife Agnilla, who lived sixty years.
EDCS-22100918.summary: This inscription records the death of Flavius Partenius and his wife Agnilla, giving their ages and serving as a joint funerary monument.

EDCS-22100932.translation: Lucius Lucilius Chares, freedman of Lucilia, for himself and his own; and Memmia, freedwoman of Caius, for herself and her own.
EDCS-22100932.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Lucilius Chares and Memmia, detailing their status as freedpersons and indicating the monument was intended for themselves and their families.

EDCS-22100934.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Ulpius Epaga­thianus, son of Marcus, decurion, aedile, magistrate, who had held all offices, lived 41 years, 8 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-22100934.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Ulpius Epaga­thianus, detailing his public career and lifespan.

EDCS-22100946.translation: Sacred to Jupiter the Victorious. Gaius Valerius Sporus, Sevirus Augustalis, with his [---] his brother Mari[---]no, from Si[---].
EDCS-22100946.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Victor by Gaius Valerius Sporus, a Sevirus Augustalis, with incomplete information about other individuals involved.

EDCS-22100950.translation: Baccia Priscilla, daughter of Sarto, while still alive, saw to the making of this for herself.
EDCS-22100950.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Baccia Priscilla for herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-22100951.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely the ownership or dedication of an object or monument to Sextus Clemens Probus.

EDCS-22100959.translation: The magistri (officials) contributed and arranged; Lucius, son of Titus, and Titia, daughter of Lucius, freedwomen (or women of status), from the magistrae.
EDCS-22100959.summary: This inscription records contributions and arrangements made by officials, possibly related to a religious or civic association.

EDCS-22100967.translation: Flavius Ardabur Aspar, illustrious man, count and master of soldiers, and ordinary consul; Ardabur the younger, praetor.
EDCS-22100967.summary: This inscription lists the high offices held by two prominent individuals, Flavius Ardabur Aspar and his son Ardabur the younger.

EDCS-22100970.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cosconia Hygiae, with whom he lived 25 years, Lucius Tettius Primitivus had this set up for his most beloved wife, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-22100970.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Cosconia Hygiae, dedicated by her husband Lucius Tettius Primitivus, mentioning their years together.

EDCS-22100972.translation: To Victor, Sevirus Augustalis, also quinquennial official, corporatus in the guild of codicarii, patron; Fructuosus, Sevirus Augustalis, also quinquennial official, corporatus in the guild of codicarii, who held all offices; Callinicus, freedman of the aforementioned Fructuosus, and Modia Parthenope, his wife, made this and transported the bones of the aforementioned Victor after 19 years.
EDCS-22100972.summary: This inscription honors Victor, a prominent member of the codicarii guild, by his freedman Callinicus and Callinicus's wife Modia Parthenope, who also managed the re-interment of Victor's remains.

EDCS-22100975.translation: ...Tertius... made ... Braetius(?), son of Quintus, Probus...
EDCS-22100975.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly recording the commissioning of a monument by Braetius Probus.

EDCS-22100977.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 17th time, Imperator for the 3rd time, Consul for the 4th time, Proconsul, Father of the Fatherland, Great and Invincible, and superior to all princes, brave, fortunate, because of his many and outstanding benefactions towards him, by divine indulgence, with public money, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22100977.summary: This is a public inscription from the decurions praising Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus for his military victories and benefactions, funded by public money.

EDCS-22100982.translation: He set this up at his own expense, as decreed by the decurions, because of his public service as a *sevirus*, with Marcus Semnius Caevianus Priscus as curator.
EDCS-22100982.summary: This is a public dedication made by an individual in his capacity as a *sevirus*, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE, as indicated by the presence of a curator.

EDCS-22100985.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publicae lived 7 years, 10 months. Tertius and Publicia Fortunata, parents, made this for their most cherished daughter Saturnia Fortunata, who lived 33 years. For her husband Primitivus, a slave of the colony, who lived 12 years, 4 months, 7 days.
EDCS-22100985.summary: A tombstone for a young girl named Publicae and her deceased husband, Primitivus, set up by her parents, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100986.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Carpus, the agent, made this for his incomparable wife Sabina, with whom he lived 20 years, 5 months; she lived 30 years, 6 months.
EDCS-22100986.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife, providing details of their married life and her lifespan, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100987.translation: To Quintus, son of Aius, and to Albia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-22100987.summary: This is a brief dedication, possibly for a tombstone, honoring two individuals, Quintus and Albia, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100989.translation: Calvisius Alexander and Velia, freedwoman of Titus, made this for themselves while they were alive.
EDCS-22100989.summary: A funerary monument made by a couple, Calvisius Alexander and Velia, for their future use, indicating their status as freedpersons, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100990.summary: A dedication likely for a tombstone, honoring a son named Sabatina Cleopatra, set up by an unnamed individual, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100991.summary: This is a dedication honoring a mother, Flavia Primilla, presumably for a tombstone or memorial, set up by her children, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100992.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lisinius Ampliatus set this up for his well-deserving wife, Minatia Primitiva.
EDCS-22100992.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, Minatia Primitiva, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100993.translation: To Gaius Munatius Calus, Marcus Alentius Quintillianus and Epexi [dedicated this].
EDCS-22100993.summary: A dedication, possibly funerary, to Gaius Munatius Calus, made by Marcus Alentius Quintillianus and Epexi, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100994.translation: Nymphicus the boy rests here. Caius Petisius Apollonius made this.
EDCS-22100994.summary: A tombstone for a young boy named Nymphicus, set up by Caius Petisius Apollonius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22100995.translation: Petisia Flora, freedwoman of Lucius Petisius, and Ammia, freedwoman of Lucius Petisius, lived.
EDCS-22100995.summary: This inscription records the lives of two freedwomen, Petisia Flora and Ammia, both freed by Lucius Petisius.

EDCS-22100996.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Aba, wife of Caius, [erected this].
EDCS-22100996.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Pompeia Aba, wife of Caius, set up by a relative.

EDCS-22100997.translation: Laspa Saturnina, heroine, in the field, 100 feet.
EDCS-22100997.summary: This inscription likely marks a burial plot of 100 feet in a field for Laspa Saturnina, referred to as a 'heroine'.

EDCS-22100998.translation: Tertulla lived 2 years and 7 months. Her mother Cornuia Vitalis set this up.
EDCS-22100998.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Tertulla and is dedicated by her mother, Cornuia Vitalis.

EDCS-22101000.translation: Sabatina, daughter of Marcus Valerius, son of Spurius.
EDCS-22101000.summary: This inscription is a simple genealogical record for Sabatina, daughter of Marcus Valerius.

EDCS-22101001.translation: Larcia, freedwoman of Lucius, [dedicated this] to her patron and to herself, 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-22101001.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Larcia, a freedwoman, to her patron and herself, possibly marking a plot of land.

EDCS-22101004.summary: This inscription records the self-dedication of a monument or tomb by a person whose name is partially lost.

EDCS-22101008.translation: Sacred to the Nymphs. Aulus Fassidius Iustus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-22101008.summary: This is a religious dedication to the Nymphs by Aulus Fassidius Iustus, made in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-22101009.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Caninius Legitimus made this for his father, Communis, freedman of Caius Caninius, who deserved excellently of him.
EDCS-22101009.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Caius Caninius Legitimus to his father Communis, a freedman.

EDCS-22101010.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Varius Eudaemon, a deserving husband. Agria Ingenua, and Varius Ingenuus and Eudaemon, sons.
EDCS-22101010.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Gaius Varius Eudaemon, a deserving husband, by his wife Agria Ingenua and his sons Varius Ingenuus and Eudaemon.

EDCS-22101011.translation: Sacred to Ceres by Caius Paetius Severus, a man of note.
EDCS-22101011.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Ceres by Caius Paetius Severus.

EDCS-22101013.translation: Tiberius Claudius Thermodon gave this gift to Diana.
EDCS-22101013.summary: This inscription records a gift offered to Diana by Tiberius Claudius Thermodon.

EDCS-22101014.translation: To Sol Invictus Mithras, Tiberius Claudius Thermodon, son of Tiberius, fulfilled his vow by dedicating a cave with statues, an altar, and other items, having received the fulfillment of his prayer.
EDCS-22101014.summary: Tiberius Claudius Thermodon dedicated a shrine with cultic objects to Sol Invictus Mithras after his vow was answered.

EDCS-22101015.translation: To the Great Holy Goddess Nortia, Caius Larcius Agathopus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-22101015.summary: Caius Larcius Agathopus made a vow to the goddess Nortia.

EDCS-22101016.translation: For the gods and goddesses, Primitivus, a slave and manager for the goddess Nortia.
EDCS-22101016.summary: This inscription seems to indicate Primitivus, a slave of the goddess Nortia, making an offering or statement regarding the gods and goddesses.

EDCS-22101017.translation: Lucius Vibius Legitimus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Holy Hercules.
EDCS-22101017.summary: Lucius Vibius Legitimus dedicated an offering to Hercules, stating his vow was fulfilled willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-22101018.translation: Cileius Priscus, with all his household, willingly fulfilled his vow by setting up this altar to Ciminian Jupiter.
EDCS-22101018.summary: Cileius Priscus and his family dedicated an altar to Jupiter Ciminus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-22101019.translation: Sacred to Holy Silvanus, Caius Vettius Primitivus restored the base with the shrine of Silvanus.
EDCS-22101019.summary: Caius Vettius Primitivus restored a shrine dedicated to Silvanus.

EDCS-22101020.translation: Caius Callius Nortinus, a decurion, set this up in accordance with his vow.
EDCS-22101020.summary: Caius Callius Nortinus, a local official, set up this monument in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-22101021.translation: Chryseros fulfilled his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-22101021.summary: Chryseros dedicated an offering to the Nymphs, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-22101027.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus.
EDCS-22101027.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperor Constantius, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-22101029.translation: To Gaius Rufius Festus, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, former primipilar tribune of the 5th cohort of vigiles, twice city prefect and thrice praetorian prefect, procurator of the province of Dalmatia and Histria. Gaius Rufius Festus Laelius Firmus, a most distinguished man, and Rufia Procula, daughter of Gaius, a most distinguished woman, [placed this] for their most devoted father, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22101029.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Rufius Festus by his children, detailing his extensive career in military and administrative posts, dating likely to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-22200485.translation: To the divine shades. Securus, imperial freedman and administrator, to his well-deserving wife Ulpia Terpsidi, and Hilarus, their son, to his most devoted mother.
EDCS-22200485.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ulpia Terpsidi, set up by her husband Securus and son Hilarus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-22200490.translation: To Volsinius Victorinus, quinquennalis of the college of Augustan artisans, archivist of the public affairs of the Volusinians and also of the Ferentinians.
EDCS-22200490.summary: This inscription records the dedication of Volsinius Victorinus to his role as quinquennalis and archivist for two communities, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200494.translation: To Rufia Primitiva, his most holy companion. Primitivus, a servant of the state and actor, made [this] for his well-deserving companion.
EDCS-22200494.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primitivus, a state employee, for his 'most holy companion' Rufia Primitiva, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200497.translation: Aulus Seppius Moderatus, curator; Aulus Volcacius Studio, curator; Caius Vibennius Threptus made [this].
EDCS-22200497.summary: This inscription records the joint work of three curatores, likely in a public or collegial capacity, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200498.summary: This inscription simply names Gaius Caetennius Saturninus as a curator, likely holding a public or administrative office, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200506.translation: Cnaeus Afreius, the master, gives a gift to Tania Detrona, daughter of Vel.
EDCS-22200506.summary: This inscription records a gift made by Cnaeus Afreius, identified as 'magister', to Tania Detrona, likely related to a collegium or religious office, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200511.translation: To the divine shades. Sextus Perperna and Manneia Res.
EDCS-22200511.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the divine shades for Sextus Perperna and Manneia Res, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200512.translation: To the divine shades. Lucius Herennius Proculus made [this] for his well-deserving wife, Ailia Caleni.
EDCS-22200512.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Herennius Proculus for his wife, Ailia Caleni, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200516.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Lucius Allius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22200517.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Allius Redemptus, his most dutiful son, who lived 10 years and 2 months. Florus and Luccia [made this].
EDCS-22200517.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Lucius Allius Redemptus, who died at the age of 10 years and 2 months, and was commemorated by Florus and Luccia.

EDCS-22200518.translation: In the year 1154 (of the AUC). Proculus lived 24 years. Allia Iucunda, daughter of Lucius, and Lucius Allius, made this for themselves and their family.
EDCS-22200518.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Proculus, who lived 24 years, and was made by Allia Iucunda and Lucius Allius, likely dated to 1154 AUC (circa 21 AD).

EDCS-22200519.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Appius Priscianus, Caesennia Fortunata [made this] for her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-22200519.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caesennia Fortunata's dedication to her husband, Lucius Appius Priscianus.

EDCS-22200520.translation: To the departed spirits. For Avilia Legitima. Avilia II [made this].
EDCS-22200520.summary: This funerary epitaph is a dedication by Avilia II to Avilia Legitima.

EDCS-22200522.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Caecinius Capriolus, Caecinia Eunia [made this] for her dearest son.
EDCS-22200522.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caecinia Eunia's dedication to her beloved son, Gaius Caecinius Capriolus.

EDCS-22200523.translation: To the departed spirits. Veiania Felicitas made this for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Coelius Urso.
EDCS-22200523.summary: This funerary epitaph records Veiania Felicitas's dedication to her husband, Lucius Coelius Urso.

EDCS-22200524.translation: Marcus Caestius Clemens, son of Gaius, of the Arnensis tribe.
EDCS-22200524.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Caestius Clemens, son of Gaius and belonging to the Arnensis tribe.

EDCS-22200526.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Calpurnius Rastus.

EDCS-22200528.translation: And for you too. Lucius Canuleius Eunus made this for himself while alive, and for you.
EDCS-22200528.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Lucius Canuleius Eunus dedicates the monument to himself and another person while he is still alive.

EDCS-22200529.translation: Lucius Canuleius Romanus [dedicated this] to Canuleia Euterpe.
EDCS-22200529.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Rome, likely from the late Republic or early Empire, recording a dedication to Canuleia Euterpe by Lucius Canuleius Romanus.

EDCS-22200531.translation: Ere, Attivos and Vitalis made [this] for their father Publius Capruus, aged 32.
EDCS-22200531.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication made by Ere, Attivos, and Vitalis for their father, Publius Capruus, who died at the age of 32.

EDCS-22200532.translation: [To the departed spirits...] Catellia, freedwoman of [---], alive. [---] Lucius Catellius, son of Lucius, freedman, alive. [---] Lucius Catellius, son of Lucius, freedman, Fusc[us...], alive. Catellia, freedwoman of Lucius, Nym[phe...], deceased. Cypr[...]
EDCS-22200532.summary: This fragmented funerary epitaph from Rome, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE, records the names and status of several deceased individuals associated with the Catellii family.

EDCS-22200539.translation: To the departed spirits of Delicata. Eupor made [this] for his deserving wife.
EDCS-22200539.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Empire, records Eupor's dedication to his deserving wife, Delicata.

EDCS-22200540.translation: To the departed spirits of Egnatia Daphne. Pomponia Maximina made [this] for her deserving friend.
EDCS-22200540.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Empire, records Pomponia Maximina's dedication to her deserving friend, Egnatia Daphne.

EDCS-22200541.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Etrius. Etrius Su made [this] for his wife.
EDCS-22200541.summary: This funerary epitaph records Etrius Su's dedication to his wife, Lucius Etrius.

EDCS-22200543.translation: To the departed spirits of Fannia Rufina. She lived 5 years and 31 days.
EDCS-22200543.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Fannia Rufina, who died at the age of 5 years and 31 days.

EDCS-22200544.translation: To the departed spirits of Popilia Iusta. Fannia Rufina [made this] for her deserving grandmother.
EDCS-22200544.summary: This funerary epitaph records Fannia Rufina's dedication to her deserving grandmother, Popilia Iusta.

EDCS-22200545.translation: Fassidia Ursa made [this] for her father, Gaius Fassidius Vitalis.
EDCS-22200545.summary: This funerary epitaph records Fassidia Ursa's dedication to her father, Gaius Fassidius Vitalis.

EDCS-22200546.translation: Felicitas [made this] for her deserving husband, who lived 3 months and 20 days after [their] daughter.
EDCS-22200546.summary: This funerary epitaph records Felicitas' dedication to her deserving husband, who outlived their daughter by 3 months and 20 days.

EDCS-22200548.translation: To the Divine Manes. Furia Aphrodite made this for her husband, Gaius Cassius Nepos, most excellent and deserving.
EDCS-22200548.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by Furia Aphrodite for her husband, Gaius Cassius Nepos.

EDCS-22200549.translation: Gavia Pampila, a freedwoman of a woman, [set this up]. Lucius Annius Anina, son of Gaius.
EDCS-22200549.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a tombstone for Gavia Pampila, a freedwoman, and Lucius Annius Anina.

EDCS-22200550.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, with names such as Luperca and Maximus appearing.

EDCS-22200554.translation: To the Divine Manes. Modia Marcellina made this for her pious mother, Modia Afrodisia.
EDCS-22200554.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by Modia Marcellina for her mother, Modia Afrodisia.

EDCS-22200555.translation: To the Divine Manes. Her husband made this for Nonia Victorina, well-deserving.
EDCS-22200555.summary: This is a funerary dedication (Dis Manibus) made by a husband for his wife, Nonia Victorina.

EDCS-22200557.translation: Paba Philomusus, freedman of Aulus; Hedone Chryse, freedwoman of Lucius; Anneia, freedwoman of Aulus, [set this up] for themselves and their third part, and Pabaea Rufina, freedwoman of Aulus; Paba Alcimus, freedman of Aulus.
EDCS-22200557.summary: This is a dedication, possibly for a building or property, made by several freedmen and freedwomen for themselves and a share of the property.

EDCS-22200558.translation: Gaius Pacilius Felix [made this] for his son Gaius Pacilius Callistus, 15 miles, [dedicated] by the will of his father, [for the sake of his] health.
EDCS-22200558.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Pacilius Felix for his son, Gaius Pacilius Callistus, indicating distance and intent.

EDCS-22200559.translation: Titus Pacinius Florus, heir [for] Gaius Pacinius Apro.
EDCS-22200559.summary: This inscription records Titus Pacinius Florus as the heir for Gaius Pacinius Apro.

EDCS-22200560.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription consisting of a single name, Lucius Petronius, likely a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-22200562.summary: This inscription records the name Polydeuces in conjunction with the consulship, possibly indicating a dedication made during their term.

EDCS-22200563.translation: To Gaius M. Proi, Marcus O. Phi Pr. P. [made this].
EDCS-22200563.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus O. Phi Pr. P. to Gaius M. Proi.

EDCS-22200564.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aulus Avillius Aper made this for his deserving wife Redempta.
EDCS-22200564.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Avillius Aper for his wife Redempta.

EDCS-22200568.translation: Sertorius Leo placed this for himself while alive.
EDCS-22200568.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sertorius Leo for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-22200569.translation: Of Caius Spurius, freedman of Caius, 10 feet in front and 10 feet in the field.
EDCS-22200569.summary: This records the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Caius Spurius, freedman of Caius.

EDCS-22200570.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Edius Successus.

EDCS-22200571.translation: Sulpicii Lupula and Restutus, and Herennia Ianuaria, fellow heirs, made this for their most beloved brother Sulpicius Felix.
EDCS-22200571.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sulpicii Lupula and Restutus, and Herennia Ianuaria for their brother Sulpicius Felix.

EDCS-22200572.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sulpicius Proculus made this for his most dutiful mother Sulpicia Fortunata.
EDCS-22200572.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sulpicius Proculus for his mother Sulpicia Fortunata.

EDCS-22200573.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Terentius Maritalis made this for his deserving wife Terentia Quintiana.
EDCS-22200573.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Terentius Maritalis for his wife Terentia Quintiana.

EDCS-22200574.translation: To Tineius Ced D [on the] day before the Nones.
EDCS-22200574.summary: This is a dedication to Tineius Ced D on a specific date.

EDCS-22200575.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Troillus, the most faithful slave.
EDCS-22200575.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for the slave Troillus.

EDCS-22200576.translation: To Lico. Trype, freedwoman of Titus [3]oria; Eros, freedman of Titus [3]orius.
EDCS-22200576.summary: This inscription records the dedication by or to Trype and Eros, freedpersons of Titus, with a lacuna in their names.

EDCS-22200577.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Valeria Surilla for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Valerius Sigerus.
EDCS-22200577.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Valeria Surilla to her husband, Lucius Valerius Sigerus.

EDCS-22200578.translation: To Gaius Var Lucius Renn for his grandfather.
EDCS-22200578.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Renn for his grandfather.

EDCS-22200579.translation: To Varius Atimetus and Nenia, his daughter.
EDCS-22200579.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Varius Atimetus and his daughter, Nenia.

EDCS-22200581.translation: To Quass Maecil for his father.
EDCS-22200581.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quass Maecil for his father.

EDCS-22200582.translation: To Iusil [iva?]. Venuleius Legitimus and Venuleia [seudam?].
EDCS-22200582.summary: This inscription appears to record the names of Venuleius Legitimus and Venuleia, possibly a dedication or funerary record, with lacunae.

EDCS-22200583.translation: Titus Venuleius Priscus, son of Titus, of the Pomptina tribe; Sextus Venuleius Fuscus, son of Titus, of the Pomptina tribe; with Titus Venuleius, son of Lucius, his father; and Larcia Aulus, daughter of Aulus, his mother; from the will, 1000 sesterces.
EDCS-22200583.summary: This inscription details a bequest from the will of Titus Venuleius Priscus and Sextus Venuleius Fuscus, mentioning their parents and a sum of 1000 sesterces.

EDCS-22200586.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Annius Caesianus and Marcius Proculus made this for their well-deserving wife, Volcasia Sabina, who lived 50 years and 5 months.
EDCS-22200586.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Annius Caesianus and Marcius Proculus for their wife, Volcasia Sabina, including her lifespan.

EDCS-22200587.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Volo by Turcia, identified as a mother.

EDCS-22200592.translation: I command the freedmen's wicked freedmen in the island where he was born.
EDCS-22200592.summary: This inscription is a command concerning freedmen and their 'wicked' status, possibly related to property or legal matters on an island.

EDCS-22200599.translation: Iuvenius Aulus Bet gave his bones to the earth.
EDCS-22200599.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iuvenius Aulus Bet, indicating the burial of his remains.

EDCS-22200614.translation: To Mettia Navigia, his wife, good daughter, most sweet daughter-in-law, most obedient daughter-in-law, whose loyalty, modesty, and piety could never be overcome, who lived 34 years, 4 months, 8 days, and with her husband lived 20 years, 4 months, 22 days. Her husband, curator of the public affairs of this city, established [this]. Her burial on the day before the Ides of September, in the consulship of our lords Valens and Valentinian. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200614.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mettia Navigia, praising her virtues and recording her age and burial date, likely from the late 4th century CE based on the consuls mentioned.

EDCS-22200615.translation: To Aelius Gentilis, a praiseworthy man and physician, who lived 78 years, 10 months, 8 days, of honorable reputation. His sons erected this for their deserving father. Buried on the 7th day before the Ides of November. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200615.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aelius Gentilis, a physician, by his sons, recording his age and burial date, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200616.translation: Recently marked by the distinguished gift of Christ, who, once torn away by the harsh death of his parents, he received his parents through a better fate. But Fortune dragged the day and did not delay the hour, for she closed the times of his life in the earth. His name is Alexander. If you seek his homeland and lineage, it is here. He lived here 9 months, 25 days. He perished on the 3rd day before the Ides of September, in the consulship of [---].
EDCS-22200616.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young man named Alexander, possibly a Christian convert, lamenting his premature death and recording his age at death, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-22200617.translation: To Aurelius Florentius, full of all innocence, who deserved well of [her]. He lived with his wife for [---] years. Erected on the 13th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-22200617.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Florentius, set up by his wife, recording the date of erection and mentioning his virtuous character.

EDCS-22200619.translation: If pure minds hold the boundaries of heaven, Castorius the young man now joins his beloved companions, leaving bodily bonds and the chains of life. He has deserved to embrace the eternal abodes of the pious, the sublime souls. Let no one think he goes under the shades, but the wise man, though he perishes on earth, lives among the stars. And now, learned boy, skilled in law, he accompanies the crowd of the pious in a green place, and recalls the praises of his life and...
EDCS-22200619.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young man named Castorius, celebrating his intellectual virtues and asserting his entry into the afterlife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200621.translation: To Decimila, who lived 13 days, and with her husband lived 14 years, 8 months, 21 days. Erected for her deserving [memory] on the 7th day [before the Ides?]. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200621.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Decimila, recording her very short lifespan and the duration of her marriage, likely from the Roman Imperial period, possibly with Christian elements.

EDCS-22200622.translation: To Flavia Marthana, a most chaste woman, by nation a Syra, a citizen of Antioch. Iulius Flavius Lupercianus of the fleet [dedicated this] to his deserving wife on the Kalends of February. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200622.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Marthana, a woman from Antioch, dedicated by her husband, a member of the fleet, on the Kalends of February, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22200628.translation: To Valeria Polemia, an innocent neophyte, who lived 24 days. Domitius Marc Maura, parents, erected [this]. Deposited on the 8th day before the Ides. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200628.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Polemia, an infant neophyte (new convert to Christianity), recording her very short life and burial date, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-22200631.translation: Sassilius, [aged] of both years... in addition... 512... 117... 33
EDCS-22200631.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented funerary text, possibly recording ages or dates with numerical components, the precise meaning of which is unclear due to damage.

EDCS-22200635.translation: Completed by the savior Pacuitus the innocent, here, in voice.
EDCS-22200635.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary or devotional, mentioning a savior and the name Pacuitus.

EDCS-22200661.translation: Cestronia Castoria, who lived 56 years, made this for her virginity; she lived 37 years and 5 months; she was buried on the 5th day before the Kalends of October, in the 6th consulship of Arcadius and Publius Anicius Probus. Peace be with you.
EDCS-22200661.summary: This epitaph records the life and burial of Cestronia Castoria, providing her age at death and the date of burial, likely from the late Roman period given the consular dating.

EDCS-22200663.translation: To Aurelia Lampadia, daughter of [---], 3 years old. Parents of good memory. And peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200663.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Aurelia Lampadia, a child, set up by her parents, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-22200664.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for a child named Gerini Pelegrina, indicating her age at death.

EDCS-22200669.translation: To the worthy spirit of Rufia Maximina, who lived 6 years and 6 months. Rufia [erected this].
EDCS-22200669.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Rufia Maximina, who died at a young age, likely erected by a relative named Rufia.

EDCS-22200674.translation: Burial of Heper, count, illustrious man, deacon, on the 15th day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-22200674.summary: This inscription records the burial date of Heper, who held the titles of count, illustrious man, and deacon, suggesting a significant figure in the late Roman or early Byzantine church.

EDCS-22200677.translation: Burial of Constans, 5th day before the Kalends of December.
EDCS-22200677.summary: This is a brief inscription recording the burial date of Constans.

EDCS-22200678.translation: Cristina, peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200678.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a Christian blessing for Cristina.

EDCS-22200679.translation: To Sapricia, who lived 70 years and 6 months and 20 days. Peace be with you among the saints. Her sons made this for their well-deserving mother.
