EDCS-22200679.summary: This epitaph records the life span of Sapricia and was erected by her sons, indicating familial piety and likely dating to the Christian era.

EDCS-22200680.translation: Burial of Valentina, 9th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-22200680.summary: This inscription records the burial date of Valentina.

EDCS-22200682.translation: To Alexandra, who deserved well, who lived 40 years, 4 months, and 7 days. Peace be with you among the saints.
EDCS-22200682.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Alexandra, likely from the early Christian period, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-22200683.translation: Maronius made this for the well-deserving Mate Secundae. The Ides of November. Peace be with you. Placed.
EDCS-22200683.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Maronius to Mate Secundae, dated to the Ides of November.

EDCS-22200684.translation: To Vettia Lea, who lived years, 7 months, 30 days. I, Victor, to my dearest.
EDCS-22200684.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vettia Lea, with a dedication from Victor.

EDCS-22200685.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly an epitaph or dedication, to Armenia Agirisapi.

EDCS-22200686.translation: To Rufina, a good soul, who lived 20 years and 8 months, who made this with her husband for 4 years and 33 days because of her chastity. Placed the 7th Ides of March.
EDCS-22200686.summary: This funerary inscription honors Rufina, noting her lifespan and the duration of her marriage, with a date on the 7th Ides of March.

EDCS-22200804.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Caesennia Fortunata, his excellent wife, daughter of Lucius Appius Calvisius Clementi, soldier of the 10th urban cohort. Lucius Appius Tryphonianus, her father, made this for himself with his own money.
EDCS-22200804.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caesennia Fortunata, set up by her father, Lucius Appius Tryphonianus, who was a soldier in the 10th urban cohort.

EDCS-22200805.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Baburia Philtate, Sextus Baburius Severus to his dearest wife.
EDCS-22200805.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Baburia Philtate, dedicated by her husband, Sextus Baburius Severus.

EDCS-22200806.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Calpurnia Galla, daughter of Caius. Attius Allianus to his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-22200806.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calpurnia Galla, dedicated by her husband, Attius Allianus.

EDCS-22200807.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Hail Calvisius Prepo, a good man, who lived 91 years, 2 months, and 1 day. Vettia Eutychia, his wife, and Calvisius Aelianus, his son, made this.
EDCS-22200807.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Calvisius Prepo, noting his lifespan and erected by his wife and son.

EDCS-22200808.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Publius Caprutius Asiaticus. Publius Caprutius Callistus, his father.
EDCS-22200808.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Caprutius Asiaticus, set up by his father, Publius Caprutius Callistus.

EDCS-22200809.translation: Cornelia Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, lived 20 years.
EDCS-22200809.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of a freedwoman named Cornelia Secunda.

EDCS-22200810.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Artaginie, a fellow freedwoman of Sentius Peculiaris, made this.
EDCS-22200810.summary: This dedication to the underworld spirits was made by Artaginie, a fellow freedwoman of Sentius Peculiaris.

EDCS-22200812.translation: Sacred to Hercules, on account of the honor of the Augustales. Hedonicus, freedman of Marcus Vettius Telesphorus, son of Marcus, was granted this place by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22200812.summary: This inscription records the granting of a place to Hedonicus, a freedman and member of the Augustales, by the decurions.

EDCS-22200813.translation: Sacred to Honos. Artoria Auxesis, wife of Marcus Minatius Sabatinus Gallus, who was twice a magistrate with five-year authority and who dispensed justice, made this honorary monument for her husband.
EDCS-22200813.summary: This is a dedication to Honos, erected by Artoria Auxesis in honor of her husband, Marcus Minatius Sabatinus Gallus, a local magistrate.

EDCS-22200814.translation: Sacred to Virtus. Maternus, son of Marcus Minatius Sabatinus Gallus, who was twice a magistrate with five-year authority and who dispensed justice, made this honorary monument for his father, and on account of the dedication ceremony he gave a banquet with cake and honey-wine to the villagers and the people.
EDCS-22200814.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Virtus by Maternus, son of a local magistrate, who also provided a public banquet.

EDCS-22200815.translation: Marcus Minatius Sabatinus Gallus, twice a magistrate with five-year authority and who dispensed justice, made this honorary tribunal for the public good and for the honor.
EDCS-22200815.summary: This inscription records the construction of an honorary tribunal by Marcus Minatius Sabatinus Gallus, a local magistrate.

EDCS-22200817.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus, Invictus, Pius, Felix, Augustus, consul for the second time, proconsul, Imperator for the fifth time, Father of the Fatherland, Germanicus Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the third time; by the Senate and People of Visentium.
EDCS-22200817.summary: This is a dedication of a monument to Emperor Valerian by the people of Visentium, listing his titles and honors.

EDCS-22200818.translation: To Lucius Caesius Balbinus, son of Lucius, of the Sabina tribe, Cestius, father; to his son Lucius Caesius Valens, of the Sabina tribe; to his daughter Cestia Balbina, daughter of Lucius; to his grandmother Caestia Quarta, daughter of Lucius; to Lucius Cestius Apro, son of Lucius, of the Sabina tribe, who lived 1 year and 6 months; Lucius Caesius Balbinus, son of Lucius, of the Sabina tribe, made this for himself and all his descendants.
EDCS-22200818.summary: This is a family tombstone erected by Lucius Caesius Balbinus for himself and his deceased relatives, including his son and father.

EDCS-22200819.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Seius Legitimus made this for his well-deserving wife, Afrania Ianuaria, who lived 31 years. Greetings, farewell.
EDCS-22200819.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated by Lucius Seius Legitimus to his wife, Afrania Ianuaria.

EDCS-22200821.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Cornelia Materna made this for her well-deserving husband, Fructus. Greetings, farewell.
EDCS-22200821.summary: This is a tombstone dedicated by Cornelia Materna to her husband, Fructus.

EDCS-22200822.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Avillius Firmus and Caius Avillius Iustus, brothers, set this up; the equites of CCCC quadringenarii made it.
EDCS-22200822.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by two brothers for unnamed deceased, and the work was executed by a group identified as 'equites CCCC quadringenarii'.

EDCS-22200823.summary: This funerary inscription names Orcus (a god of the underworld) and was made by Terpusa.

EDCS-22200825.translation: To Juno Regina. Antonius, son of Publius, and Lucius Virginius, son of Titus, magistrates of the pagus.
EDCS-22200825.summary: This dedication to Juno Regina was made by two officials identified as 'magistri pagi' (magistrates of the district).

EDCS-22200826.translation: To Junia Felicitas, who lived 50 years. Her sons set this up for their well-deserving mother.
EDCS-22200826.summary: This funerary inscription was erected by sons for their deserving mother, Junia Felicitas.

EDCS-22200827.translation: Mavius C. rvos, by decree of the Senate, to be restored. Mavius C. by decree of the Senate, to be restored.
EDCS-22200827.summary: This inscription, possibly a public notice or dedication, mentions restoration ordered by a senatorial decree and is associated with a person named Mavius.

EDCS-22200828.translation: To the Divine Manes. His sons and wife placed this for Ventedius Proclus, who lived 53 years, a deserving man.
EDCS-22200828.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by the sons and wife for Ventedius Proclus.

EDCS-22200829.translation: To holy Apollo. Lucius Minicius Natalis, consul, proconsul of Africa, augur, legate of the emperor with praetorian authority in Lower Moesia.
EDCS-22200829.summary: This dedication to Apollo was made by Lucius Minicius Natalis, who held significant imperial and senatorial offices in various provinces.

EDCS-22200833.translation: For Marcus Aurelius Lucius, tribune of the soldiers of the II Augusta legion, and Antia Sebera, his wife. Marcus Aurelius Menophilus, freedman, made this for his well-deserving patron.
EDCS-22200833.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a freedman to his patron, who was a military tribune, and his wife.

EDCS-22200835.summary: This is a maker's mark or inscription indicating that an object came from the workshop of Ursinius.

EDCS-22200836.translation: For Gaius Mestrius Alapa, a sponge dealer, his freedwoman Chia made this for herself and her family while she was alive.
EDCS-22200836.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by a freedwoman for herself and her family, commemorating her living master, Gaius Mestrius Alapa, a sponge dealer.

EDCS-22200837.translation: Lucius and Ulfius, freedman of Lucius, Antaris.
EDCS-22200837.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming two individuals, Lucius and Ulfius.

EDCS-22200838.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely funerary, identifying Quintus Caecilius by his father.

EDCS-22200840.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Clodia, identified by her patron Sextus and by a cognomen.

EDCS-22200842.translation: Fannia, freedwoman of Caius, Antusa, made this for herself and her son Protio.
EDCS-22200842.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Fannia, identified by her patron Caius, for herself and her son Protio.

EDCS-22200843.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Graecinius Hilmo, aged 65. Graecinia Diucia, freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-22200843.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Graecinius Hilmo and Graecinia Diucia, providing their ages and relationships.

EDCS-22200845.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Caelius Lucretius, son of Caius, Sabatinus, Tettianus, freedmen of Lucretius Achilleus, Trophimus, Pollux, Castor, placed [this] for their patron.
EDCS-22200845.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by freedmen for their patron, Lucretius Achilleus, naming several individuals and their relationships.

EDCS-22200846.translation: Naneia Musa made [this] at home, a freedwoman, deservedly.
EDCS-22200846.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Naneia Musa, a freedwoman, for herself.

EDCS-22200847.translation: Caius Plotius, son of Caius, Sabatinus.
EDCS-22200847.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely funerary, identifying Caius Plotius by his father and a cognomen.

EDCS-22200848.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely funerary, identifying Posilla by her father.

EDCS-22200851.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Publius Serveilius.

EDCS-22200852.translation: Lucius Servilius, son of Lucius, aged forty-five.
EDCS-22200852.summary: This inscription records the age of Lucius Servilius, son of Lucius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22200853.summary: This inscription identifies Quinctus Tiberilius as a freedman of Quinctus, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22200854.translation: To the good memory of Discolius, who lived twenty-nine years and eleven months, with his wife Mucianeta.
EDCS-22200854.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Discolius, commemorating his life span and mentioning his wife, Mucianeta.

EDCS-22200863.translation: To Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, chief priest, in his fifth year of tribunician power, commander for the eleventh time, father of the fatherland, consul designate for the sixth time, censor. The townspeople, with their wives and children, from a collection of money.
EDCS-22200863.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Emperor Vespasian, likely erected by the local community (municipes) to honor him.

EDCS-22200867.translation: Lucius Valerius and Licinia Vo, citizens of Ovia, their freedman [or slave]...
EDCS-22200867.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the names of Lucius Valerius and Licinia Vo, followed by a person associated with them.

EDCS-22200871.translation: Sextus Acilius, son of Sextus, lived nineteen years.
EDCS-22200871.summary: This inscription records the age of Sextus Acilius, son of Sextus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22200873.translation: Aemilia, wife of Caelus, lived seventy years.
EDCS-22200873.summary: This inscription records the age of Aemilia, wife of Caelus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22200874.translation: Publius Aperius, son of Sextus, lived seventy-four years.
EDCS-22200874.summary: This inscription records the age of Publius Aperius, son of Sextus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22200878.translation: Calpurnia, daughter of Lucius, lived twenty years and ten months.
EDCS-22200878.summary: This inscription records the age of Calpurnia, daughter of Lucius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22200880.translation: Silana Legitima made this for her well-deserving husband, Gaius Clodius Castor, who lived fourteen years.
EDCS-22200880.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Silana Legitima dedicates a monument to her husband, Gaius Clodius Castor, specifying his age at death.

EDCS-22200881.translation: Thania Coelia, daughter of Lucius, aged 46.
EDCS-22200881.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Thania Coelia.

EDCS-22200882.translation: Lucius Corana, aged 81, lived for years.
EDCS-22200882.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Lucius Corana.

EDCS-22200884.translation: Tania Fafricia, daughter of Caius, lived for 31 years.
EDCS-22200884.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Tania Fafricia.

EDCS-22200885.translation: Publius Cavius, son of Sextus, lived for 35 years.
EDCS-22200885.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Publius Cavius.

EDCS-22200886.translation: Sextus Geganius, son of Publius Galle, lived for 70 years.
EDCS-22200886.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Sextus Geganius.

EDCS-22200887.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Sextus Hirius.

EDCS-22200890.translation: Caius Munatius, son of Caius, lived for 64 years.
EDCS-22200890.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Caius Munatius.

EDCS-22200891.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Sempronia Aprulla made this for her most dutiful son, Naevius Sempronius, who lived for 26 years.
EDCS-22200891.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a mother to her son, recording his age.

EDCS-22200892.translation: Lucius Petronius, son of Lucius, aged 13.
EDCS-22200892.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Lucius Petronius.

EDCS-22200893.translation: Titus Pompilius, son of Lucius, lived for 75 years.
EDCS-22200893.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Titus Pompilius.

EDCS-22200894.translation: Quintus Rubrius Mocos, son of Sextus, aged 56 years.
EDCS-22200894.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Rubrius Mocos, recording his name and age.

EDCS-22200901.translation: To my most innocent son Theodosius, whose exceptional love urges me to grieve. I, his father, struck by eternal grief, did not deserve to have such a son surviving me. He lived 18 years and rested in peace on the 13th day before the Kalends of October, during the consulship of our lords Honorius VII and Theodosius II Augustus.
EDCS-22200901.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Theodosius, a son grieving his father and the son's lifespan, mentioning his death date and the consuls, placing it in the early 5th century CE.

EDCS-22200904.translation: Valeria Victorina gave this gift to the August Good Goddess.
EDCS-22200904.summary: This is a dedication to the Bona Dea Augusta by Valeria Victorina, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-22200905.translation: To the Holy Fortune for the well-being of Rufius Festus, Marcellinus, and Proculus, three most distinguished men. Antigonus, freedman and agent, with his household.
EDCS-22200905.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna for the health of three prominent men, made by a freedman and agent named Antigonus and his household.

EDCS-22200907.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus built it. Emperor Caesar Augustus Vespasian, chief priest, holding tribunician power,Imperator for the 18th time, father of the country, consul for the 8th time, censor, restored it.
EDCS-22200907.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Emperor Vespasian, listing his numerous titles and offices, likely from the Flavian period (69-96 CE).

EDCS-22300169.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Quintus Ancharius Restitutus made this for his dearest and most dutiful son, Quintus Ancharius Pudentus, a soldier of the 3rd Praetorian cohort, an equestrian, who well deserved it. He lived 17 years, 7 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-22300169.summary: This is a funerary monument for Quintus Ancharius Pudentus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, erected by his father and detailing his age at death.

EDCS-22300175.translation: Titus Calpurnius Libicus, son of Gallus, having completed his public service. Luculla Psamathe, his wife.
EDCS-22300175.summary: This inscription commemorates Titus Calpurnius Libicus, who served in a public office, and mentions his wife Luculla Psamathe.

EDCS-22300176.translation: Merenna Vitellius, son of Vitellius, a local magistrate of the Surrini people, made this for himself and his deserving wife, Annia Ceticula.
EDCS-22300176.summary: This is a dedication made by Merenna Vitellius, a local magistrate of the Surrini, for himself and his wife, Annia Ceticula.

EDCS-22300179.translation: To Turranius Titianus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-22300179.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial for Turranius Titianus, noted for his distinguished status.

EDCS-22300180.translation: To Flavia Vitellia Seleuciana, a most distinguished woman...
EDCS-22300180.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to Flavia Vitellia Seleuciana, described as a most distinguished woman.

EDCS-22300185.translation: Gaius Aemilius Passer and Aemilia Pyrallis, freedwoman of Gaius, [erected this] for themselves and their family.
EDCS-22300185.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Aemilius Passer and Aemilia Pyrallis for themselves and their family.

EDCS-22300187.summary: This is the name of Lucius Fabricius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-22300190.translation: Julia Vitalis erected this for her deserving husband, Sextus Attius Marcellus, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-22300190.summary: A funerary dedication by Julia Vitalis to her husband Sextus Attius Marcellus.

EDCS-22300191.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gaius Marcius Primitivus and Marcia Oma.
EDCS-22300191.summary: A funerary dedication to Gaius Marcius Primitivus and Marcia Oma.

EDCS-22300193.translation: For the living Marcus Poblicius, freedman of the Marcorum women, and his mother.
EDCS-22300193.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Poblicius and his mother.

EDCS-22300194.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Primilla, dearest wife, most rare for her merits, [erected by] her husband Peculiaris. She lived 14 years. Farewell.
EDCS-22300194.summary: A funerary dedication by Peculiaris for his wife Primilla, who died at age 14.

EDCS-22300196.translation: Stellatina, daughter of Crispinus, wife of Sabinus. H[ic situs est/sita est].
EDCS-22300196.summary: A funerary dedication for Stellatina, wife of Sabinus.

EDCS-22300197.translation: Lucius Salvius Clonius for himself, his son Graphidus, and Faustas, his freedwoman.
EDCS-22300197.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Salvius Clonius for himself, his son, and his freedwoman.

EDCS-22300198.translation: For Gaius Tampius Diophantus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-22300198.summary: A dedication to Gaius Tampius Diophantus, freedman of Gaius.

EDCS-22300199.summary: The names Tampia Sabina, daughter of Gaius.

EDCS-22300200.translation: Lucius Tullius, son of Publius, of the Stellatina tribe, lived 30 years.
EDCS-22300200.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, parentage, tribal affiliation, and age at death of Lucius Tullius.

EDCS-22300202.translation: To Caius Turius, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, for his father.
EDCS-22300202.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, honoring the father of Caius Turius, indicating the dedicatee's name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22300205.translation: Lucius Lucceius Narcissus, a decurion in perpetual service in Rome.
EDCS-22300205.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Lucceius Narcissus and his role as a perpetual decurion in Rome.

EDCS-22300206.translation: A private road for the two Domitii.
EDCS-22300206.summary: This records the construction or designation of a private road belonging to two individuals named Domitius.

EDCS-22300207.translation: Servilius, 4 feet; Marcius Rufus, 2 feet; Lucius Silvius Rufus, master for the third time.
EDCS-22300207.summary: This inscription appears to record measurements of property or land boundaries, possibly related to a magistracy held by Lucius Silvius Rufus.

EDCS-22300208.translation: Marcus Avillius Diocles, freedman of Marcus; Marcus Avillius Apollonida, freedman of Marcus; Marcus Avillius Mena, freedman of Marcus; Avilia Metrogenea, freedwoman of Marcus; Avilia Cleopatra, freedwoman of a woman; Munatia Rufa, freedwoman of Marcus; Munatia Athenais, freedwoman of Marcus; Marcus Avillius Menander, freedman of Marcus; Zetus, freedman of Quintus Macilius and of the woman.
EDCS-22300208.summary: This is a complex funerary or commemorative inscription listing several freedmen and freedwomen associated with Marcus Avillius and Quintus Macilius.

EDCS-22300209.translation: Quintus Calfurnius, son of Caius, of the Arnensi tribe; Calfurnia Stratonica, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-22300209.summary: This inscription names Quintus Calfurnius, his father, tribal affiliation, and his freedwoman Calfurnia Stratonica.

EDCS-22300210.translation: Decimus Coelius Alexander, freedman of Decimus; Quintia Hilara, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-22300210.summary: This inscription records the names of Decimus Coelius Alexander, his patron, and Quintia Hilara, and her patron.

EDCS-22300211.translation: Marcus Durmius Crestus, freedman of Marcus; Flora, freedwoman of Loretana (a woman).
EDCS-22300211.summary: This inscription names Marcus Durmius Crestus, his patron, and Flora, the freedwoman of a woman named Loretana.

EDCS-22300212.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of an individual named Heros.

EDCS-22300215.translation: Lucius Volusenus Felix, freedman of Lucius, and Titus Annaienatius, attending officer, [dedicated this] to his patroness Annaiena Thais, freedwoman of Titus, his wife.
EDCS-22300215.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Volusenus Felix and Titus Annaienatius to their patroness and wife, likely a funerary or honorary monument.

EDCS-22300216.translation: Gaius Urinatius Dama, freedman of Gaius, and Petronia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-22300216.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Gaius Urinatius Dama and Petronia Rufa, likely a married couple or joint dedication, possibly funerary.

EDCS-22300221.translation: Sextus Atusius Priscus, son of Sextus, of the Fabia tribe, from Rome, a chief recruiting officer ('evocatus Augusti') of Tiberius, was the first of all to set up this altar, which Caligatus had vowed.
EDCS-22300221.summary: This inscription records the erection of an altar by Sextus Atusius Priscus, a high-ranking military official, likely dedicated to Tiberius.

EDCS-22300222.summary: This is a simple inscription of a single name, Marcus Cornelius Primus, likely a tombstone or a marker.

EDCS-22300223.summary: This inscription indicates that Marcus Cornelius Primus, along with others, was responsible for the creation of something, possibly a building or monument.

EDCS-22300225.summary: This is a short funerary epitaph recording the name and age at death of P. Carso.

EDCS-22300227.translation: [This was made] for Cocceia Lollia and for Ammia, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Nicephorus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-22300227.summary: This inscription records a dedication made for three individuals, Cocceia Lollia, Ammia, and Nicephorus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-22300229.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Turia Crispina, daughter of Lucius, made this for her well-deserving husband, Ianuarius Maior, son of Marcus, of the Poblicii family.
EDCS-22300229.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Turia Crispina dedicated a monument to her husband, Marcus Poblicius Ianuarius Maior, emphasizing his deserving nature.

EDCS-22300230.translation: While alive, Gaius Titius Metrophanes, freedman of Gaius, [dedicated] 12 feet in the field, 12 feet.
EDCS-22300230.summary: This inscription records a land division or boundary marking made by Gaius Titius Metrophanes during his lifetime.

EDCS-22300231.translation: Gaius Appius Metrophanes, freedman of Gaius, 12 feet in the field, 12 feet.
EDCS-22300231.summary: This inscription records a land division or boundary marking made by Gaius Appius Metrophanes, similar to EDCS-22300230.

EDCS-22300236.translation: Caius Tuccius Scaeva, son of Tiberius, of the Arnensis tribe, made this for himself and his family according to his means, for his father Tiberius, his mother Catia, his brother Rufus Tuccius, and his wife Ofillia Cala.
EDCS-22300236.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Caius Tuccius Scaeva to his family members, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-22300238.translation: Umpricius, son of Caius, a quaestor of Apollo, dedicates this.
EDCS-22300238.summary: This is a dedication of a statue or object to Apollo by Umpricius, a quaestor, probably from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-22300241.translation: For the Genius of Augustus and Tiberius Caesar, for Juno, Mystes, freedman, dedicated this.
EDCS-22300241.summary: This is a dedication to the Genii of Emperors Augustus and Tiberius, and to Juno, made by a freedman named Mystes, likely from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-22300243.translation: Falesce, who are in Sardinia, gave this gift to Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva. Lucius Latrius, son of Kaeso, and Caius Salvena, son of Volts, presided as magistrates. The college, which was accepted for the purpose of conducting business and sustaining life, for celebrating festivals, and which has often decorated these very things with their own skill and those of Vulcan, the chief emperors, so that they might gladly and willingly favor the petitioners.
EDCS-22300243.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a gift by the magistrates of a college to Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva, likely related to civic or religious festival funding in Roman Sardinia, probably from the 1st century BCE to 1st century CE.

EDCS-22300245.translation: In fulfillment of a vow, Julia Tigranis, daughter of King [I]ulia, Ammia, made this from the ground and dedicated it.
EDCS-22300245.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Mother of the Gods (Magna Mater) by Ammia, daughter of King [I]ulia Tigranis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22300247.summary: This is a simple dedication to the god Silvanus, likely a personal dedication from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22300252.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Britain, holding tribunician power for the 13th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 3rd time, Proconsul, son of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, conqueror of Arabia, Adiabene, Parthia, and Britain, the most brave, most fortunate, Pontifex Maximus, Father of the Fatherland.
EDCS-22300252.summary: This is a lengthy honorific inscription for Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), detailing his titles and parentage, likely dating to around 213 CE.

EDCS-22300263.translation: For Titus Nummius Augustalis, son of Titus, of the Horatia tribe, military tribune of the V Macedonica legion, of the equestrian order, prefect of the artisans. Caius Nummius Verus [dedicated this] for himself and for...
EDCS-22300263.summary: This is a dedication for Titus Nummius Augustalis, honoring his military and civic career, erected by Caius Nummius Verus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22300275.translation: To the departed spirits. Valerius Florentius served as a soldier for 6 years, lived 27 years, 3 months, and 5 days. A citizen of Cumae. To one who deserved well.
EDCS-22300275.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valerius Florentius, a soldier from Cumae, who served for 6 years and died at the age of 27, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22300284.translation: Lucius Afullinius Fronto, son of Lucius, and Caius Vibullenus Pollio, son of Caius, as duovirs with judicial power, [dedicated this] with their own money.
EDCS-22300284.summary: This records a public work or dedication funded by two duovirs (magistrates) named Lucius Afullinius Fronto and Caius Vibullenus Pollio, likely from a Roman municipality during the Imperial period.

EDCS-22300289.translation: Quintus Tullius Cincius Priscus, pontifex sacrarius of Juno Quiritis and patron of the municipality, by his will ordered this to be set up for Mammia Iusta, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-22300289.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Tullius Cincius Priscus for Mammia Iusta, with the dedicator also holding priesthood and patronal titles, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-22300290.translation: The two Publii Nigrinii Martialis, father and son Dexter, restored the Augustan road from the Cimina gate to the Annius road, and the Sacred Road from the chalcidicum to the grove of Juno Curritis, which had been consumed by age; they did this with 100,000 sesterces, out of gratitude for all the honors and immunities established for them by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22300290.summary: This inscription records the restoration of two roads by Publius Nigrinus Martialis and his son Dexter, funded by 100,000 sesterces and motivated by civic honors, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-22300291.translation: The citizens and residents [dedicated this to] Publius Oppius, as aedile/quaestor and duumvir.
EDCS-22300291.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication by the local community to Publius Oppius, who held a high magistracy, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300295.translation: To Quintus Tirrius, duumvir for the administration of justice.
EDCS-22300295.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to Quintus Tirrius, who served as a duumvir with judicial authority, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300296.translation: Quintus Turpilius, at his own expense.
EDCS-22300296.summary: This brief inscription records a construction or dedication by Quintus Turpilius, funded by himself, possibly for a public building or monument, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300297.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions Gaius Vibulenus, who held the office of duumvir, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300321.translation: Daphnus made this for Aurelius Lucius.
EDCS-22300321.summary: This short inscription records Daphnus as the maker or dedicator of something for Aurelius Lucius, possibly a tombstone or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300322.translation: Felix, slave of the municipality of Falerii.
EDCS-22300322.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Felix, a slave belonging to the municipality of Falerii, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300323.summary: This inscription records the name and status of Felix, a slave belonging to a municipality, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300324.translation: September, slave of the Faliscan Republic, made this.
EDCS-22300324.summary: This inscription records that September, a slave of the Faliscan Republic, was responsible for its creation, possibly a public work or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22300325.summary: A dedication made by Marcus Antonius Salvius, likely for a monument or object he created.

EDCS-22300326.summary: A dedication made by Caius Cremutius Secundinus, likely for a monument or object he created.

EDCS-22300327.summary: A dedication made by Caius Titienus Augustianus, likely for a monument or object he created.

EDCS-22300329.translation: Hirmio, son of Marcius, and Cepio Tertineus, son of Caius, praetors.
EDCS-22300329.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Hirmio and Cepio Tertineus, holding the office of praetor, possibly on a shared monument.

EDCS-22300330.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple epitaph or marker identifying a person named Cavis Tertineus.

EDCS-22300331.translation: Marcus Clipearios, son of Marcus, haruspex, Sorex, twice censor.
EDCS-22300331.summary: This inscription lists the titles and offices of Marcus Clipearios, identifying him as a haruspex and censor.

EDCS-22300332.translation: Caius Clippearios, son of Marcus, haruspex, Sorex, quaestor, VII times censor. Plenes, son of Quintus, lies here.
EDCS-22300332.summary: This inscription records Caius Clippearios as a haruspex and censor, and also serves as an epitaph for Plenes.

EDCS-22300333.translation: To Lucius Vecilius Volti, son, and Pola, daughter of Abelese, elected 1st; given to Caius Vecilius, son of Lucius, and Plenese; elected 1st. Not further, against their will. Lucius Caius Levieis, son of Lucius, and those who would have mourned them, do not place before.
EDCS-22300333.summary: This complex inscription records familial relations, electoral designations, and a prohibition regarding placement, possibly related to inheritance or burial rights.

EDCS-22300334.translation: Titus P. took care of digging the road for vehicles at Furculae.
EDCS-22300334.summary: This inscription records Titus P. undertaking the task of excavating a road for vehicles at a location called Furculae.

EDCS-22300335.translation: Here the ashes of Aquila, buried in a miserable urn, lie covered; and tragically died too soon by the fates, unhappy, just beginning the flower of youth, whom the seventeenth year finished, handsome, sensible, learned, pious. Received by a sorrowful father, who should have given him tombs and the space of feet in every direction.
EDCS-22300335.summary: This is a poignant epitaph for Aquila, a seventeen-year-old boy who died young, detailing his virtues and the grief of his father.

EDCS-22300336.translation: Gaius Aquinius Crescens and Furia Epictesis made this monument for themselves and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, and placed it with their own money.
EDCS-22300336.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Aquinius Crescens and Furia Epictesis for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-22300337.translation: To the departed spirits. Cornelia Secunda, mother, who lived 100 years and 2 months. Her sons and grandsons, the Furiani, made this.
EDCS-22300337.summary: A funerary dedication to Cornelia Secunda, made by her descendants.

EDCS-22300338.translation: Princeps, freedman of Creventius Anteronis, made this for himself and his family: his daughter Latina, who lived 10 years; Creventia Fausta, freedwoman; Creventius Anteron, patron; Numerius Munitor Panurgus, father; Gaius Creventius Euctatus, brother; Hilara, freedwoman of Septimia Numeri; and for Gaius Tintorius.
EDCS-22300338.summary: A funerary monument erected by Princeps, a freedman, for himself and numerous family members, including his young daughter.

EDCS-22300339.translation: Curtia Rufa, freedwoman of Publius, 12 feet in front, 12 feet in the ground.
EDCS-22300339.summary: An inscription likely marking the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Curtia Rufa.

EDCS-22300340.translation: Marcus Egnatius Plocamus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-22300340.summary: A simple funerary epitaph identifying Marcus Egnatius Plocamus.

EDCS-22300341.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Aermophila, who lived 2 years and 5 months.
EDCS-22300341.summary: A funerary dedication to Sextilia Aermophila, who died in childhood.

EDCS-22300342.translation: Flavia Philo, freedwoman of Flavia, and her son Gaius Flavius Thiasus, freedman of Flavia, ordered this to be made by their will for Flavia Helena.
EDCS-22300342.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Flavia Philo and her son Gaius Flavius Thiasus for Flavia Helena.

EDCS-22300343.translation: Lucis Furius Eutactus made this for his most beloved wife, Furia Repentina, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-22300343.summary: A funerary dedication made by Lucis Furius Eutactus for his wife, Furia Repentina.

EDCS-22300344.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Iulius Eutychus made this for his deserving wife, Calliope.
EDCS-22300344.summary: A funerary dedication made by Lucius Iulius Eutychus for his wife, Calliope.

EDCS-22300345.summary: An inscription indicating the resting place of Iulia Danaes' remains.

EDCS-22300347.translation: To Iunius Nimonius, who deserved well, who lived 8 months and 3 days.
EDCS-22300347.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Iunius Nimonius, recording his brief life.

EDCS-22300349.translation: To Numisius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Horatia tribe, son of Numisius; and to Caius' daughter Secunda, for herself and her family.
EDCS-22300349.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Numisius Rufus and Secunda, likely a married couple, set up by Secunda.

EDCS-22300350.translation: Sextus Papinius Liberalis, freedman of Sextus, lived 20 years.
EDCS-22300350.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Papinius Liberalis, recording his age at death.

EDCS-22300351.translation: Paullus, freedman of Philargurus; Prima, freedwoman; Elegans, freedman; Potitus, freedman.
EDCS-22300351.summary: This inscription lists four freedmen, likely members of the same household or group, without further context.

EDCS-22300353.translation: To Pontia Modesta, daughter of Aulus, a deserving patroness; Aulus Pontius Heraclida, freedman.
EDCS-22300353.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Aulus Pontius Heraclida, a freedman, for his patroness Pontia Modesta.

EDCS-22300354.translation: Praecilia Setoriana, daughter of Sextus, made [this] for her daughter Titia Praecilia, and for her granddaughter Titia Luria, and for her grandson Lucius Lurio Lurianus.
EDCS-22300354.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Praecilia Setoriana for her daughter, granddaughter, and grandson.

EDCS-22300357.translation: Lucius Stertinius Krisermus, freedman of Lucius; Stertinía Ecloge, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-22300357.summary: This inscription records two freedpersons, Lucius Stertinius Krisermus and Stertinia Ecloge, both freed by a Lucius Stertinius.

EDCS-22300358.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Gaius Stertinius Maximus.

EDCS-22300359.translation: Gaius Titius Zetus; Calventia Prima; Gaius Titius Clarus; Titia, freedwoman of Caius; Titia Amabilis, from her own resources.
EDCS-22300359.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members or associates, with Titia Amabilis contributing from her own funds.

EDCS-22300360.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Turpilina Irena, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22300364.translation: To themselves and to Lucius Volumnius.
EDCS-22300364.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely for a tomb, by and for members of the Volumnii family.

EDCS-22300371.translation: To Ceres Augusta, Mother of the Harvests. Lucius Bennius Primus, the male official, and Benna Primigenia, the female official, made this during the consulship of Germanicus Caesar (II) and Lucius Seius Tubero, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May for the sacrifice.
EDCS-22300371.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Ceres by local officials in 19 AD, detailing a sacrifice on a specific date.

EDCS-22300372.translation: Sacred to Ceres Frugifera. Lucius Veianius Cosmus, dutiful, dedicated this.
EDCS-22300372.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Ceres, likely on an altar or shrine, by Lucius Veianius Cosmus.

EDCS-22400115.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the second time, acclaimed imperator for the fourth time, consul for the second time, father of the country, their devoted unsurpassed and most valiant prince.
EDCS-22400115.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus by the people of Nepesinum, likely on a public building or monument.

EDCS-22400116.translation: To our Lord Gaius Valerius Maximianius, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, from the public treasury of Nepesinum.
EDCS-22400116.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Caesar Galerius Maximinus by the public administration of Nepesinum.

EDCS-22400117.translation: Flavius Eusebius made this memorial in his own property for himself and his family, who served commendably in the urban cohorts in Campania and completed his military service with honor while holding the highest office.
EDCS-22400117.summary: This is an epitaph for Flavius Eusebius, commemorating his military service and his construction of a memorial for his family.

EDCS-22400119.translation: Quintus Veturius Pexsus, son of Quintus, of the Pomptina tribe, lupercus Fabianus, from the college of Virtus, military tribune twice, prefect of the Fabri; Fidustia, daughter of Lucius; Raecia, daughter of Marcus, his sister; by the arbitration of Agrilia, daughter of Lucius, his maternal aunt, by testament, 20,000 sesterces.
EDCS-22400119.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the deceased Quintus Veturius Pexsus, his family members, and the distribution of 20,000 sesterces by testament, possibly for a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-22400120.translation: To Marcus Ulpius Thallus, freedman of Augustus, procurator. Flavia Inventa, his wife, and Ulpia Procula, his daughter, gave a feast to him, who deserved well of them, and to the Augustal decurions and the plebeian wives and children. A site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22400120.summary: This inscription records a dedication and a commemorative feast given by the wife and daughter of Marcus Ulpius Thallus, a procurator, to him and local officials and their families.

EDCS-22400122.translation: To Quintus Haterius O. Lucius Protacius Maximus... [The text is fragmented but seems to relate to the use of a portico, possibly leased or managed by Maximus, with several individuals from the Stellatina tribe involved.]
EDCS-22400122.summary: This fragmented inscription concerns the use and possibly the management or lease of a public portico in relation to Quintus Haterius O. and individuals from the Stellatina tribe.

EDCS-22400124.translation: To Lucius Aurelianus Victor, the youth of Nepesinum Dianenses, with contributions of money, a site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22400124.summary: This inscription records the granting of a site by the town council to Lucius Aurelianus Victor and the youth of Nepesinum Dianenses, funded by contributions.

EDCS-22400126.translation: To Herennia Iusta, daughter of Gaius. Marcus Apisius Sabinus, son of Marcus, of the Palatine tribe, duumvir and formerly a quaestor in Nepete, ordered this to be made by his will to his most sacred and most devoted wife, who deserved exceptionally well of him.
EDCS-22400126.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Nepete, commissioned by a husband for his wife, likely dating to the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-22400127.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Publius Luscius Sabinus Augustalis, freedman of Publius, of Nepete.
EDCS-22400127.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Nepete, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400128.translation: [...] Nestor, Augustalis of Nepete. Here he held games and on the occasion of the dedication of a statue of his patron, which he himself erected, and of his own shield, he again gave a banquet to the citizens of Nepete.
EDCS-22400128.summary: This inscription from Nepete records a series of public benefactions, including games, statue dedication, and a banquet, by a freedman named Nestor, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400134.summary: This is a personal name inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, from Nepete, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400136.translation: Lucius Oppius Trabeicus, son of Publius, son of Gnaeus, Flaccus.
EDCS-22400136.summary: This is a personal name inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary marker, from Nepete, likely dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-22400137.translation: Gaius Agisenna Pothus, freedman of Gaius, to Voluptas, daughter of Spurius, to Socconia; to Gaius Agisenna Eros Lanio Maior, patron.
EDCS-22400137.summary: This inscription from Nepete records a dedication from a freedman to his wife and also to his patron, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400138.translation: Who also to Aelius Ma Aelia Ch
EDCS-22400138.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely from Nepete, possibly recording a dedication or familial relationship, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-22400139.translation: Amaryllis to Fronton, freedman of Tertulla, my mother; to Acutus, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-22400139.summary: This inscription from Nepete records dedications from Amaryllis to her freedman Fronton and to her freedman Acutus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400141.translation: To Gnaeus Domitius Apollonius and Domitia Prusadis.
EDCS-22400141.summary: This inscription from Nepete is a dedication to two individuals, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400143.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavia Viatrix made this for Titus Flavius Nicephorus, her fellow freedman and deserving patron, after she made [it].
EDCS-22400143.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Nepete, made by a freedwoman for her fellow freedman and patron, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22400145.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Hilaro for his wife Julia Grisis, his son Lucius Terpe, and himself.
EDCS-22400145.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a wife and son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400146.translation: To Lucius Paconius Romanus, son of Publius, from his freedman Salutaris. His heirs made this for their deserving patron, who lived 68 years.
EDCS-22400146.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Lucius Paconius Romanus, commemorating his life and the actions of his freedman and heirs.

EDCS-22400147.translation: To Gaius Papirius Philologus, freedman of the CCC (collegium?), and to Fidustia Prepesa, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-22400147.summary: This is a dedication or funerary marker for two freedpersons, Gaius Papirius Philologus and Fidustia Prepesa.

EDCS-22400148.translation: To Saleia Arescusa, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-22400148.summary: A simple funerary inscription for Saleia Arescusa, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22400150.translation: Vitia Mycale, freedwoman of Gaius, chaste and pious, lived 22 years. Gaius Vetius Felix made this for his deserving freedwoman and himself.
EDCS-22400150.summary: This funerary epitaph commemorates Vitia Mycale, a freedwoman, and was erected by her patron.

EDCS-22400152.translation: Sebastianus of good memory rests here, in Christ, who lived one year, three months, and three days, deposited in peace, in the consulship of the most excellent man Stilicho.
EDCS-22400152.summary: This early Christian funerary inscription records the burial of a child named Sebastianus during the consulship of Stilicho.

EDCS-22400159.translation: Sacred to Diana. Marcus Valerius Restitutus.
EDCS-22400159.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana, made by Marcus Valerius Restitutus.

EDCS-22400160.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Youth. Gnaeus Domitius Ingenuus, freedman of Afrius, accensus.
EDCS-22400160.summary: This is a religious dedication to Jupiter Youth, made by Gnaeus Domitius Ingenuus, who held the office of accensus.

EDCS-22400161.translation: Servilia Felix, freedwoman of Lucius, the magistra, gives this gift to Minerva.
EDCS-22400161.summary: This inscription records a gift to the goddess Minerva made by Servilia Felix, a freedwoman who held a magisterial position.

EDCS-22400163.translation: Publius Vergilius, son of Publius, gave again to the same ones for whom he dedicated this temple.
EDCS-22400163.summary: This inscription records a repeated dedication by Publius Vergilius concerning a temple he had previously consecrated.

EDCS-22400168.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. The remains of the body of Marcus Tarquitius Crispus Fronto, a most distinguished young man, a capital triumvir.
EDCS-22400168.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Tarquitius Crispus Fronto, who held the office of capital triumvir.

EDCS-22400170.translation: The pontiffs, Marcus Valerius Restitutus, in the place of Caius Lollus Callidus.
EDCS-22400170.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or land transaction involving pontiffs and Marcus Valerius Restitutus, situated on land belonging to Caius Lollus Callidus.

EDCS-22400171.translation: To Marcus Anteius Restitutus, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe, prefect of the youth, aedile, augur, curator of public money, by the Augustales and the people, with contributions of bronze.
EDCS-22400171.summary: This is a dedication by the town council and people to Marcus Anteius Restitutus, listing his various public offices.

EDCS-22400174.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Prastina Fronto, scribe of the aedile, (and) the Diespitris (deities).
EDCS-22400174.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Prastina Fronto, who served as a scribe for an aedile, and possibly to the Diespitris deities.

EDCS-22400175.translation: Publius, son of Publius, twice quinquennial duovir, by the plebs.
EDCS-22400175.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the plebs to Publius, son of Publius, who served twice as quinquennial duovir.

EDCS-22400179.translation: Aelianus Rogator, for himself and his family.
EDCS-22400179.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription by Aelianus Rogator for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-22400180.translation: Aufidius, son of Lucius, grandson, lived 16 years, by his mother.
EDCS-22400180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aufidius, son of Lucius, who died at the age of 16, set up by his mother.

EDCS-22400181.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Aurelius Palatrcontius, son of Domnus, who lived 22 years, 2 months, and 12 days. His most devoted brother placed this.
EDCS-22400181.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aurelius Palatrcontius, who died at the age of 22, erected by his devoted brother.

EDCS-22400182.translation: Cassius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe. Aquila Cassius, son of Marcus, of the Papiria tribe.
EDCS-22400182.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment naming two individuals, likely Cassius and Aquila Cassius, both sons of Marcus and from the Papiria tribe, possibly as part of a larger dedication or family record.

EDCS-22400555.translation: To Titus Accarcelinus, son of Marcus, of the Popillia tribe, he held the office of ....
EDCS-22400555.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicating something to Titus Accarcelinus, son of Marcus, noting his tribal affiliation and an office he held.

EDCS-22400556.translation: Cavia Vecinea, wife of Macius Acarcelinus.
EDCS-22400556.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Cavia Vecinea and her husband, Macius Acarcelinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400557.translation: Marcius Acarcelinus and Cavia Vecinea offer this.
EDCS-22400557.summary: This inscription records an offering made by Marcius Acarcelinus and Cavia Vecinea, likely of Roman Imperial date.

EDCS-22400559.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription for Pola Marcia, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400560.translation: Vipia Zertenea offers this to Marcia, mother of Marcius Acarcelinus.
EDCS-22400560.summary: This inscription records an offering made by Vipia Zertenea to Marcia, mother of Marcius Acarcelinus, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400561.summary: This is a dedication by Cesula Tiperilia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400563.translation: Ca. Vecineus Voltius and Ca. Manius offer this.
EDCS-22400563.summary: This inscription records an offering made by two individuals, Ca. Vecineus Voltius and Ca. Manius, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400564.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Ca. Vecineus and Ca. Manius, possibly related to a dedication or funerary context from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400565.translation: Voltiius Vecineus, the greatest, offers this to the younger (son/relative) of Carconia.
EDCS-22400565.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Voltiius Vecineus to a younger relative of Carconia, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400567.summary: This is a dedication by Tepius Vetthius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400571.summary: This inscription names two individuals, Leiveliius Purtis and Voltius, possibly related to a dedication or funerary context from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22400572.translation: Marcus, son of Pleina, son of Marcus; Manomo, son of Caviacus; Veculia, daughter of Voltilia, daughter of Ventarci.
EDCS-22400572.summary: This inscription appears to record names, possibly related to a family or property.

EDCS-22400574.translation: To C. Mecius and A. Caesilia.
EDCS-22400574.summary: This is a dedication to C. Mecius and A. Caesilia.

EDCS-22400575.translation: To Voltius, son of Folcozeus, the sixth.
EDCS-22400575.summary: This is a dedication to Voltius, son of Folcozeus.

EDCS-22400578.translation: To Titus, son of Mareius Voltilis.
EDCS-22400578.summary: This is a dedication to Titus, son of Mareius Voltilis.

EDCS-22400579.translation: To Gaius, son of Folcuzeus; Gaius, son of Volc.
EDCS-22400579.summary: This inscription records the names Gaius, son of Folcuzeus, and Gaius, son of Volc.

EDCS-22400582.summary: This is a dedication to Reiclius and Caesilia.

EDCS-22400583.translation: To Iuna, daughter of Celio; Arutielia.
EDCS-22400583.summary: This inscription records the names Iuna, daughter of Celio, and Arutielia.

EDCS-22400584.translation: Celio, son of Cesi; Cavia, daughter of A.
EDCS-22400584.summary: This inscription records the names Celio, son of Cesi, and Cavia, daughter of A.

EDCS-22500174.translation: Quintus Statius, son of T. Iuventius; Quintus Statius, alive.
EDCS-22500174.summary: This inscription mentions Quintus Statius, son of T. Iuventius, and notes that Quintus Statius is alive.

EDCS-22500175.translation: Sacred to the Dis Manes. Titicus made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-22500175.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titicus to his wife.

EDCS-22500178.translation: To Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, aged eleven. Aulus Octavius Ligus, son of Aulus, and Marcus Genicilius Sabinus, son of Marcus, as duovirs.
EDCS-22500178.summary: This is a dedication to the young Lucius Caesar, son of Augustus, by two local magistrates (duovirs).

EDCS-22500179.translation: To Marcus Agrippa, son of Marcus, grandson of Augustus, aged seven. Aulus Octavius Ligus, son of Aulus, and Marcus Genicilius Sabinus, son of Marcus, as duovirs.
EDCS-22500179.summary: This is a dedication to the young Marcus Agrippa, grandson of Augustus, by two local magistrates (duovirs).

EDCS-22500180.translation: To Germanicus Caesar, son of Tiberius Augustus.
EDCS-22500180.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Germanicus Caesar, son of Tiberius.

EDCS-22500181.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Drusus Caesar.

EDCS-22500184.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, consul twice, proconsul, with tribunician power twice, father of the fatherland, restorer of public security and liberty, the devoted council of Forum Clodii dedicated this to his divine will and majesty, with Gaius Antistius Martial, Roman equestrian, and Gaius Vettius Felicissimus, Roman equestrian, and Quintus Aemilius Severianus overseeing.
EDCS-22500184.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Forum Clodii to Emperor Valerian, praising his titles and achievements, likely from the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-22500185.translation: To Gaius Clodius Vestalis, son of Gaius, proconsul. The Claudian townspeople from the prefecture of Claudia Urbana, to their patron.
EDCS-22500185.summary: This is an inscription by the citizens of Claudia Urbana honoring Gaius Clodius Vestalis, a former proconsul, as their patron.

EDCS-22500187.translation: To Aulus Octavius Ligus, son of Aulus, military tribune, duovir. The centurions of the VI Legion from Hispania.
EDCS-22500187.summary: This is a dedication by centurions of the VI Legion from Hispania to Aulus Octavius Ligus, who held military and civic offices.

EDCS-22500189.translation: [...] Ol[...] agelentin[...] Sassulanus [...] Sassulanus [...] Nundinesis [...] on which days...
EDCS-22500189.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription with names and possibly a reference to days, making its purpose unclear.

EDCS-22500191.translation: Pausilypon. To Hedone, freedwoman of Titus, wife of Mattia.
EDCS-22500191.summary: This is an epitaph for Hedone, a freedwoman, likely from the first or second century CE.

EDCS-22500192.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with a name ending in -inus and mentions Lucius Volcacius Tullus.

EDCS-22500195.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Avillius Rufinus.

EDCS-22500196.translation: Sacred to Augusta Mater, Acris, freedwoman of Opicernia Quinti, placed this.
EDCS-22500196.summary: This is a religious dedication made by Acris, a freedwoman, to Augusta Mater.

EDCS-22500205.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Fidus Damus.

EDCS-22500206.translation: Cnaeus Matrinius, son of Manius, Manius Matrinius, son of Manius, Manius Matrinius, son of Manius, by the will of Manius Matrinius, father, son of Cnaeus; Cosinia, mother, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-22500206.summary: This inscription records the parentage of several individuals, likely relating to a funerary monument or family record, possibly dating to the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-22500208.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, and to all the gods and goddesses, Laecani Modestus and Moderatus placed this.
EDCS-22500208.summary: This is a religious dedication made by Laecani Modestus and Moderatus to Jupiter and all the gods and goddesses.

EDCS-22500209.translation: Sacred to Silvanus Sanctus, Aulus Avilius Iustinus, son of Aulus, by vision, dedicated this.
EDCS-22500209.summary: This is a religious dedication made by Aulus Avilius Iustinus to Silvanus Sanctus, inspired by a vision.

EDCS-22500213.translation: To Gaius Anteius, son of Gaius, of the Tromentina tribe, his father; to Vomaniae, daughter of Lucius, his mother.
EDCS-22500213.summary: This funerary epitaph honors a father, Gaius Anteius, who held the office of IIIIvir, and his mother Vomaniae.

EDCS-22500214.translation: Octavius Trelius Caenius Atiti Cominius, Augustalis.
EDCS-22500214.summary: This inscription records the name of Octavius Trelius Caenius Atiti Cominius, who held the office of Augustalis.

EDCS-22500216.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Antonia Isias is buried in this location.

EDCS-22500217.translation: Caius Clodius Thalpius, with his own money, [gave?] 40 [units?] [the road?].
EDCS-22500217.summary: This inscription records a public donation by Caius Clodius Thalpius, likely for the construction or maintenance of a road.

EDCS-22500218.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to a person named Gaius Cu[---], whose other name is Sevi[---].

EDCS-22500219.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Fulvia Murcilla.

EDCS-22500220.translation: Philetus, freedman of Lucius Iulius Acratus, [son of] Iulius III, freedman of Lucius Lollius.
EDCS-22500220.summary: This inscription records a man named Philetus, freedman of Iulius Acratus, and mentions his patron and possibly another freedman.

EDCS-22500221.translation: Notiliatus lived 7 years, 1 month. Lucius Terminalis [dedicated this] to his son.
EDCS-22500221.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Notiliatus, who died at the age of 7 years and 1 month, dedicated by Lucius Terminalis.

EDCS-22500222.translation: Iunia Hedone, freedwoman of a woman. Quintus Fabius Staphylus, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-22500222.summary: This inscription names two individuals: Iunia Hedone and Quintus Fabius Staphylus, likely a funerary or commemorative text.

EDCS-22500223.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription naming Epagathus, a freedman of Maecilius.

EDCS-22500224.translation: Maecilia Agathene made [this] for her mother.
EDCS-22500224.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Maecilia Agathene for her mother.

EDCS-22500225.translation: [He/She] made [this] for Maximilla, his/her deserving wife.
EDCS-22500225.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to Maximilla, a deserving wife.

EDCS-22500227.translation: [---] from the will, 15,000 sesterces, under the supervision of Suavis, freedman of Quintus, and [---]ae, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-22500227.summary: This inscription details the distribution of 15,000 sesterces from a will, supervised by two freedmen.

EDCS-22500232.translation: [---] daughter Avilia. [---] lies here. [---] deposited on the 3rd day before the Ides of September.
EDCS-22500232.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the burial of Avilia, daughter [of---], on September 11th.

EDCS-22500247.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Centonius, prefect of the Graviscani and Tarquinians, a magistrate with judicial powers and a town councillor, made this for his deserving wife, Lodia Mituria.
EDCS-22500247.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by Centonius to his wife Lodia Mituria, and records his civic offices.

EDCS-22500255.translation: Sextus Petronius, son of Publius, lived 94 years in Tarquinia.
EDCS-22500255.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, age at death, and residence of Sextus Petronius.

EDCS-22500260.translation: Gaius Vetilius, son of Quintus, twice magistrate with judicial powers and quinquennial.
EDCS-22500260.summary: This inscription honours Gaius Vetilius, detailing his magistracies, likely as part of a public monument.

EDCS-22500272.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription records the name and age at death of Sextus Aelius.

EDCS-22500275.translation: Lucius Alina, son of Lucius, lived 67 years.
EDCS-22500275.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, and age at death of Lucius Alina.

EDCS-22500607.translation: Publius Alina, son of Publius, lived 60 years.
EDCS-22500607.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, and age at death of Publius Alina.

EDCS-22500609.translation: Allia, daughter of Caius, lived 55 years.
EDCS-22500609.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, and age at death of Allia.

EDCS-22500610.translation: Helena, freedwoman of Caius Allia, lived 50 years.
EDCS-22500610.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, patron, and age at death of Helena.

EDCS-22500611.summary: This funerary inscription records the name and age at death of Allia Helenia.

EDCS-22500612.translation: Sextus Ancarius, son of Sextus, lived 25 years.
EDCS-22500612.summary: This funerary inscription records the name, parentage, and age at death of Sextus Ancarius.

EDCS-22500613.translation: Ancilia, daughter of Lucius Bassa, lived 22 years.
EDCS-22500613.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Ancilia.

EDCS-22500614.translation: Publius Atilius, son of Naieus, lived 16 years.
EDCS-22500614.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Publius Atilius.

EDCS-22500615.translation: Sextus Atilius, son of Sextus, lived 18 years.
EDCS-22500615.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Sextus Atilius.

EDCS-22500616.translation: Caius Atinius, son of Titus, lived 65 years.
EDCS-22500616.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caius Atinius.

EDCS-22500617.translation: Avilia, daughter of Publius, lived 4 years.
EDCS-22500617.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Avilia.

EDCS-22500618.translation: Lucius Berienus Primus, freedman of a woman named Beriena, for himself and his own people, and for Beriena Prima, freedwoman of a woman named Beriena, his mother.
EDCS-22500618.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication by Lucius Berienus Primus for himself, his family, and his mother, Beriena Prima.

EDCS-22500619.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Caenius.

EDCS-22500620.translation: Caenius Rufus lived 50 years. What a crime!
EDCS-22500620.summary: This funerary epitaph records the lifespan of Caenius Rufus and expresses lamentation over his death.

EDCS-22500622.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely names Publius Caesennius, son of Sextus, possibly as a dedication or for identification.

EDCS-22500625.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Cava Dionisia.

EDCS-22500626.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Vols, freedman of Didae, placed this for his deserving wife Charis, who served him well.
EDCS-22500626.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman to his wife.

EDCS-22500627.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Lucius Cipius Celsus.

EDCS-22500628.translation: Lucius Cipius Celsus, son of Postumus, lived 26 years.
EDCS-22500628.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Lucius Cipius Celsus, son of Postumus.

EDCS-22500629.translation: To Gaius Clodius Maximus, his brothers Fortunatus and Rogatus, sons of Clodius, made this for him as he deserved well.
EDCS-22500629.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by brothers for their father, Gaius Clodius Maximus.

EDCS-22500630.translation: Felicla, freedwoman of Thyrsus, lived 7 years.
EDCS-22500630.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Felicla, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22500632.translation: Sextus Cominius, son of Lucius, lived [unknown number of] years.
EDCS-22500632.summary: This is an incomplete tombstone recording the lifespan of Sextus Cominius.

EDCS-22500634.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Gaius Coponius Bassus, possibly on a tombstone or public monument.

EDCS-22500635.translation: Publius Corona, son of Sextus, lived 9 years.
EDCS-22500635.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Publius Corona, son of Sextus.

EDCS-22500636.translation: Galla, daughter of Lucius, lived 40 years. Publius Annius made this at his own expense.
EDCS-22500636.summary: This is a funerary monument for Galla, daughter of Lucius, funded by Publius Annius.

EDCS-22500637.summary: This is a tombstone recording the lifespan of Gaius Qurtius.

EDCS-22500638.translation: Caius Curtius Storax, son of Caius, and Clara, freedwoman of Curtia, made this.
EDCS-22500638.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Caius Curtius Storax and Clara, dedicated to themselves or a relative.

EDCS-22500639.translation: Elegans, freedman of Hercennia, lived for 15 years.
EDCS-22500639.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Elegans, a freedman, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-22500640.translation: Ennia, freedwoman of Lucius, lived for 65 years.
EDCS-22500640.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Ennia, a freedwoman, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-22500641.translation: To the departed spirits. Tullius Heurtus for his deserving wife Fabia Themis, who lived 38 years.
EDCS-22500641.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Tullius Heurtus to his wife Fabia Themis.

EDCS-22500643.translation: Lucius Flavius Niger, freedman of Lucius, lived for 31 years.
EDCS-22500643.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Lucius Flavius Niger, a freedman, who died at the age of 31.

EDCS-22500644.translation: Publius G G lived for 78 years.
EDCS-22500644.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Publius G G, who died at the age of 78.

EDCS-22500645.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Craecinia, who died at the age of 36.

EDCS-22500646.translation: Caius Graecinius, son of Caius, lived for 26 years.
EDCS-22500646.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Caius Graecinius, son of Caius, who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-22500647.translation: Publius Graecinius, son of Caius, lived for 36 years.
EDCS-22500647.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Publius Graecinius, son of Caius, who died at the age of 36.

EDCS-22500650.summary: This epitaph records the life and death of Caius Hortensius, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-22500651.translation: Lucius Hortensius Grecula, son of Lucius, lived 48 years.
EDCS-22500651.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Hortensius Grecula, who died at the age of 48.

EDCS-22500653.translation: Hortensius Iuvencus erected this for his deserving mother, Hortensia Trophima, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-22500653.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Hortensius Iuvencus for his mother, Hortensia Trophima, who lived 50 years.

EDCS-22500654.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iegia Tyche, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-22500656.translation: Licinia, daughter of Numerius, lived 55 years.
EDCS-22500656.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinia, daughter of Numerius, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-22500657.translation: Licinia Hilara, freedwoman of Decimus, lived 65 years.
EDCS-22500657.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinia Hilara, a freedwoman of Decimus, who died at the age of 65.

EDCS-22500658.translation: Loteia Creste, freedwoman of Publius, lived 45 years.
EDCS-22500658.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Loteia Creste, a freedwoman of Publius, who died at the age of 45.

EDCS-22500659.translation: Lucius Lucanius Tityrus, freedman of Lucius, lived 55 years.
EDCS-22500659.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Lucanius Tityrus, a freedman of Lucius, who died at the age of 55.

EDCS-22500660.translation: Gaius Lucilius, son of Sextus, [lived] 23 years.
EDCS-22500660.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Lucilius, son of Sextus, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-22500661.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Valentinus erected this for his most sweet wife, Lucretia Aprulla, deserving, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-22500661.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Iulius Valentinus for his wife Lucretia Aprulla, who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-22500662.translation: Publius Marcius, son of Lucius, lived 11 years.
EDCS-22500662.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Marcius, son of Lucius, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-22500667.translation: Netia, daughter of Sextus, lived 95 years.
EDCS-22500667.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Netia, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-22500668.translation: Occia, daughter of Caius, lived 60 years, a good woman.
EDCS-22500668.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, age, and a commendation of the deceased, Occia, daughter of Caius.

EDCS-22500670.translation: Lucius Papinius, son of Lucius, lived 63 years.
EDCS-22500670.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Lucius Papinius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22500671.translation: Papinia, daughter of Sextus, lived 50 years.
EDCS-22500671.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Papinia, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-22500673.translation: Sextus Pedanius, son of Publius, lived 80 years.
EDCS-22500673.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Sextus Pedanius, son of Publius.

EDCS-22500674.translation: Petronia, daughter of Sextus, lived 72 years.
EDCS-22500674.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Petronia, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-22500676.translation: Gaius Pinius, son of Lucius, lived 27 years.
EDCS-22500676.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Gaius Pinius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22500677.translation: Plotia, daughter of Sextus, an excellent woman, lived 54 years.
EDCS-22500677.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, age, and a commendation of the deceased, Plotia, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-22500679.summary: This is a funerary epitaph providing the name of the deceased, Pompeia, daughter of Laro.

EDCS-22500681.translation: Rutilia, daughter of Titus, lived 11 years.
EDCS-22500681.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of the deceased, Rutilia, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-22500682.translation: To the Divine Shades. Antigonus the husband made this for his wife Sabina, who lived 13 years and 10 months.
EDCS-22500682.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his deceased wife, indicating her age at death.

EDCS-22500683.translation: To the Divine Shades. Hail Saturnina, who lived 2 years, 8 months, and 9 days. Antigonus and Sabina, parents, made this for their well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-22500683.summary: A funerary dedication from parents for their young daughter, stating her age at death.

EDCS-22500684.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Posila Salonia.

EDCS-22500685.translation: Lucius Satrenus, son of Titus, lived 20 years.
EDCS-22500685.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Lucius Satrenus, son of Titus.

EDCS-22500686.translation: Caius Saufeius, son of Lucius, lived 90 years.
EDCS-22500686.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Caius Saufeius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22500689.translation: Sergia Arbuscula, freedwoman of Caius, lived 50 years.
EDCS-22500689.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Sergia Arbuscula, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22500690.translation: Setria, freedwoman of Aulus, aged 54, an excellent daughter, aged 44.
EDCS-22500690.summary: A tombstone that confusingly records two ages for Setria, a freedwoman and daughter.

EDCS-22500692.translation: Publius Sosius Neicepor, freedman of Publius, by will, under the supervision of Marcus Durmius, son of Publius, of the Arnensian tribe.
EDCS-22500692.summary: A legal inscription detailing the execution of a will, likely related to a funerary monument or property.

EDCS-22500693.translation: Publius Sosius Sarmides, freedman of Publius, lived 90 years.
EDCS-22500693.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Publius Sosius Sarmides, a freedman.

EDCS-22500694.translation: Lucius Spurilius, son of Lucius, lived 65 years.
EDCS-22500694.summary: A tombstone recording the lifespan of Lucius Spurilius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22500697.translation: Statilia Quarta, freedwoman of Gaius, made this for herself and for Gaius Statilius Primus, freedman of the woman, and for Statilia Agaphomena, freedwoman of the woman, freedwoman. Primus lived 26 years, Agaphomena lived 14 years.
EDCS-22500697.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by a freedwoman for herself and her freedmen, also recording the ages of two of them.

EDCS-22500698.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription identifying a freedman named Gaius Tessius.

EDCS-22500699.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Tiburtia Posilla.

EDCS-22500700.translation: Lucius Titius, son of Publius, lived 55 years.
EDCS-22500700.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Lucius Titius.

EDCS-22500702.translation: Ossuary of Ossia, daughter of Galaes.
EDCS-22500702.summary: This is an inscription on an ossuary belonging to Ossia, daughter of Galaes.

EDCS-22500703.translation: Trebia, daughter of Publius, lived 73 years.
EDCS-22500703.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Trebia, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-22500704.translation: Trebia, daughter of Sextus, lived 13 years.
EDCS-22500704.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Trebia, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-22500706.translation: To the departed spirits of Sabina, daughter of Gaius, Tudennius.
EDCS-22500706.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sabina, daughter of Gaius Tudennius.

EDCS-22500707.translation: Lucius Cassius Restitutus made this for his most beloved, playful, and cherished Claudia Chrysis, who lived 4 years and 31 days.
EDCS-22500707.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Lucius Cassius Restitutus to his young daughter Claudia Chrysis, recording her name and lifespan.

EDCS-22500709.translation: Sulcania Myrtale made this for her deserving husband Lucius Manneius Abascantus and for herself.
EDCS-22500709.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by a wife for her deceased husband and herself.

EDCS-22500710.translation: To Minatia, to Gaius Minatius, son of Gaius, and Mulvia, daughter of Lucius. To Mulvia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-22500710.summary: This is an epitaph for Minatia, with repeated parentelic information for Gaius Minatius and Mulvia, likely family members.

EDCS-22500711.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Perennius Hermeros and Sergia Sedata, freedwoman of Sergius Laidis, made this for their son, and for themselves.
EDCS-22500711.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Publius Perennius Hermeros and Sergia Sedata for their son and themselves.

EDCS-22500712.translation: To the departed spirits. For Salasia Merula, daughter of Lucius, aged 13 years and 5 days. Forbidden sorrow and tears. Merula, her most unhappy mother, made this for herself and all her own while alive, for we die as we are born, and the end hangs from the beginning.
EDCS-22500712.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Salasia Merula, set up by her mother who laments her death and reflects on mortality.

EDCS-22500713.translation: To Gaius Vehilius, freedman of Gaius, and to you, Isochrysus, and to you.
EDCS-22500713.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Vehilius Isochrysus, a freedman, and to two other unnamed individuals.

EDCS-22500718.translation: Sergius Eutyches made this for Valeria Euposias, who deserved well.
EDCS-22500718.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sergius Eutyches for Valeria Euposias.

EDCS-22500722.translation: To Apollo and the holy Nymphs, Naevia Bassilla gave this gift.
EDCS-22500722.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a dedication by Naevia Bassilla to Apollo and the Nymphs.

EDCS-22500724.translation: Minucia Zosime gave this gift to the Nymphs.
EDCS-22500724.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a dedication by Minucia Zosime to the Nymphs.

EDCS-22500725.translation: Gaius F. H. gave this gift.
EDCS-22500725.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a dedication by Gaius F. H.

EDCS-22500732.translation: Belisarius acquired this in the tenth year.
