EDCS-22500732.summary: This inscription records an acquisition made by Belisarius in a specific year, possibly related to property or a building.

EDCS-22500733.translation: To the departed spirits. Hail, Columbula! Polyaenus, the actor, made this for his most sweet and incomparable wife, who lived 23 years, 11 months, and 3 days, and lived with me 8 years, 2 months, and 15 days, who deserved well.
EDCS-22500733.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Polyaenus for his wife Columbula, detailing her age and duration of their marriage.

EDCS-22600306.translation: To the spirits of Tullia Ampliata, who lived 41 years. Hyginus, fellow freedman, and Ampliatus, son, made this for her deserving spirit, and for themselves, their freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants.
EDCS-22600306.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman and son for Tullia Ampliata, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600307.translation: For Tullia Calemeria and Marcus Oppius Tullius Enipaeus, and for his sons, Lucius Tullius Enipaeus and Tullia Enipaea.
EDCS-22600307.summary: This is a funerary dedication for multiple individuals, likely members of the Tullia family, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600309.translation: Aulus Veturius Amphio, freedman of Aulus, lived 53 years.
EDCS-22600309.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, filiation, status, and age of Aulus Veturius Amphio, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600311.translation: Caius Virsius Rufus, son of Caius, lived 30 years.
EDCS-22600311.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, filiation, and age of Caius Virsius Rufus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600313.translation: To the spirits of Volumnia Maxima, dearest mother, who lived 22 years and 6 months. Quintus Veturius Maximus made this for her deserving spirit.
EDCS-22600313.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Veturius Maximus for his mother, Volumnia Maxima, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600314.translation: Petilia, daughter of Lucius, lived 58 years.
EDCS-22600314.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, filiation, and age of Petilia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600316.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of L. Tuni(us), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600317.translation: Publius Papirius, son of Publius, lived 10 years.
EDCS-22600317.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name, filiation, and age of Publius Papirius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600319.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Caius Oni Antus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600320.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the name and age of Spurinna Firmus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22600325.translation: Aulus Larcius Ampliatus and Marcus Ulpius Baradatus, his heirs, made this in memory of his 55 years of life in the XIII Gemina legion.
EDCS-22600325.summary: This is a funerary monument for a soldier of the XIII Gemina legion, erected by his heirs.

EDCS-22600338.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Iulius Sabinus and Artoria Euplia made this for their deserving husband, Marcus Helvius Maximus, aged 70, of the Ravenna fleet.
EDCS-22600338.summary: This is a funerary monument for Marcus Helvius Maximus, a member of the Ravenna fleet, erected by his wife and another individual.

EDCS-22600350.translation: Sextus Caecilius Sozon, an Augustalis, gave this as a gift to the state of Als.
EDCS-22600350.summary: This inscription records a gift made to the city of Als by Sextus Caecilius Sozon, an Augustalis, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22600359.translation: Caius Proculeius, priestess of the Great Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-22600359.summary: This is a dedication or identification of Caius Proculeius as a priestess of the Magna Mater cult.

EDCS-22600361.translation: Sacred to Diana. In memory of Terentia Prisca, daughter of Gnaeus, Caius Decimius Ammonianus Flavianus, and his daughter Ammonilla, his wife, made this for his mother.
EDCS-22600361.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Diana for Terentia Prisca, made by her husband and daughter, likely from the Flavian period.

EDCS-22600364.summary: This is a dedication or dedication to Caius Cassius Cassius, possibly a tombstone or votive inscription.

EDCS-22600365.translation: Cornelius Comus and Cornelia Trophime made this for their most devoted daughter, Cornelia Comina.
EDCS-22600365.summary: This is a funerary monument for Cornelia Comina, erected by her parents.

EDCS-22600366.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the name and age of Marcus Gellius Proculus.

EDCS-22600367.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Lucius Nerionius Phrastus and his fellow freedwoman Neronia Felicula.
EDCS-22600367.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Nerionius Phrastus and Neronia Felicula, likely erected by a relative or friend.

EDCS-22600369.translation: Lucius Statilius, son of Marcus, ordered this to be made for Marcus Statilius, son of Marcus, [---].
EDCS-22600369.summary: This inscription is a funerary commission, indicating that Lucius Statilius ordered a monument to be made for Marcus Statilius.

EDCS-22600371.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased Quintus Sulpicius Victor.

EDCS-22600372.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Sulpicius Astericus, who lived for 18 years, 8 months, and 26 days.
EDCS-22600372.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sulpicius Astericus, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-22600373.translation: Volteius Rufus, son of Volteius, and Philematio, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-22600373.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Volteius Rufus and Philematio, identifying their parentage and status.

EDCS-22600377.translation: Here rests in peace Vilifara, who lived more or less 40 years. She was buried on the 9th day before the Kalends of August, in the 16th year after the consulship of the most distinguished Basilius, in the 5th indiction. Sacred to the departed spirits.
EDCS-22600377.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vilifara, who died around age 40 and was buried on a specific date in the 6th century AD.

EDCS-22600378.translation: Here rests Melleus, a schoolmaster, friend of friends, who lived 30 years. He was buried in the tomb on the 5th day before the Ides of July. He rests.
EDCS-22600378.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Melleus, a schoolmaster who died at the age of 30.

EDCS-22600381.translation: Here rests in peace Apollonius, who lived more or less 65 years, and with his wife Dulcaia, 40 years. He died on the Kalends of May. Also, after his death, his granddaughter named Pascasia died and was placed on the 18th [day?] above her uncle, in peace. And she lived with her husband for nine months, leaving eternal sorrow to her father, mother, and grandmother.
EDCS-22600381.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Apollonius, his wife Dulcaia, their granddaughter Pascasia, and Apollonius's husband, detailing their lives and deaths.

EDCS-22600383.translation: Sacred to Apollo. Lucius Statilius Primus erected this altar at his own expense. Lucius Statilius Pollio renovated and restored it at his own expense, as it was weakened by age.
EDCS-22600383.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to Apollo, initially erected by Lucius Statilius Primus and later restored by Lucius Statilius Pollio.

EDCS-22600386.translation: To Hadrian Augustus, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22600386.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Hadrian, authorized by local town council (decurions).

EDCS-22600388.translation: To Cornelia Salonina, most holy Augusta, the colony Julia Castronovo is devoted to her divine power.
EDCS-22600388.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the colony of Castronovo to the Empress Cornelia Salonina.

EDCS-22600389.translation: To Publius Cornelius Licinius Valerianus, most noble Caesar, the colony Julia Castronovo is devoted to his divine power.
EDCS-22600389.summary: This inscription records the devotion of the colony of Castronovo to the Caesar Publius Cornelius Licinius Valerianus.

EDCS-22600390.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the fatherland, consul, the people of Castronovum, by decree of the decurions, have set this up.
EDCS-22600390.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Castronovum to Emperor Aurelian.

EDCS-22600391.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Maximian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, father of the fatherland, consul, holder of tribunician power, the people of Castronovum, by decree of the decurions, have set this up.
EDCS-22600391.summary: This is a dedication by the town council of Castronovum to Emperor Maximian, likely Maximian Hercules.

EDCS-22600392.translation: By Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Severus, most noble Caesar, of the people of Castronovum.
EDCS-22600392.summary: This inscription records the association of Emperor Severus with the community of Castronovum.

EDCS-22600396.translation: Felix and Iucundus, ward officials of the street of Augusta in the colony of Castronovum.
EDCS-22600396.summary: This is a record of two local officials in the colony of Castronovum.

EDCS-22600399.summary: This is a simple naming inscription, likely for a tombstone.

EDCS-22600400.summary: This is a possessive or genitive inscription, likely for a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-22600401.translation: Publius Cornelius Cornelianus made this. Publius Cornelius Cornelianus made this. Publius Cornelius Cornelianus made this. Publius Cornelius Cornelianus made this.
EDCS-22600401.summary: This repetitive inscription records the act of creation by Publius Cornelius Cornelianus, possibly for a building or monument.

EDCS-22600407.translation: The ward officials, the Genius of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus, father of the fatherland, of the ward of Asernia, Aulus Avillius Acanthus, dictator, and Marcus Junius Eutychus, have set this up at their own expense.
EDCS-22600407.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus by local officials of the Asernia ward.

EDCS-22600413.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontiff, holder of tribunician power.
EDCS-22600413.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus.

EDCS-22600419.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, chief pontiff, holder of tribunician power, Imperator ten times, consul four times, father of the fatherland, censor, designated successor; the Senate and People of Caere.
EDCS-22600419.summary: This is a dedication by the Senate and People of Caere to Emperor Vespasian.

EDCS-22600425.translation: To Sextus Campatius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-22600425.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sextus Campatius, son of Marcus, with part of the text missing.

EDCS-22600426.translation: Tiberius Claudius Bucolas, freedman of Augustus, chief taster of the dining room, procurator of the privileges, procurator of the waters, and garrison procurator, with his son Quintus Claudius Flavianus and his mother Sulpicia Cantabra, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22600426.summary: This inscription honors Tiberius Claudius Bucolas, a freedman of Augustus with several official titles, likely erected by local authorities.

EDCS-22600427.translation: [---] / [---] / [Gaius Cerenius, freedman of Caius, ---] / [Lucius Magilius ---] / [Titus Mercellus ---] / [Lucius Tuccius Celsus, viator of the consuls and praetors,] / [Lucius Arruntius Helenus, freedman of Lucius,] / [Gaius Titinius Adiutor, freedman of Caius,] / [Marcus Visinius Philadelphus, freedman of Marcus,] / [Quintus Pomponius Urbanus, freedman of Quintus,] / [Gaius Sulpicius Cthetus, freedman of Caius,] / [Gaius Calumeius Erastus, freedman of Caius,] / [Lucius Otius Communis, freedman of Lucius,] / [Gaius Oppius Secundus, freedman of Caius,] / [they presented the Ludi Latini and Graeci on the 9th, 8th, and 7th days before the Kalends of March, and they gave cakes and mulsum to the people, in the consulship of Marcus Asinius Agrippa Cosso and Cornelius Lentulus.]
EDCS-22600427.summary: This inscription records a series of public games and donations presented by various individuals, including freedmen and officials, during the consulship of Marcus Asinius Agrippa Cosso and Cornelius Lentulus.

EDCS-22600430.translation: Marcus Manlius Pollio, son of Caius, military tribune, chosen by the people, prefect of the artisans, perpetual censor.
EDCS-22600430.summary: This is an epitaph or record of honors for Marcus Manlius Pollio, detailing his military and civic career.

EDCS-22600432.summary: This inscription identifies Pu Bellicus as a scribe with quaestorian rank.

EDCS-22600439.translation: From the workshop of Aurelius Aquila.
EDCS-22600439.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product or artwork from the workshop of Aurelius Aquila.

EDCS-22600440.summary: This is a simple identification of Aulus Tarcna, son of Marcus.

EDCS-22600441.translation: Gaius Tarquinia, son of Marcus, from Stra.

EDCS-22600503.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Gaius Vesius, likely on a tombstone or other personal marker.

EDCS-22600504.summary: This inscription records the name, filiation, and cognomen of Lucius Veturius Polio, likely on a tombstone or other personal marker.

EDCS-22600505.translation: Lucius Villonius Nicephor, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-22600505.summary: This inscription records the name, manumission, and patron of Lucius Villonius Nicephor, probably on a funerary monument.

EDCS-22600507.translation: Laris Tursus, of the clan Larisal.
EDCS-22600507.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Laris Tursus, likely on a tombstone or other personal marker.

EDCS-22600509.translation: To Gaius Aburius Pamphilus, freedman of Caius, and to Hilara, freedwoman of Caius, and to Felicula, freedwoman of Caius, while alive, for themselves and their kin.
EDCS-22600509.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely to funerary arrangements, made by Gaius Aburius Pamphilus and other freedmen and freedwomen for themselves and their families.

EDCS-22600510.translation: Quinto Avidio Agathoni, while alive, Caius Sulpicius Auctus gave the shrine as it is, and 14 ossuary pots, and a place in his tomb for cremation for him and his descendants, and for Caius Terentius Onesimus, the shrine with 20 pots as it is, and for his descendants.
EDCS-22600510.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Caius Sulpicius Auctus, including a shrine and ossuary pots, for several individuals and their descendants.

EDCS-22600511.translation: Quintus Avidius Optatus, freedman of Quintus, 15 feet in front, 20 feet in the land.
EDCS-22600511.summary: This inscription records funerary plot dimensions for Quintus Avidius Optatus, a freedman, indicating the extent of his burial space.

EDCS-22600512.translation: Of Caius Sulpicius Auctus, 16 feet in front, 20 feet in the land.
EDCS-22600512.summary: This inscription records funerary plot dimensions for Caius Sulpicius Auctus, indicating the extent of his burial space.

EDCS-22600513.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Cilnia Briseis. Cilnia Procula [dedicated this].
EDCS-22600513.summary: A funerary dedication by Cilnia Procula to Cilnia Briseis.

EDCS-22600514.translation: Larcius Avillius Trophimus made this for Procula, freedwoman of Cilnia Panhemerus, most dutiful.
EDCS-22600514.summary: A funerary dedication by Larcius Avillius Trophimus for Procula, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22700162.translation: To Caius Numonius, son of Publius.
EDCS-22700162.summary: An inscription likely identifying property boundaries or ownership for Caius Numonius.

EDCS-22700163.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Plotia Musa made this for herself and her own slaves, Quartae who lived for 1 year and Silvanae who lived for 6 years; in this place are included, in every direction, 6 feet.
EDCS-22700163.summary: A tomb inscription by Plotia Musa for herself and her slaves, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-22700164.summary: A dedication, likely funerary, to Pompeia Physice.

EDCS-22700168.translation: Sacred to Asclepius the Saving August One, in honor of his father Pyrgensis. Lucius Volumnius Carus made this at his own expense. The site was allocated by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22700168.summary: A dedication to Asclepius by Lucius Volumnius Carus, authorized by the local senate.

EDCS-22700170.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Trebonius Melipthongus, father [dedicated this] to Euhelpistus.
EDCS-22700170.summary: A funerary dedication by Trebonius Melipthongus to Euhelpistus.

EDCS-22700171.translation: Publius Flavius Iucundus, Flavia Erotis, Flavia Rufa.
EDCS-22700171.summary: A list of names, possibly family members or individuals associated with a property, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-22700173.translation: 9 feet in front, 10 feet on the front, of the monument of the same Iulius [on the Appian Way] at the first milestone, land of the same mother, and a passage was granted to those exiting on the right.
EDCS-22700173.summary: A boundary description for a monument belonging to Iulius on the Appian Way, specifying dimensions and granting passage rights.

EDCS-22700179.translation: By decree of the decurions, under the supervision of Caius Cornelius Rufus, the four quaestors, the four officials.
EDCS-22700179.summary: An inscription detailing administrative supervision of a project, involving decurions and local officials.

EDCS-22700180.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Silius Rufus, a friend, granted this plot to Gaius Cornelius Furo, a quaestor and member of the college of four, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22700180.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the grant of a burial plot to a decurion by a friend.

EDCS-22700183.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Verginia Amanda, to her husband Marcus Baebius Abascantus, and Verginius Venustus, to his son, who deserved well.
EDCS-22700183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to a husband and son by a wife and mother.

EDCS-22700184.translation: Pomnia and her freedwoman colleague made this for her deserving companion. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-22700184.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly a tombstone, dedicated to a deserving individual.

EDCS-22700186.translation: Aurelius Zoticus made this in region IV near Raffo.
EDCS-22700186.summary: This is an inscription recording the construction of something by Aurelius Zoticus, possibly related to a building or land division.

EDCS-22700188.translation: Lucius Annius Largus gave this offering to the Household Gods.
EDCS-22700188.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a gift to the household deities by Lucius Annius Largus.

EDCS-22700193.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Trophimus, an imperial financial official, made this for his deserving wife, Pomponia Rufina.
EDCS-22700193.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by an imperial official to his wife.

EDCS-22700195.translation: Of our Lords Emperors, Aufidius Orfaeus, of our Lords Emperors, Aufidius Orfaeus.
EDCS-22700195.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or reference to the Emperors by Aufidius Orfaeus, possibly multiple times.

EDCS-22700196.translation: Aurelius Hylas, a supplier, made this, 28 units.
EDCS-22700196.summary: This inscription records a construction or provision by Aurelius Hylas, likely a contractor or supplier, with a quantity indicated.

EDCS-22700197.translation: Aurelius Hylas, a supplier, made this.
EDCS-22700197.summary: This inscription records a construction or provision by Aurelius Hylas, likely a contractor or supplier.

EDCS-22700198.summary: This inscription records a construction or provision by Aurelius Hylas, likely a contractor or supplier.

EDCS-22700199.translation: Aurelius Hylas, the provider, made this.
EDCS-22700199.summary: This inscription records that Aurelius Hylas, identified as a 'praebitor' (provider or supplier), erected this monument.

EDCS-22700200.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark belonging to Marcus Aurelius Saturninus.

EDCS-22700201.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark belonging to Marcus Aurelius Saturninus.

EDCS-22700202.summary: This inscription records that Aurelius Cornelianus erected this monument.

EDCS-22700203.summary: This inscription records that Aurelius Cornelianus erected this monument.

EDCS-22700212.translation: Antonius Astralis uses the private road of Annius Largus by permission.
EDCS-22700212.summary: This inscription records an agreement where Antonius Astralis is granted permission to use a private road belonging to Annius Largus.

EDCS-22700213.translation: To Aelia Felicissima, my wife with whom I lived for 4 years and 3 months. Aurelius Papas made this for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-22700213.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Aurelius Papas for his wife Aelia Felicissima, likely dated to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22700214.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Anthusa, servant of our Emperor.
EDCS-22700214.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Anthusa, a servant of the emperor, likely dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-22700216.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Cocceienia Pia made this for Cocceienia Octabia, her patroness, who deserved well.
EDCS-22700216.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Cocceienia Pia for her patroness Cocceienia Octabia, likely dated to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22700217.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Gaius Julius Justus, son of Julius, made this for his wife Cocceienia Helpidi, who deserved well, and for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-22700217.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Julius Justus for his wife Cocceienia Helpidi, also intended for himself and his descendants, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22700218.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Maelius Firmus made this for his most devoted wife, Iulia Procula, daughter of Gaius Iulius Proculus, who lived 24 years, 8 months, and 13 days.
EDCS-22700218.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Procula, daughter of Gaius Iulius Proculus, erected by her husband Lucius Maelius Firmus, likely dated to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22700219.translation: For Quintus Laelius Philargyrus, freedman of Quintus, under the direction of Laelia Prima, freedwoman of the Quintorum, his concubine.
EDCS-22700219.summary: An inscription recording a legal arrangement or disposition concerning Quintus Laelius Philargyrus and Laelia Prima, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-22700220.translation: Here I lie, I who cultivated these fertile lands with my husband, always beloved by my husband. My name was Myrsina, and I lived a life without fault. And I have completed the course that Fortune allotted. Farewell, my husband and dearest daughter, and always give due rites to my tomb.
EDCS-22700220.summary: A poetic epitaph by Myrsina, addressing her husband and daughter, reflecting on her life and requesting remembrance, likely dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700221.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Tertius and Victorinus made this for their most sweet mother Tyche, wife of Aurelius Felix, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-22700221.summary: A funerary epitaph for Tyche, wife of Aurelius Felix, erected by her sons Tertius and Victorinus, likely from the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-22700225.translation: Here lies in peace Rufinus, blameless, god-fearing, a connoisseur of holy laws and wisdom, aged 21 years, 8 months, and 10 hours.
EDCS-22700225.summary: A Greek funerary epitaph for Rufinus, a learned and pious individual, likely dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700228.translation: Aulus Romanius Bassus, freedman of Aulus, for himself and for Romanius Restitutus, son of Aulus, and for Onia, freedwoman of Mulier.
EDCS-22700228.summary: An epitaph possibly for multiple individuals including Aulus Romanius Bassus and Romanius Restitutus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700231.translation: To Catia Rufina, his wife, Quintus Catius Felix [erected this].
EDCS-22700231.summary: A funerary dedication by Quintus Catius Felix to his wife, Catia Rufina.

EDCS-22700232.translation: [Erected] to Flavia Chrysis and her descendants, and to [---]celadus and [---]ula.
EDCS-22700232.summary: A funerary dedication to Flavia Chrysis and others, whose relationships and the dedicator are lost.

EDCS-22700233.translation: To Cercenia Tryphera, his excellent mother, Titus Flavius Cercenianus [erected this].
EDCS-22700233.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Flavius Cercenianus to his mother, Cercenia Tryphera.

EDCS-22700235.translation: To his dearest friend, Pollia Coponia, his fellow soldier, and Secundus, his brother, and Tertius, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-22700235.summary: A funerary dedication by Pollia Coponia, Secundus, and Tertius to a deceased friend, likely a fellow soldier.

EDCS-22700236.translation: To Saenia Eutychia, his patroness, well-deserving, Gaius Saenius Eros [erected this] for himself and for Saenia Phasis, his wife, and for Saenia Eutychia, his freedwoman, and for all his freedmen and freedwomen and their descendants.
EDCS-22700236.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Saenius Eros for himself, his wife, his freedwoman, and his patroness, indicating a complex family and social structure.

EDCS-22700242.translation: Fabia Meline, freedwoman of Lucius. Lucius Fabius Pistus, freedman of Lucius. Marcus Clodius Menander, freedman of Marcus. Marcus Clodius Rufus, son of Spurius, from the Collina tribe.
EDCS-22700242.summary: A list of names, likely from a tomb, indicating familial and freedman relationships.

EDCS-22700243.translation: Lucius Longius Philomusus, freedman of Lucius. Lucius Longius Rufus, son of Lucius. Licinia Artimisia, freedwoman of Sextus.
EDCS-22700243.summary: A list of names, likely from a tomb, indicating familial and freedman relationships.

EDCS-22700757.summary: A brief inscription mentioning Marcus Tarquitius and his son, possibly on a shared monument.

EDCS-22700773.summary: A dedication or ownership mark related to Lucius Vettius Felicianus.

EDCS-22700783.translation: To the departed spirits of Artidia Procula, daughter of Titus, his most excellent and most holy mistress and most loving to him, and of Tiberius Claudius Callistus, Gaius Julius Heliodorus made this.
EDCS-22700783.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Julius Heliodorus to his mistress Artidia Procula and Tiberius Claudius Callistus.

EDCS-22700785.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Calestrius Flavianus to his father, Gaius Calestrius Nicetas.
EDCS-22700785.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a son to his father.

EDCS-22700786.translation: Diotima, freedwoman of Ce[---], to Carminia Liviana, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-22700786.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a woman named Diotima.

EDCS-22700787.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Claudianus to Claudian Veientensis.
EDCS-22700787.summary: This is a funerary dedication for an individual named Claudian Veientensis.

EDCS-22700800.translation: Gorgonis made this, in memory of her foster child, in the month of [---].
EDCS-22700800.summary: This is a dedication in Greek, likely a votive offering by Gorgonis to commemorate a foster child.

EDCS-22700808.translation: Lucius Julius Faventinus gave and set up this gift to Apollo.
EDCS-22700808.summary: This inscription records a double dedication of a gift to the god Apollo by Lucius Julius Faventinus.

EDCS-22700809.translation: Sacred to Augusta Diana. Aulus Servilius Clarus [dedicated this].
EDCS-22700809.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana Augusta by Aulus Servilius Clarus.

EDCS-22700810.translation: Marcus Ulpius Thaumastus, freedman of Augustus, from the office of public works and from the accounts of the patrimony, gave this gift to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-22700810.summary: This dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Ulpius Thaumastus, who held significant administrative positions.

EDCS-22700811.translation: Avonia T() and Trebatia [dedicated this] to the [Great Mother] of the gods.
EDCS-22700811.summary: This is a dedication to the Magna Mater by Avonia T() and Trebatia.

EDCS-22700813.translation: Gnaeus Cornelius Charito, Aulus Timinius Ianuarius, Marcus Quintilius Hermeros, and Abascantus, slave of Gnaeus Cornelius Charito, willingly gave this gift to Silvanus.
EDCS-22700813.summary: This is a collective dedication to the god Silvanus by several individuals, including a slave.

EDCS-22700814.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Quintus Lollius Dio [dedicated this] on behalf [of another].
EDCS-22700814.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus made by Quintus Lollius Dio, possibly on behalf of someone else.

EDCS-22700815.summary: This inscription is a dedicatory hymn, likely to a victorious figure.

EDCS-22700821.translation: The decurions and seviri dedicated [this] on the Kalends of October, when Anullinus and Fronton were consuls.
EDCS-22700821.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by local magistrates (decurions and seviri) during a specific consular year.

EDCS-22700832.translation: From the lands, sent by divine power.
EDCS-22700832.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely referring to the origin or divine inspiration of something related to land.

EDCS-22700833.translation: To the Divine Manes of Titus Atticus Strabo Romulus, a most distinguished boy.
EDCS-22700833.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young boy named Titus Atticus Strabo Romulus, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-22700835.translation: To the pious Fl(avius) Titus Flavius Tranquillinus Cornelius Sor and...
EDCS-22700835.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins as a dedication to a pious individual, likely a Flavius Titus Flavius Tranquillinus Cornelius Sor.

EDCS-22700836.translation: To Gaius Julius Montanus, son of Gaius, of the Claudian tribe, military tribune of the Fifth Legion Macedonica, prefect of armorers, member of the board of ten for judging lawsuits, and designated quaestor; Julia Nobilis, daughter of Gaius, dedicated [this] to her father.
EDCS-22700836.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a daughter to her father, who held various military and administrative positions.

EDCS-22700838.translation: Titus Flavius Protogenes, freedman of Augustus, who was in charge of correspondence, for himself and for his wife Tettaia Sabina, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-22700838.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Titus Flavius Protogenes, a freedman of the emperor, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-22700839.translation: To the Divine Manes of Quintus Lollius Valerianus, son of Quintus, scribe to the curule aediles. Quintus Lollius Bathyllus made [this] and for himself, his freedmen, freedwomen, and their descendants, 60 feet in front and 60 feet in the field.
EDCS-22700839.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Lollius Valerianus, made by Quintus Lollius Bathyllus, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-22700840.translation: To the Divine Manes of Lucius Vetulenius Caricus, III decurion of three decuries. Lucius Iulius Theseus, his heir, made [this] for his excellent and incomparable friend.
EDCS-22700840.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Vetulenius Caricus, a decurion, set up by his heir and friend.

EDCS-22700842.translation: [...], for Vetulenus Proculus, son of Lucius, of the Palatine tribe, a viator of the consuls. Decimia Gemina, his wife, placed [this] according to his will, on the condition that because he, most devoted to the Republic of Capena, had bequeathed the aforementioned sum of money in his will, on his birthday the decurions should receive two sportulae [baskets of food/gifts] according to the terms of the will; [the] place [was] given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-22700842.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vetulenus Proculus, funded by his wife according to his will, which stipulated a distribution of money to decurions on his birthday, with the burial plot granted by decree.

EDCS-22700843.translation: Titus Flavius Victorinus, decurion of the Emperor's elite guards, had this made by both his heirs.
EDCS-22700843.summary: This is a dedication from Titus Flavius Victorinus, a decurion, mentioning his heirs.

EDCS-22700844.translation: To the departed spirits. His heirs, Lucretius Gallius, a man of the highest distinction, and Gnori Silvanus and Charito, his freedmen, had this made by his will for their most excellent patron.
EDCS-22700844.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titus Gnori Atilianus, a primipilaris, made by his heirs and freedmen in accordance with his will.

EDCS-22700846.translation: To the memory of Lucius Veturius Pudentis, a veteran of the VI Praetorian cohort. Aulus Larcius Successus and Larcia Aucta, his son-in-law, [had this made].
EDCS-22700846.summary: This is a memorial inscription for Lucius Veturius Pudentis, a veteran, erected by his son-in-law and another individual.

EDCS-22700855.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with illegible names and letters.

EDCS-22700858.translation: [---]ius Nereus / [---]us Rufinus / [---]us Leo, the VI/[viri, of the ---] games, dedicated [this].
EDCS-22700858.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication by a group of six men (possibly VIviri) associated with games.

EDCS-22700883.translation: To Gaius Agernius Flavus, son of Gaius, a man who held the office of judge and the five-year census in Faleris, his wife Antonia Antulla, daughter of Gaius, made this.
EDCS-22700883.summary: This is a dedication made by Antonia Antulla for her husband, Gaius Agernius Flavus, who held judicial and census roles in Faleris.

EDCS-22700884.translation: The master, Gaius Claudius Euthicus, and the priests of the boar god had this made.
EDCS-22700884.summary: This inscription records a dedication for a boar god, made by its master, Gaius Claudius Euthicus, and priests.

EDCS-22700886.translation: To Flavia Ammia, priestess of Ceres, for the honor of her most distinguished ceremonial duties, by decree of the council.
EDCS-22700886.summary: This inscription honors Flavia Ammia, a priestess of Ceres, for her distinguished service, as decreed by the local council.

EDCS-22700887.translation: To Marcus Junius Rufus Pytho, patron of Aquis Sextis, a good and eloquent man.
EDCS-22700887.summary: This is an inscription honoring Marcus Junius Rufus Pytho, a patron of the colony of Aquis Sextis.

EDCS-22700892.translation: To the departed spirits. His most unhappy mother Aurelia Mariame and his most devoted wife Flavia Marcellina made this for Lucius Valerius Maximus, who lived with them for 20 years, 8 months, and 7 days, a man deserving of all honors in three cities.
EDCS-22700892.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Valerius Maximus, made by his mother and wife, noting his honors and lifespan.

EDCS-22700894.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Munia Celerina, daughter of Quintus, most beloved and devoted mother, a woman of admirable and holy character, Vennonius Pius and Celer, sons, [made this].
EDCS-22700894.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by sons to their mother.

EDCS-22700897.summary: A funerary or building inscription recording a maker.

EDCS-22700899.translation: Gaius Titius Eros, freedman of Gaius, physician.
EDCS-22700899.summary: An epitaph for a freedman physician.

EDCS-22700900.summary: A funerary epitaph for Titus, son of Publius.

EDCS-22700902.translation: Private road of Lucius Occius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-22700902.summary: An inscription marking a private road belonging to Lucius Occius.

EDCS-22700903.translation: Tertius and Pamphilus, freedmen, made a maceria from their own funds.
EDCS-22700903.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a maceria by two freedmen.

EDCS-22700904.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Allidia Sedata [dedicated this] to her most beloved son, Marcus Allidius Cominianus.
EDCS-22700904.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a mother to her son.

EDCS-22700905.translation: Gaius Annius Himerus, freedman of Gaius; Annia Cleopatra, freedwoman of Gaius; Gaius Annius Urilio, freedman of Gaius; Annia Modesta, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-22700905.summary: An epitaph listing four individuals, likely family members or freedmen associated with a household.

EDCS-22700906.translation: Larcia Pia made this for her most devoted mother, Antonia Musa.
EDCS-22700906.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a daughter to her mother.

EDCS-22700909.translation: Lucius Autronius Philargurus, freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-22700910.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Laecanius Saturninus of the Stellatina tribe, son of Lucius, to his most excellent wife, Caia Venusta, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-22700910.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius Laecanius Saturninus to his wife Caia Venusta.

EDCS-22700911.translation: Caius Canienus Olumpus, freedman of Caius, to Prima, freedwoman of Husilla, his wife, who deserved well of him, and to Caius Canienus Primo, son of Caius.
EDCS-22700911.summary: This epitaph honors Prima, wife of the freedman Caius Canienus Olumpus, and their son Caius Canienus Primo.

EDCS-22700912.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Faenia Vi made this for Celsus, her freedman.
EDCS-22700912.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Faenia Vi for her freedman Celsus.

EDCS-22700913.translation: To Caius Clodius Appaeus Pudentus, son of Caius, who lived 5 years, 8 months, and 8 days. Aurelius Flaccinus to his dearest son.
EDCS-22700913.summary: This epitaph records the death of a child, Caius Clodius Appaeus Pudentus, and is dedicated by his father Aurelius Flaccinus.

EDCS-22700914.translation: Claudia, daughter of Caius, on the third day before the Ides of Sextilis.
EDCS-22700914.summary: This is a funerary marker for Claudia, daughter of Caius, with a date of death.

EDCS-22700915.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Clodius, son of D(ecimus?).
EDCS-22700915.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for Marcus Clodius.

EDCS-22700917.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Coelia Volusiana, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-22700917.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Coelia Volusiana.

EDCS-22700918.translation: Cornelius took care to have this made.
EDCS-22700918.summary: This is a brief inscription indicating that Cornelius was responsible for commissioning the monument.

EDCS-22700920.translation: Caius Crepereius Menander, freedman of Caius, and Crepereia Lais, freedwoman of Caius, and Caius Crepereius Rufus, son of Spurius, and Creperius Bassus, son of Spurius, [made this] for their [---].
EDCS-22700920.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for several individuals, possibly family members, including freedmen and their patrons.

EDCS-22700922.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Niceta and Materna, his most holy and most loving wife, made this eternal house for Eccelsinus, her freedman.
EDCS-22700922.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Niceta and his wife Materna built a tomb for Niceta's freedman, Eccelsinus.

EDCS-22700923.translation: Publilia Quartilla, daughter of Caius, made this for herself and her husband, Lucius Epitanus Rufus, son of Lemonia.
EDCS-22700923.summary: This is a funerary monument made by a wife for herself and her husband, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE based on naming conventions.

EDCS-22700924.translation: To the Divine Spirits. His mother made this for her dearest son, Euplutio, who lived 4 years and 17 days.
EDCS-22700924.summary: This is a tombstone for a young child, Euplutio, set up by his mother.

EDCS-22700926.translation: The remains of the body of Favonia, freedwoman of Lucius Stabilis.
EDCS-22700926.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Favonia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-22700927.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Flavia Charis, sister and daughter, made by Cupitus, freedman of Augustus.
EDCS-22700927.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Flavia Charis, set up by her brother, Cupitus.

EDCS-22700928.translation: Quintus Fulvius Apollonius, freedman of Quintus, and Fulvia Trypera, freedwoman of Quintus, made this for their patron, their patron, and for Fulvius Phileros.
EDCS-22700928.summary: This monument was erected by two freedmen for their patron and another individual, Fulvius Phileros.

EDCS-22700929.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Rutilia Faustina made this for her husband, Gaius Julius Festus.
EDCS-22700929.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife for her husband, Gaius Julius Festus.

EDCS-22700930.translation: For Gaius Julius Pericenus, a true friend, who deserved well.
EDCS-22700930.summary: This is a dedication to a friend, Gaius Julius Pericenus.

EDCS-22700931.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Julia Esquilina, who lived 29 years and 10 months, made by her husband Julius Polemoninus and her brother Julius Sympheros; and for her sister Julia Clodiana, who lived 10 years.
EDCS-22700931.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a husband and brother to two sisters, Julia Esquilina and Julia Clodiana.

EDCS-22700932.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For his dearest wife, Julia Marcella, made by her husband Lucius Verginius Fortunatus for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-22700932.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, Julia Marcella.

EDCS-22700933.translation: To Marcus Junius Maximus, from Cronia.
EDCS-22700933.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to Marcus Junius Maximus by Cronia.

EDCS-22700934.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying a woman named Iunia Sanctula.

EDCS-22700936.translation: Lucius Marcius, son of Lucius, of the Tromentina tribe.
EDCS-22700936.summary: This inscription names Lucius Marcius and identifies his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-22700937.translation: Philetus made [this] for Marcus Marcius Eros, his patron.
EDCS-22700937.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Philetus to his patron Marcus Marcius Eros.

EDCS-22700938.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Marcius Sabinus [lived] 7 months. Cominia M... most dutiful.
EDCS-22700938.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Marcius Sabinus who died after only seven months, with a partial mention of Cominia.

EDCS-22700941.translation: To the Divine Shades. Victorina made [this] for her husband Onesion, an excellent veteran, and for herself.
EDCS-22700941.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Victorina for her husband Onesion, described as a veteran, and for herself.

EDCS-22700944.translation: Peldusius, son of Quintus, of the Clustumina tribe. Veturia Chelido, freedwoman of a woman. Veturia Laudica, freedwoman of a woman. Occius Philodamus. He made [it] for his own people.
EDCS-22700944.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, and indicates a person named Occius Philodamus made a dedication for his household.

EDCS-22700945.translation: Perelia Fortunata, wife of Publius Scanti, for herself and her descendants.
EDCS-22700945.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Perelia Fortunata for herself and her family.

EDCS-22700947.translation: Marina, mother, [made this] for her dearest son Gaius Pontius Niciatus, who lived 2 years, 3 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-22700947.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a mother, Marina, for her young son Gaius Pontius Niciatus.

EDCS-22700948.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. For Pontia Modesta, daughter of Aulus.
EDCS-22700948.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pontia Modesta, daughter of Aulus.

EDCS-22700949.translation: For Gaius Popillius Eros, freedman of a woman, by testament. Gaius Popillius Cinnamus, freedman of Gaius, [and] Tertia, freedwoman of Gaius. For Gaius Popillius Tertius, freedman of a woman.
EDCS-22700949.summary: This inscription details bequests from a testament, recording several freedmen and freedwomen of the Popillia family.

EDCS-22700951.summary: This inscription is a simple name and parentage, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-22700952.translation: Cnaeus Baebius Hymetus made this for himself and for them, his wife Helpidia, daughter of Baebius, and for Gnaeus Baebius, son of Titus, and for them and their descendants during his lifetime.
EDCS-22700952.summary: This is an funerary dedication made by Cnaeus Baebius Hymetus for himself, his wife, and others, during his lifetime.

EDCS-22700954.translation: For his wife Naida and for Lucius Curius, son of Lucius and the woman, and for their freedmen, freedwomen, and descendants.
EDCS-22700954.summary: This funerary dedication is for a wife and several freedpersons and their descendants.

EDCS-22700955.summary: This inscription records the name and relation of Statilius, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22700956.translation: Tarquitius Bassus, son of Titus, of the Stellatina tribe; Tarquitius, father, son of Titus, of the Stellatina tribe; Sitiana, mother, daughter of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe; Tarquitius, brother, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe.
EDCS-22700956.summary: This inscription records the names and relations of several family members, likely for a shared tomb or monument, belonging to the gens Tarquitia.

EDCS-22700958.translation: For themselves, Valerius and her husband Marcus Valerius.
EDCS-22700958.summary: This inscription is a dedication for a couple, Valerius and Marcus Valerius, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-22700959.translation: Lucius Valutius Rufus, son of Spurius, placed this according to the judgment of his freedman Suavis, by his will, with 20,000 sesterces.
EDCS-22700959.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by a freedman named Suavis, according to the will of Lucius Valutius Rufus.

EDCS-22700960.translation: To the spirits of Lucius Versenius Paulinus.
EDCS-22700960.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirit of Lucius Versenius Paulinus, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-22700961.translation: To the spirits of Lucius Vibius Varus, most devoted brother, for whom his freedman Vibia Irene and his freedman Anthion, his most excellent patron, made this according to his will, with 20,000 sesterces which he left them to manage.
EDCS-22700961.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by the freedpersons of Lucius Vibius Varus, following his will and using funds he bequeathed for its construction.

EDCS-22700963.translation: To the spirits of the bones of Zmaragdus.
EDCS-22700963.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the departed spirit and remains of Zmaragdus, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-22700976.translation: To Aurelia Ampliata, dearest wife, deserving well, who lived 23 years, 50 days, without complaint. Atheneus made (this).
EDCS-22700976.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Atheneus to his wife Aurelia Ampliata, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-22700990.translation: Burial on October 29th, during the consulship of Iulianus IIII and Sallustius. Lived 4 months.
EDCS-22700990.summary: This inscription records the burial of an individual named Vitalinis who lived for 4 months, dated by the consuls Iulianus and Sallustius.

EDCS-22700991.translation: Burial on December 5th, during the consulship of Iulianus and Salustius.
EDCS-22700991.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Maximini, dated by the consuls Iulianus and Salustius.

EDCS-22700992.translation: Burial on November 20th, during the consulship of Gratiano V and Theodosius.
EDCS-22700992.summary: This inscription records the burial of Sedatus, dated by the consuls Gratiano V and Theodosius.

EDCS-22700993.translation: Burial on August 27th, during the consulship of Merobaudes II and Saturninus.
EDCS-22700993.summary: This inscription records the burial of Rufinus, dated by the consuls Merobaudes II and Saturninus.

EDCS-22700994.translation: During the consulship of Anicius Olybrius and Probinus, burial on September 30th of Vervices, who lived 25 years, a maiden, deserving well, in peace. Parents made (this).
EDCS-22700994.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Vervices, a 25-year-old maiden, dedicated by her parents and dated by the consuls Olybrius and Probinus.

EDCS-22700995.translation: During the consulship of Anicius Olybrius and Probinus, burial of Iulia on December 8th, who lived 6 years and 22 days, deserving well, in peace. Parents made (this).
EDCS-22700995.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Iulia, who lived 6 years and 22 days, dedicated by her parents and dated by the consuls Olybrius and Probinus.

EDCS-22700996.translation: Burial of Leo, on August 8th, during the consulship of Theodosius Augustus and Romudorus.
EDCS-22700996.summary: This inscription records the burial of Leo, dated by the consuls Theodosius Augustus and Romudorus.

EDCS-22700997.translation: Burial on September 28th, who lived nine years, six months, six days, during the consulship of Theodosius and Romudorus.
EDCS-22700997.summary: This inscription records the burial of an unnamed individual who lived nine years, six months, and six days, dated by the consuls Theodosius and Romudorus.

EDCS-22700999.translation: ---, on the Kalends of August, during the consulship of Castinus, most distinguished man.
EDCS-22700999.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording an event or burial on the Kalends of August during the consulship of Castinus.

EDCS-22701024.translation: Burial of Oocis on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-22701024.summary: This inscription records the burial date of an individual named Oocis.

EDCS-22701027.translation: His sons, grieving, made this for Baebius Vindemialinus, who lived more or less 55 years, buried on the seventh day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-22701027.summary: This epitaph commemorates Baebius Vindemialinus, erected by his grieving sons and noting his age and burial date.

EDCS-22701032.translation: Here rests in peace Eucaria Vigilia, a praiseworthy woman who lived 24 years, buried on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February. The monument was placed by her most beloved husband Vigilius, a most distinguished man and consul of the most distinguished Maricanus.
EDCS-22701032.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial date of Eucaria Vigilia, placed by her husband Vigilius, and mentions a consul.

EDCS-22701033.translation: To Nunfe, our patroness in Christ.
EDCS-22701033.summary: This is a dedication to a Christian patroness named Nunfe.

EDCS-23000251.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Umbricius commissioned the work.

EDCS-23200921.translation: To our good lord, born for the republic, Flavius Claudius Julianus, and to our lords Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Valens.
EDCS-23200921.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Julianus, Valentinianus, and Valens.

EDCS-23200968.translation: The emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, emperor for the 2nd time, father of the country, undertook the restoration of the Via Aemilia, which had fallen into disrepair through age, with amplified works, for 188 miles from Rome, and for our lords the emperors Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Valens, most victorious Augusti, for 188 miles.
EDCS-23200968.summary: This inscription records Emperor Antoninus Pius's restoration of the Via Aemilia, and also mentions the emperors Valentinianus and Valens, suggesting a later date for the inscription or a dual purpose.

EDCS-23200969.translation: To the emperor Caesar, our lord Flavius Valens Pius Felix semper Augustus, to the emperor Caesar, our lord Flavius Gratianus Pius Felix semper Augustus, son of the deified Valentinianus Augustus, to the emperor Caesar, our lord Flavius Valentinianus Pius Felix semper Augustus, son of the deified Valentinianus Augustus, the city of Pisa [dedicated this for] 4 miles.
EDCS-23200969.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the city of Pisa to the emperors Valens, Gratian, and Valentinian II, likely concerning road maintenance.

EDCS-23200971.translation: For our lords Lucius Valerius Constantinus, Titus Gallius Valerius Maximianus Licinianus Licinius, always Augusti, 42 miles.
EDCS-23200971.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely for road maintenance, to the emperors Constantinus, Maximianus Licinianus, and Licinius.

EDCS-23200973.translation: To the liberator of the Roman world, restorer of freedom and the republic, preserver of soldiers and provincials, our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, the invincible, perpetual, always Augustus.
EDCS-23200973.summary: This is a panegyric inscription dedicated to Emperor Julian for his perceived role as a savior and restorer.

EDCS-23200975.translation: Titus Quinctius Flamininus, son of Titus, consul, to Pisa, 40 [units].
EDCS-23200975.summary: This is a milestone inscription recording the construction or repair of a road by Titus Quinctius Flamininus, a consul, near Pisa.

EDCS-23200976.translation: The most invincible lords, Constantius Maximus and Licinius, ever Augusti, and Crispus, Licinianus, and Claudius Constantinus, most blessed Caesar, ordered the fallen road, which was entirely ruined, to be made and restored, 182,000 [units].
EDCS-23200976.summary: This inscription records an order by the emperors Constantius, Licinius, Crispus, Licinianus, and Constantinus to repair a road, indicating a large-scale public works project.

EDCS-23800819.translation: Gaius Julius Euprepes made Ostia happy.
EDCS-23800819.summary: This dedication, possibly for a public building or amenity, was made by Gaius Julius Euprepes in Ostia.

EDCS-23800820.translation: Lucius Arlenus, freedman of Strabo, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23800820.summary: This is a dedication or dedication fragment, possibly for a religious or public monument, by Lucius Arlenus.

EDCS-23800824.translation: Quintus Caecilius Rufus, son of Quintus; Quintus Minucius Philargurus; Parhalia, freedwoman of Quintus Minucius; Marcus Cutius Clarus, Cutius is clear, sound, without blemish in life; whom he saw, he makes them similar in gesture and voice; no one is against him who wishes to imitate; why do you ask? the duty of a poor man is: in front 10 feet, in the field 25 feet. Cutia Aucta, bath attendant, freedwoman of Marcus. Caius Julius Amiantus, salinator, freedman of Philotimus.
EDCS-23800824.summary: This complex inscription appears to be a property boundary marker or dedication, detailing measurements and listing several individuals, some identified by occupation and status.

EDCS-23800825.translation: Eureto, most sweet, requested on the first day.
EDCS-23800825.summary: This inscription is likely a short dedication or remembrance, possibly for a person or a pet, dated to the first day of a month.

EDCS-24400735.translation: To Gaius Petronius Aper, from Epidiana.
EDCS-24400735.summary: This is a dedication or a funerary inscription, likely from Epidiana to Gaius Petronius Aper.

EDCS-24400738.summary: This is a possessive inscription, possibly marking property or a tomb belonging to Quintus Granius Priscus.

EDCS-24400742.summary: This is a possessive inscription, possibly marking property or a tomb belonging to Lucius Epidius Theodorus.

EDCS-24400743.summary: This is a possessive inscription, possibly marking property or a tomb belonging to Lucius Epidius Theodorus.

EDCS-24400744.translation: Of Epiborus, son of Gaius Marcius.
EDCS-24400744.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Epiborus, son of Gaius Marcius.

EDCS-24400747.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Quintus Clodius Ambrosus.

EDCS-24400748.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Iuvenalis, son of Aqua.

EDCS-24400750.translation: Of Lucius Barbus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-24400750.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Lucius Barbus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-24400751.translation: Of Marcus, son of Gaius Marcius.
EDCS-24400751.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Marcus, son of Gaius Marcius.

EDCS-24601016.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming the deceased Gaius Marius Celer.

EDCS-24601020.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Quintus Puplieius Marcus Veturius.

EDCS-24601023.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription by Quintus Tossius Priscus.

EDCS-24601024.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Lucius Vi, son of Frilius.

EDCS-24601027.translation: To Hilarus, of Lucius Avilius Sura.
EDCS-24601027.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb to Hilarus, possibly belonging to Lucius Avilius Sura.

EDCS-24601029.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Nonius Florus, likely on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-24601032.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Optatus to the goddess Salus (Health).

EDCS-24601034.translation: To Callisto, a happy and fortunate new year.
EDCS-24601034.summary: This is a New Year's greeting or dedication to Callisto, possibly for a festival or commemoration.

EDCS-24700001.translation: Mamilius son of Marcus, Caius Mamilius Limetanus, Caius Mamilius Atelus, Caius Macius Copo, Lucius Laterius Balbus, Lucius Laterius Corvinus, Lucius Laterius Corvus, Quintus Laterius Rabilinus, Laterius Hispanus, Publius Laterius Luscus, Marcus Laterius, son of Quintus, Laterius Paperianus, Laterius Balbus, son of Minucius Cai, Marcus Laterius Mulus, Hileria Midia, Patolcia, Pineia.
EDCS-24700001.summary: This inscription lists a large number of names, likely associated with a family, collegium, or official body, possibly related to funerary or commemorative purposes.

EDCS-24700002.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Apollonius, who is identified by the cognomen 'Licinianus'.

EDCS-24700053.translation: Teopropus Fabi saw [this] before the seventh day before the Kalends of October, [in the presence] of Lucius Domitius Appius Claudius.
EDCS-24700053.summary: This inscription records an observation or event witnessed by Teopropus Fabi on a specific date, in the presence of named individuals.

EDCS-24700113.translation: Maraeus Popius, son of Statius, gives this gift deservedly.
EDCS-24700113.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Maraeus Popius, son of Statius, as a deserved recognition.

EDCS-24700129.translation: Sextus Salvius, son of Aulus, lived 28 years, four times a duovir.
EDCS-24700129.summary: This funerary inscription records the age at death and public offices held by Sextus Salvius, son of Aulus.

EDCS-24700131.translation: Lucius Caecina, son of Lucius, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor, proconsul, paved the roads with his own money.
EDCS-24700131.summary: This inscription details the career of Lucius Caecina, son of Lucius, and records his public works project of paving roads at his own expense.

EDCS-24700141.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter (Iuppiter) in his aspect as Liberator (the deliverer).

EDCS-24700144.translation: Decimus Sortes Dionisius, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-24700144.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman named Dionisius, identified by his patron Lucius Sortes.

EDCS-24700145.translation: Aulus Sortes, son of Decimus, from the tribe Fastia, from Ceartia.
EDCS-24700145.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Aulus Sortes, son of Decimus.
